    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Enterprise
GP Holdings L.P. is a publicly traded Delaware limited partnership, the limited
partnership interests (the &#8220;Units&#8221;) of which are listed on the NYSE under the
ticker symbol &#8220;EPE.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Our business consists of the ownership of
general and limited partner interests of publicly traded partnerships engaged in
the midstream energy industry and related businesses.&#160;&#160;Our goal is to
increase cash distributions to unitholders.&#160;&#160;Our principal executive
offices are located at 1100 Louisiana Street, 10<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">th</font>
Floor, Houston, Texas 77002, our telephone number is (713) 381-6500 and our
website address is <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.enterprisegp.com</font>.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Business
Strategy</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
primary objective of the Parent Company is to increase cash available for
distributions to its unitholders. There has been significant demand for the
development of new midstream energy infrastructure to meet the needs of
producers and consumers of natural gas, natural gas liquids (&#8220;NGLs&#8221;), crude oil
and refined products.&#160;&#160;In addition, there have been several
transactions involving the sale of general partner interests in publicly traded
partnerships.&#160;&#160;Finally, in recent years, major independent oil and gas
and other energy companies have divested significant midstream
assets.&#160;&#160;These trends are generally expected to
continue.&#160;&#160;The Parent Company seeks to capitalize on these trends
by:</font></div>

    <div>

      successful execution of its business
strategy;</font></div>
            </td>

      opportunities to acquire general partner interests and, if applicable,

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>For information regarding our results

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NGL
Pipelines &amp; Services</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our NGL
Pipelines &amp; Services business segment includes our (i) natural gas
processing business and related NGL marketing activities; (ii) NGL pipelines
aggregating approximately 16,300 miles; (iii) NGL and related product storage
and terminal facilities with 163.4 MMBbls of working storage capacity and (iv)
NGL fractionation facilities.&#160;&#160;This segment also includes our import
and export terminal operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NGL
products (ethane, propane, normal butane, isobutane and natural gasoline) are
used as raw materials by the petrochemical industry, as feedstocks by refiners
in the production of motor gasoline and by industrial and residential users as
fuel.&#160;&#160;Ethane is primarily used in the petrochemical industry as a
feedstock for ethylene production, one of the basic building blocks for a wide
range of plastics and other chemical products.&#160;&#160;Propane is used both
as a petrochemical feedstock in the production of ethylene and propylene and as
a heating, engine and industrial fuel.&#160;&#160;Normal butane is used as a
petrochemical feedstock in the production of ethylene and butadiene (a key
ingredient of synthetic rubber), as a blendstock for motor gasoline and to
produce isobutane through isomerization.&#160;&#160;Isobutane is fractionated
from mixed butane (a mixed stream of normal butane and isobutane) or produced
from normal butane through the process of isomerization, and is used in refinery
alkylation to enhance the octane content of motor gasoline, in the production of
isooctane and other octane additives and in the production of propylene
oxide.&#160;&#160;Natural gasoline, a mixture of pentanes and heavier
hydrocarbons, is primarily used as a blendstock for motor gasoline or as a
petrochemical feedstock.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Natural
gas processing and related NGL marketing activities</font>.&#160;&#160;At the
core of our natural gas processing business are 25 processing plants located
across Colorado, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico, Texas and
Wyoming.&#160;&#160;Natural gas produced at the wellhead (especially in
association with crude oil) contains varying amounts of NGLs.&#160;&#160;This
rich natural gas in its raw form is usually not acceptable for transportation in
the nation&#8217;s natural gas pipeline systems or for commercial use as a
fuel.&#160;&#160;Natural gas processing plants remove NGLs from the natural gas
stream, which enables the natural gas to meet pipeline and commercial quality
specifications.&#160;&#160;In addition, on an energy equivalent basis, NGLs
generally have a greater economic value as a raw material for petrochemical and
motor gasoline production than their value as components of a natural gas
stream.&#160;&#160;After extraction by the processing plants, we typically
transport the mixed NGLs to a centralized facility for fractionation into purity
NGL products such as ethane, propane, normal butane, isobutane and natural
gasoline.&#160;&#160;The purity NGL products can then be used in our NGL
marketing activities to meet contractual requirements or sold on spot and
forward markets.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">When
operating and extraction costs of natural gas processing plants are higher than
the incremental value of the NGL products that would be extracted, the recovery
levels of certain NGL</font></div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">5</font></div>
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">products,
principally ethane, may be reduced or eliminated.&#160;&#160;This leads to a
reduction in NGL volumes available for transportation and
fractionation.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In our natural gas processing business,
we enter into percent-of-liquids contracts, percent-of-proceeds contracts,
fee-based contracts, hybrid contracts (a combination of percent-of-liquids and
fee-based contract terms), keepwhole contracts and margin-band
contracts.&#160;&#160;Under keepwhole and margin-band contracts, we take
ownership of mixed NGLs extracted from the producer&#8217;s natural gas stream and
recognize revenue when the extracted NGLs are delivered and sold to customers on
NGL marketing sales contracts.&#160;&#160;In the same way, revenue is recognized
under our percent-of-liquids contracts except that the volume of NGLs we extract
and sell is less than the total amount of NGLs extracted from the producers&#8217;
natural gas.&#160;&#160;Under a percent-of-liquids contract, the producer
retains title to a percentage of the mixed NGLs we extract and generally bears
the cost of natural gas associated with shrinkage and plant
fuel.&#160;&#160;Under a percent-of-proceeds contract, we share in the proceeds
generated from the sale of the mixed NGLs we extract on the producer&#8217;s
behalf.&#160;&#160;If a cash fee for natural gas processing services is
stipulated by the contract, we record revenue when the natural gas has been
processed and delivered to the producer.&#160;&#160;The NGL volumes we earn and
take title to in connection with our processing activities are referred to as
our equity NGL production.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
general, our percent-of-liquids, hybrid and keepwhole contracts give us the
right (but not the obligation) to process natural gas for a producer; thus, we
are protected from processing natural gas at an economic loss during times when
the sum of our costs exceeds the value of the mixed NGLs in which we would take
ownership.&#160;&#160;Generally, our natural gas processing agreements have
terms ranging from month-to-month to life of the producing
lease.&#160;&#160;Intermediate terms of one to ten years are also
common.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To the
extent that we are obligated under our keepwhole and margin-band gas processing
contracts to compensate the producer for the natural gas equivalent energy value
of mixed NGLs we extract from the natural gas stream, we are exposed to various
risks, primarily commodity price fluctuations.&#160;&#160;However, our margin
band contracts typically contain terms which limit our exposure to such
risks.&#160;&#160;The prices of natural gas and NGLs are subject to fluctuations
in response to changes in supply and demand and a variety of additional factors
that are beyond our control.&#160;&#160;Periodically, we attempt to mitigate
these risks through the use of commodity derivative instruments.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our NGL marketing activities generate
revenues from the sale and delivery of NGLs obtained through our processing
activities and spot and contract purchases from third parties.&#160;&#160;These
sales contracts may also include forward product sales contracts.&#160;&#160;In
general, sales prices referenced in the contracts utilized within our NGL
marketing activities are market-based and may include pricing differentials for
such factors as delivery location.&#160;&#160;The majority of our consolidated
revenues and costs and expenses are generated from marketing activities,
including those associated with NGLs.&#160;&#160;Changes in our consolidated
revenues and operating costs and expenses period-to-period are explained in part
by changes in market prices for the products we sell.&#160;&#160;The results of
operations from our NGL marketing activities are generally dependent upon the
volume of products sold and the sales prices charged to
customers.&#160;&#160;&#160;The volume of products sold may fluctuate from
period-to-period depending on market conditions, volumes produced and
opportunities, which may be influenced by current and forward market prices for
purity NGL products and our hedging activities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our NGL
marketing activities include production and purchases of inventories of mixed
NGLs and purity NGL products.&#160;&#160;As a result of exceptional energy
market conditions during 2009, we significantly increased our physical NGL
inventory purchases and related forward physical sales
commitments.&#160;&#160;In general, the significant increase in volumes
dedicated to forward physical sales contracts improves the overall utilization
and profitability of our fee-based assets.&#160;&#160;Our inventories of ethane,
propane and normal butane are typically at higher levels from March through
November since these products are normally in higher demand and at higher price
levels during the winter months.&#160;&#160;Isobutane and natural gasoline
inventories are generally stable and less cyclical throughout the
year.&#160;&#160;Generally, our inventory cycle begins in late-February to
mid-March (the seasonal low point), building through September, and remaining
level until early December before being drawn down through winter until the
seasonal low is reached again.</font></div>
    <div><br></div>

          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For
additional information regarding our inventories and consolidated segment
revenues and expenses, see Notes 7 and 14, respectively, of the Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements included under Item 8 of this annual
report.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">NGL
pipelines, storage facilities and import/export terminals</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.</font>&#160;&#160;Our NGL
pipelines transport mixed NGLs and other hydrocarbons from natural gas
processing facilities, refineries and import terminals to fractionation plants
and storage facilities; distribute and collect purity NGL products to and from
fractionation plants, petrochemical plants and refineries; and deliver propane
to customers along the Dixie Pipeline and certain sections of the Mid-America
Pipeline System.&#160;&#160;Revenues from our NGL pipeline transportation
agreements are generally based upon a fixed fee per gallon of liquids
transported multiplied by the volume delivered.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the
results of operations for this business are generally dependent upon the volume
of product transported and the level of fees charged to customers (including
those charged internally, which are eliminated in the preparation of our
consolidated financial statements).&#160;&#160;The transportation fees charged
under these arrangements are either contractual or regulated by governmental
agencies, including the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
(&#8220;FERC&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Excluding inventories held in connection with our marketing
activities, we typically do not take title to the products transported by our
NGL pipelines; rather, the shipper retains title and the associated commodity
price risk.&#160;&#160;However, we occasionally act as shipper for certain
volumes being transported.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our NGL and related product storage
facilities are integral parts of our operations used for the storage of products
owned by us and our customers.&#160;&#160;In general, our underground salt dome
storage caverns (or wells) are used to store mixed NGLs, purity NGL products and
petrochemical products.&#160;&#160;We collect storage revenues under our NGL and
related product storage contracts based on the number of days a customer has
volumes in storage multiplied by a storage rate (as defined in each
contract).&#160;&#160;With respect to capacity reservation agreements, we
collect a fee for reserving storage capacity for certain customers in our
underground storage wells.&#160;&#160;The customers pay reservation fees based
on the level of storage capacity reserved rather than the actual volumes
stored.&#160;&#160;When a customer exceeds its reserved capacity, we charge
those customers an excess storage fee.&#160;&#160;In addition, we charge other
customers throughput fees based on volumes delivered into and subsequently
withdrawn from storage.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the profitability of our storage
operations is dependent upon the level of storage capacity reserved by
customers, the volume of product delivered into and withdrawn from the
underground caverns and the level of throughput fees charged.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
operate NGL import and export facilities located on the Houston Ship Channel in
southeast Texas and an NGL terminal in Providence, Rhode Island with ship
unloading capabilities.&#160;&#160;Our NGL import facility is primarily used to
offload volumes for delivery to our storage and fractionation facilities located
in Mont Belvieu, Texas.&#160;&#160;Our NGL export facility is used for loading
refrigerated marine tankers for customers.&#160;&#160;Revenues from our terminal
services are primarily based on fees per unit of volume loaded or unloaded and
may also include demand payments if terminaling contracts are
cancelled.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the profitability of our NGL terminal
activities primarily depends on the available quantities of NGLs to be loaded
and offloaded and the fees we charge for these services.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">NGL
fractionation</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.
</font>We own or have interests in 11 NGL fractionation facilities located in
Texas, Louisiana, Colorado and Ohio.&#160;&#160;NGL fractionation facilities
separate mixed NGL streams into purity NGL products.&#160;&#160;The primary
sources of mixed NGLs fractionated in the United States are domestic natural gas
processing plants and crude oil refineries and imports of butane and propane
mixtures.&#160;&#160;Mixed NGLs sourced from domestic natural gas processing
plants and crude oil refineries are typically transported by NGL pipelines and,
to a lesser extent, by railcar and truck to NGL fractionation
facilities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Mixed
NGLs extracted by domestic natural gas processing plants represent the largest
source of volumes processed by our NGL fractionators.&#160;&#160;Based upon
industry data, we believe that sufficient volumes of mixed NGLs, especially
those originating from Gulf Coast, Rocky Mountain and Midcontinent natural gas
processing plants, will be available for fractionation in commercially viable
quantities for the foreseeable future.&#160;&#160;Significant volumes of mixed
NGLs are contractually committed to be processed by our NGL fractionation
facilities by joint owners and third-party customers.</font></div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

    </div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our NGL
fractionation facilities process mixed NGL streams for third-party customers and
support our NGL marketing activities.&#160;&#160;We typically earn revenues from
NGL fractionation under fee-based arrangements.&#160;&#160;These fees (usually
stated in cents per gallon) are contractually subject to adjustment for changes
in certain fractionation expenses, including natural gas fuel
costs.&#160;&#160;At our Norco facility in Louisiana, we perform fractionation
services for certain customers under percent-of-liquids
contracts.&#160;&#160;The results of operations of our NGL fractionation
business are generally dependent upon the volume of mixed NGLs fractionated and
either the level of fractionation fees charged (under fee-based contracts) or
the value of NGLs received (under percent-of-liquids
arrangements).&#160;&#160;Our fee-based fractionation customers retain title to
the NGLs that we process for them.&#160;&#160;To the extent we fractionate
volumes for customers under percent-of-liquids contracts, we are exposed to
fluctuations in NGL prices (i.e., commodity price
risk).&#160;&#160;Periodically, we attempt to mitigate these risks through the
use of commodity derivative instruments such as forward sales
contracts.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Seasonality</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.</font> Our natural gas processing
and NGL fractionation operations typically exhibit little to no seasonal
variation.&#160;&#160;NGL pipeline transportation volumes are generally higher
from October through March due to higher demand for propane (for residential
heating) and normal butane (for blending into motor gasoline).&#160;&#160;With
respect to our NGL and related product storage facilities, we usually experience
an increase in demand for storage services during the spring and summer months
due to increased feedstock storage requirements for motor gasoline production
and a decrease during the fall and winter months when propane inventories are
being drawn down for heating needs.&#160;&#160;Likewise, the revenues we
recognize from NGL marketing activities are predicated on the overall demand for
such products, which may fluctuate due to seasonal needs for gasoline blending
feedstocks, heating requirements and similar factors.&#160;&#160;In general, our
import volumes peak during the spring and summer months and our export volumes
are typically at their highest levels during the winter
months.&#160;&#160;Lastly, our facilities located along the Gulf Coast of the
United States may be affected by weather events such as hurricanes and tropical
storms, which generally arise during the summer and fall months.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Competition</font>.&#160;&#160;Within
their respective market areas, our natural gas processing business activities
and related NGL marketing activities encounter competition from fully integrated
oil companies, intrastate pipeline companies, major interstate pipeline
companies and their non-regulated affiliates, financial institutions with
trading platforms and independent processors.&#160;&#160;Each of our marketing
competitors has varying levels of financial and personnel resources, and
competition generally revolves around price, quality of customer service and
proximity to customers and other market hubs.&#160;&#160;In the markets served
by our NGL pipelines, we compete with a number of intrastate and interstate
pipeline companies (including those affiliated with major oil, petrochemical and
gas companies) and barge, rail and truck fleet operations.&#160;&#160;In
general, our NGL pipelines compete with these entities in terms of
transportation fees and quality of customer service.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
primary competitors in the NGL and related product storage businesses are
integrated major oil companies, chemical companies and other storage and
pipeline companies.&#160;&#160;We compete with other storage service providers
primarily in terms of the fees charged, number of pipeline connections provided
and operational dependability.&#160;&#160;Our import and export operations
compete with those operated by major oil and chemical companies primarily in
terms of loading and offloading throughput capacity.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
compete with a number of NGL fractionators in Texas, Louisiana and
Kansas.&#160;&#160;Competition for such services is primarily based on the
fractionation fee charged.&#160;&#160;However, the ability of an NGL
fractionator to receive a customer&#8217;s mixed NGLs and store and distribute its
purity NGL products is also an important competitive factor and is a function of
having the necessary pipeline and storage infrastructure.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
natural gas processing facilities can be characterized as two distinct types:
(i) straddle plants situated on mainline natural gas pipelines owned either by
us or by third parties or (ii) field plants that process natural gas from
gathering pipelines.&#160;&#160;We operate the Meeker, Pioneer, Toca, Chaco,
North Terrebonne, Calumet, Neptune, Burns Point, Carlsbad and Chaparral plants
and all of the Texas facilities.&#160;&#160;On a weighted-average basis,
utilization rates for these assets were 48.3%, 52.4% and 51.5% during the years
ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively.&#160;&#160;These rates
reflect the periods in which we owned an interest in such
facilities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our NGL marketing activities utilize a
fleet of approximately 600 railcars, the majority of which are leased from third
parties.&#160;&#160;These railcars are used to deliver feedstocks to our
facilities and to distribute NGLs throughout the United States and parts of
Canada.&#160;&#160;We have rail loading and unloading facilities in Alabama,
Arizona, California, Kansas, Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, Nevada, New
York, North Carolina and Texas.&#160;&#160;These facilities service both our
rail shipments and those of our customers.</font></div>

      pipelines located in the coastal regions of Alabama, Louisiana,
      Mississippi and Texas; Port Arthur, Wilcox, Panola and San Jacinto
      pipelines located in east Texas; and our Meeker pipeline in
      Colorado.</font></div>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(9)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">The
      amount shown for Texas includes 34 underground NGL and petrochemical
      storage caverns with an aggregate working capacity of approximately 100
      MMBbls that are owned by EPO (34%) and Duncan Energy Partners
      (66%).&#160;&#160;These 34 caverns are located in Mont Belvieu,
      Texas.</font></div>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(10)&#160;&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Includes
      storage capacity at our facilities in Alabama, Arizona, California,
      Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada,
      New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island,
      South Carolina, South Dakota and Wisconsin.</font></div>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(11)&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Our
      underground storage caverns and above ground storage tanks have an
      aggregate 163.4 MMBbls of total working storage capacity, which includes
      23.4 MMBbls held under long-term operating leases.&#160;&#160;The leased
      facilities are located in Indiana, Kansas, Louisiana, South Dakota and
      Texas.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
maximum number of barrels that our NGL pipelines can transport per day depends
upon the operating balance achieved at a given point in time between various
segments of the systems.&#160;&#160;Since the operating balance is dependent
upon the mix of products being shipped and demand levels at various delivery
points, the exact capacities of our NGL pipelines cannot be reliably
determined.&#160;&#160;We measure the utilization rates of such pipelines in
terms of net throughput, which is based on our ownership
interest.&#160;&#160;Total net throughput volumes for these pipelines were 2,099
MBPD, 1,948 MBPD and 1,794 MBPD during the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008
and 2007, respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
following information highlights the general use of each of our principal NGL
pipelines.&#160;&#160;We operate our NGL pipelines with the exception of the
Skelly-Belvieu Pipeline, Tri-States and a small portion of the Louisiana
Pipeline System.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div>
      <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
            <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
      <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Mid-America Pipeline
      System</font> is a regulated NGL pipeline system consisting of three
      primary segments: the 2,793-mile Rocky Mountain pipeline, the 2,773-mile
      Conway North pipeline and the 2,266-mile Conway South
      pipeline.&#160;&#160;This system is present in 13 states: Wyoming, Utah,
      Colorado, New Mexico, Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas, Missouri, Nebraska, Iowa,
      Illinois, Minnesota and Wisconsin.&#160;&#160;The Rocky Mountain pipeline
      transports mixed NGLs from the Rocky Mountain Overthrust and San Juan
      Basin areas to the Hobbs hub located on the Texas-New Mexico
      border.&#160;&#160;The Conway North segment links the NGL hub at Conway,
      Kansas to refineries, petrochemical plants and propane markets in the
      upper Midwest.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Conway North segment has access
      to NGL supplies from Canada&#8217;s Western Sedimentary Basin through
      third-party connections.&#160;&#160;The Conway South pipeline connects the
      Conway hub with Kansas refineries and transports NGLs to and from Conway,
      Kansas to the Hobbs hub.&#160;&#160;The Mid-America Pipeline System
      interconnects with our Seminole Pipeline and Hobbs NGL fractionator and
      storage facility at the Hobbs hub.&#160;&#160;This system includes 15
      unregulated propane terminals.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
2009, approximately 50% of the volumes transported on the Mid-America Pipeline
System were mixed NGLs originating from natural gas processing
plants.&#160;&#160;The remaining volumes consisted of purity NGL products
originating from NGL fractionators located in Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas, as
well as deliveries from Canada.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div>
      <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
            <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
      <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Seminole Pipeline</font>
      is a regulated pipeline that transports NGLs from the Hobbs hub and the
      Permian Basin area of west Texas to markets in southeast Texas including
      our NGL fractionator in Mont Belvieu, Texas.&#160;&#160;NGLs originating
      on the Mid-America Pipeline System are the primary source of throughput
      for the Seminole Pipeline.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>

<tr valign="top">
            <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
      <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">South Texas NGL
      System</font> is a network of NGL gathering and transportation pipelines
      located in south Texas.&#160;&#160;The system gathers and transports mixed
      NGLs from our south Texas natural gas processing plants to our south Texas
      NGL fractionation facilities.&#160;&#160;In turn, the system
      transports&#160;&#160;NGLs from our south Texas NGL fractionation
      facilities to refineries and petrochemical plants located between Corpus
      Christi, Texas and Houston, Texas and within the Texas City-Houston area,
      as well as to interconnects with common carrier NGL
    pipelines.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>

<tr valign="top">
            <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">

              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
      <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dixie</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Pipeline</font> is a regulated
      pipeline that extends from southeast Texas and Louisiana to markets in the
      southeastern United States and transports propane and other
      NGLs.&#160;&#160;Propane supplies transported on this system primarily
      originate from southeast Texas, south Louisiana and
      Mississippi.&#160;&#160;This system includes eight unregulated propane
      terminals and operates in seven states:&#160;&#160;Texas, Louisiana,
      Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina and North
      Carolina.</font></div>
            </td>

      NGL fractionators and other assets located in Louisiana.&#160;&#160;In
      December 2009, we acquired 215 miles of intrastate pipelines from Chevron
      Midstream Pipelines LLC that expand and extend our Louisiana Pipeline
      System.&#160;&#160;Originating from a central point in Henry, Louisiana,
      the acquired pipelines extend westward to Lake Charles, northward to an
      interconnect with the Dixie Pipeline at Breaux Bridge, and eastward to
      Napoleonville, Louisiana, where our Promix NGL fractionation and storage
      facilities are located.</font></div>

              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
      <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Mont Belvieu</font> NGL
      fractionation facility is located in Mont Belvieu, Texas, which is a key
      hub of the NGL industry.&#160;&#160;This facility fractionates mixed NGLs
      from several major NGL supply basins in North America including the
      Mid-Continent, Permian Basin, San Juan Basin, Rocky Mountains, east Texas
      and the Gulf Coast.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In August
2009, we announced plans to build a new 75 MBPD NGL fractionator at our Mont
Belvieu facility that will provide us with additional capacity to process
growing NGL volumes from producing areas in the Rockies, the Barnett Shale and
the emerging Eagle Ford Shale supply basin in south Texas.&#160;&#160;This
growth capital project will increase our gross NGL fractionation capacity at
Mont Belvieu to approximately 305 MBPD.&#160;&#160;The project is expected to be
completed in the first quarter of 2011.</font></div>

located on the Houston Ship Channel that can load or offload two barges of NGLs
or refinery-grade propylene simultaneously at rates up to 5,000 barrels per
hour.&#160;&#160;We also own an NGL terminal in Providence, Rhode Island that
includes 0.4 MMBbls of refrigerated tank storage capacity and ship unloading
capabilities at rates up to 11,800 barrels per hour. Our average combined NGL
import and export </font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Onshore
Natural Gas Pipelines &amp; Services</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
Onshore Natural Gas Pipelines &amp; Services business segment includes
approximately 19,200 miles of onshore natural gas pipeline systems that provide
for the gathering and transportation of natural gas in Alabama, Colorado,
Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico, Texas and Wyoming.&#160;&#160;We own two
salt dome natural gas storage facilities located in Mississippi and lease
natural gas storage facilities located in Texas and Louisiana.&#160;&#160;This
segment also includes our related natural gas marketing activities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Onshore
natural gas pipelines and related natural gas marketing activities</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">. </font>Our onshore natural gas
pipeline systems provide for the gathering and transportation of natural gas
from major producing regions such as the San Juan, Barnett Shale, Permian,
Piceance, Greater Green River and Eagle Ford supply basins in the western United
States.&#160;&#160;In addition, certain of these systems receive natural gas
production from the Gulf of Mexico through coastal pipeline interconnects with
offshore pipelines.&#160;&#160;Our onshore natural gas pipelines receive natural
gas from producers, other pipelines or shippers through system interconnects and
redeliver the natural gas to processing facilities, local gas distribution
companies, industrial or municipal customers, or to other onshore
pipelines.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
onshore natural gas pipelines typically generate revenues from transportation
agreements whereby shippers are billed a fee per unit of volume transported
(typically per MMBtu) multiplied by the volume gathered or
delivered.&#160;&#160;The transportation fees charged under these arrangements
are either contractual or regulated by governmental agencies, including the
FERC.&#160;&#160;Certain of our onshore natural gas pipelines offer firm
capacity reservation services whereby the shipper pays a contractually stated
fee based on the level of throughput capacity reserved in our pipelines whether
or not the shipper actually utilizes such capacity.&#160;&#160;In connection
with our natural gas transportation services and marketing activities,
intrastate natural gas pipelines (such as our Acadian Gas System) may also
purchase natural gas from producers and other suppliers for transport and resale
to customers such as electric utility companies, local natural gas distribution
companies, industrial users and other natural gas marketing
companies.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
natural gas marketing activities generate revenues from the sale and delivery of
natural gas obtained from third-party well-head purchases, regional natural gas
processing plants and the open market.&#160;&#160;In general, sales prices
referenced in the contracts utilized within our natural gas marketing activities
are market-based and may include pricing differentials for such factors as
delivery location.&#160;&#160;We entered the natural gas marketing business in
an effort to maximize the utilization of our portfolio of natural gas pipeline
and storage assets.&#160;&#160;We expect our natural gas marketing business to
continue to expand in the future.&#160;&#160;The results of operations for our
onshore natural gas pipelines and related marketing activities are generally
dependent upon the volume of natural gas transported and/or sold and amounts
charged to customers (including those charged internally, which are eliminated
in the preparation of our consolidated financial statements).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are
exposed to commodity price risk to the extent that we take title to natural gas
volumes in connection with certain intrastate natural gas transportation
contracts and our natural gas marketing activities.&#160;&#160;In addition, we
purchase and resell natural gas for certain producers that use our San Juan,
Carlsbad and Jonah Gathering Systems and certain segments of our Texas
Intrastate System.&#160;&#160;Also, several of our gathering systems, while not
providing marketing services, have some exposure to risks related to
fluctuations in commodity prices through transportation arrangements with
shippers.&#160;&#160;For example, nearly all of the transportation revenues
generated by our San Juan Gathering System are based on a percentage of a
regional price index for natural gas.&#160;&#160;This index is subject to change
based on a variety of factors including natural gas supply and consumer
demand.&#160;&#160;We use derivative instruments to mitigate our exposure to
commodity price risks associated with our natural gas pipelines and services
business.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Underground
natural gas storage</font>. We own two underground salt dome natural gas storage
facilities located near Hattiesburg, Mississippi that serve the domestic
Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Southeast natural gas markets.&#160;&#160;On a
combined basis, these facilities (our Petal Gas Storage (&#8220;Petal&#8221;)
and</font></div>
    <div><br></div>

        </div>

    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Hattiesburg
Gas Storage locations) are capable of delivering in excess of 1.4 Bcf/d of
natural gas into six interstate pipeline systems.&#160;&#160;We also lease
underground salt dome natural gas storage caverns that serve markets in Texas
and Louisiana.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our natural gas storage facilities are
designed for sustained periods of high natural gas deliveries, including the
ability to quickly switch from full injection to full withdrawal modes of
operation.&#160;&#160;The ability of underground salt dome storage caverns to
handle high levels of injections and withdrawals of natural gas benefits
customers who desire the ability to meet load swings and to cover major supply
interruption events, such as hurricanes and temporary losses of
production.&#160;&#160;High injection and withdrawal rates also allow customers
to take advantage of periods of volatile natural gas prices and respond quickly
in situations where they have natural gas imbalance issues on pipelines
connected to the storage facilities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Under our natural gas storage
contracts, there are typically two components of revenues: (i) monthly demand
payments, which are associated with a customer&#8217;s storage capacity reservation
and paid regardless of actual usage, and (ii) storage fees per unit of volume
stored at our facilities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Seasonality</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">. </font>Typically, our onshore
natural gas pipelines experience higher throughput rates during the summer
months as natural gas-fired power generation utilities increase their output to
meet residential and commercial demand for electricity used for air
conditioning.&#160;&#160;Higher throughput rates are also experienced in the
winter months as natural gas is used to meet residential and commercial heating
requirements.&#160;&#160;Likewise, this seasonality also impacts the timing of
injections and withdrawals at our natural gas storage facilities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Competition</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">. </font>Within their market areas,
our onshore natural gas pipelines compete with other natural gas pipelines on
the basis of price (in terms of transportation fees), quality of customer
service and operational flexibility.&#160;&#160;Competition for natural gas
storage is primarily based on location and the ability to deliver natural gas in
a timely and reliable manner.&#160;&#160;Our natural gas storage facilities
compete with other providers of natural gas storage, including other salt dome
storage facilities and depleted reservoir facilities.&#160;&#160;Our natural gas
marketing activities compete primarily with other natural gas pipeline companies
and their marketing affiliates and financial institutions with trading
platforms.&#160;&#160;Competition in the natural gas marketing business is based
primarily on quality of customer service, competitive pricing and proximity to
customers and other market hubs.</font></div>

64.4%, 68.7% and 67.0% during the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007,

for 2007 excludes our Piceance Basin Gathering System, which operated at an

system. &#160;Our utilization rates reflect the periods in which we owned an
interest in such assets or, for recently constructed assets, since the dates
such assets were placed into service.</font></div>

173-mile Sherman Extension pipeline, which is part of our Texas Intrastate
System, was completed in late February 2009 and is capable of transporting up to
1.2 Bcf/d of natural gas from the prolific Barnett Shale production basin in
north Texas.&#160;&#160;The Sherman Extension provides producers with
connections to third-party interstate pipelines having access to markets outside
of Texas.&#160;&#160;An aggregate of 1.0 Bcf/d of the Sherman Extension&#8217;s
throughput capacity has been contracted for by customers, including EPO, under
long-term contracts.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In late
2008, we began design of the 40-mile Trinity River Lateral, which is expected to
be completed during the second quarter of 2010.&#160;&#160;The Trinity River
Lateral will be capable of transporting up to 1.0 Bcf/d of natural gas and will
provide producers in the Barnett Shale production basin with additional takeaway
capacity.&#160;&#160;We are also constructing a new storage cavern adjacent to
the leased Wilson natural gas storage facility that is expected to be completed
in 2010.&#160;&#160;When completed, this new cavern is expected to provide us
with an additional 5.0 Bcf of natural gas storage capacity.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Onshore
Crude Oil Pipelines &amp; Services</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
Onshore Crude Oil Pipelines &amp; Services business segment includes
approximately 4,400 miles of onshore crude oil pipelines and 10.5 MMBbls of
above-ground storage tank capacity.&#160;&#160;This segment includes our crude
oil marketing activities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Onshore
crude oil pipelines, terminals and related marketing
activities</font>.&#160;&#160;Our onshore crude oil pipeline systems gather and
transport crude oil primarily in Oklahoma, New Mexico and Texas to refineries,
centralized storage terminals and connecting pipelines.&#160;&#160;Revenue from
crude oil transportation is generally based upon a fixed fee per barrel
transported multiplied by the volume delivered.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the
results of operations for this business are generally dependent upon the volume
of crude oil transported and the level of fees charged to customers (including
those charged internally, which are eliminated in the preparation of our
consolidated financial statements).&#160;&#160;The transportation fees charged
under these arrangements are either contractual or regulated by governmental
agencies, including the FERC.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We own crude oil terminal facilities in
Cushing, Oklahoma and Midland, Texas that are used to store crude oil volumes
for us and our customers.&#160;&#160;Under our crude oil terminaling agreements,
we charge customers for crude oil storage based on the number of days a customer
has volumes in storage multiplied by a contractual storage rate.&#160;&#160;With
respect to storage capacity reservation agreements, we collect a fee for
reserving storage capacity for customers at our terminals.&#160;&#160;The
customers pay reservation fees based on the level of storage capacity reserved
rather than the actual volumes stored.&#160;&#160;In addition, we charge our
customers throughput (or &#8220;pumpover&#8221;) fees based on volumes withdrawn from our
terminals.&#160;&#160;Lastly, we provide fee-based trade documentation services
whereby we document the transfer of title for crude oil volumes transacted
between buyers and sellers at our terminals.&#160;&#160;In general, the
profitability of our crude oil terminaling operations is dependent upon the
level of storage capacity reserved by our customers, the volume of product
withdrawn from our terminals and the level of fees charged (including those
charged internally, which are eliminated in the preparation of our consolidated
financial statements).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our crude oil marketing activities
generate revenues from the sale and delivery of crude oil obtained from
producers or on the open market.&#160;&#160;In general, the sales prices
referenced in these contracts are market-based and may include pricing
differentials for such factors as delivery location.&#160;&#160;To limit the
exposure of our crude oil marketing activities to commodity price risk, our
purchases and sales of crude oil are generally contracted to occur within the
same calendar month.&#160;&#160;We also use derivative instruments to mitigate
our exposure to commodity price risks associated with our crude oil marketing
business.</font></div>

onshore crude oil pipelines and related activities typically exhibit little to
no effects of seasonality.&#160;&#160;However, our onshore pipelines situated
along the Texas Gulf Coast may be affected by weather events such as hurricanes
and tropical storms.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Competition</font>.&#160;&#160;Within
their respective market areas, our onshore crude oil pipelines, terminals and
related marketing activities compete with other crude oil pipeline companies,
major integrated oil companies and their marketing affiliates, financial
institutions with trading platforms and independent crude oil gathering and
marketing companies.&#160;&#160;The onshore crude oil business can be
characterized by thin operating margins and strong competition for supplies of
crude oil.&#160;&#160;Declines in domestic crude oil production have intensified
this competition.&#160;&#160;Competition is based primarily on quality of
customer service, competitive pricing and proximity to customers and other
market hubs.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
maximum number of barrels that our crude oil pipelines can transport per day
depends upon the operating balance achieved at a given point in time between
various segments of the systems.&#160;&#160;Since the operating balance is
dependent upon product composition and demand levels at various delivery points,
the exact capacities of our crude oil pipelines cannot be reliably
determined.&#160;&#160;We measure the utilization rates of such pipelines in
terms of net throughput, which is based on our ownership
interest.&#160;&#160;Total net throughput volumes for these pipelines were 680
MBPD, 696 MBPD and 652 MBPD during the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and
2007, respectively.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
following information highlights the general use of each of our principal crude
oil pipelines and terminals, all of which we operate with the exception of the
Basin Pipeline System.</font></div>

<tr valign="top">
            <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
      <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Seaway Crude Pipeline
      System</font> is a regulated system that transports imported crude oil
      from Freeport, Texas to Cushing, Oklahoma and supplies refineries in the
      Houston, Texas area through its terminal facility at Texas City,
      Texas.&#160;&#160;The Seaway Crude Pipeline System also has a connection
      to our South Texas System that allows it to receive both onshore and
      offshore domestic crude oil production from the Texas Gulf Coast area for
      delivery to Cushing.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>

      <div>
        <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
              <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
                <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
              </td>
              <td>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
                  <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
                    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
      <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Red River System</font>
      is a regulated pipeline that transports crude oil from north Texas to
      south Oklahoma for delivery to either two local refineries or pipeline
      interconnects for further transportation to Cushing,

      <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

            <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic"> South Texas System</font>
      transports crude oil from an origination point in south Texas to the

Oklahoma.</font></div>

            <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
      <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Cushing </font>and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Midland terminals</font>
      provide crude oil storage, pumpover and trade documentation
      services.&#160;&#160;Our terminal in Cushing, Oklahoma has 19 above-ground
      storage tanks with aggregate crude oil storage capacity of 3.1
      MMBbls.&#160;&#160;The Midland terminal has a storage capacity of 1.0
      MMBbls through the use of 12 above-ground storage
  tanks.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Offshore
Pipelines &amp; Services</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
Offshore Pipelines &amp; Services business segment serves some of the most
active drilling and development regions, including deepwater production fields,
in the northern Gulf of Mexico offshore Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi and
Alabama.&#160;&#160;This segment includes approximately 1,400 miles of offshore
natural gas pipelines, approximately 1,000 miles of offshore crude oil pipelines
and six offshore hub platforms.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
offshore Gulf of Mexico pipelines provide for the gathering and transportation
of natural gas or crude oil.&#160;&#160;In general, revenues from our offshore
pipelines are derived from fee-based agreements whereby the customer is charged
a fee per unit of volume gathered or transported (typically per MMBtu of natural
gas or per barrel of crude oil) multiplied by the volume
delivered.&#160;&#160;These agreements tend to be long-term, often involving
life-of-reserve commitments with both firm and interruptible
components.&#160;&#160;In the case of our Poseidon Oil Pipeline System, we
purchase crude oil from producers and shippers at a receipt point (at a fixed or
index-based price less a location differential) and then sell like quantities of
crude oil back to the customer at onshore Louisiana locations (at the same fixed
or index-based price, as applicable).&#160;&#160;The net revenue we recognize
from such arrangements is based on the location differential, which represents
the fee Poseidon charges for providing transportation services.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
offshore platforms are integral components of our pipeline
operations.&#160;&#160;In general, platforms are critical components of the
energy-related infrastructure in the Gulf of Mexico, supporting drilling and
producing operations, and therefore play a key role in the overall development
of offshore crude oil and natural gas reserves.&#160;&#160;Platforms are used
to:&#160;&#160;interconnect the offshore pipeline grid; provide an efficient
means to perform pipeline maintenance; locate compression, separation and
production handling equipment and similar assets; conduct drilling operations
during the initial development phase of an oil and natural gas property and
process off-lease production.&#160;&#160;Revenues from offshore platform
services generally consist of demand fees and commodity
charges.&#160;&#160;Demand fees are similar to firm capacity reservation
agreements for a pipeline in that they are charged to a customer regardless of
the volume the customer actually delivers to the platform.&#160;&#160;Revenues
from commodity charges are based on a fixed-fee per unit of volume delivered to
the platform (typically per MMcf of natural gas or per barrel of crude oil)
multiplied by the total volume of each product delivered.&#160;&#160;Contracts
for platform services often include both demand fees and commodity charges, but
demand fees generally expire after a contractually fixed period of time and in
some instances may be subject to cancellation by customers.&#160;&#160;For
example, the producers utilizing our Independence Hub platform have agreed to
pay us $54.6 million of demand fees annually through March
2012.&#160;&#160;These demand fees are in addition to commodity charges they pay
us based on volumes delivered to the platform.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In August
2008, we and Oiltanking Holding Americas, Inc. (&#8220;Oiltanking&#8221;) announced the
formation of a joint venture, the Texas Offshore Port System (&#8220;TOPS&#8221;), that
would design, construct, operate and own a Texas offshore crude oil port and
related onshore pipeline and storage system located</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Seasonality</font>.
Our offshore operations exhibit little to no effects of seasonality; however,
they may be affected by weather events such as hurricanes and tropical storms in
the Gulf of Mexico.&#160;&#160;See Note 19 of the Notes to Consolidated
Financial Statements included under Item 8 of this annual report for information
regarding weather-related risks and insurance matters.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Competition</font>.
Within their respective market areas, our offshore pipelines compete with other
offshore pipelines primarily on the basis of fees charged, available throughput
capacity, connections to downstream markets and proximity and access to existing
reserves.&#160;&#160;Our competitors may have access to greater capital
resources than we do, which could enable them to address business opportunities
in the Gulf of Mexico more quickly than we can.</font></div>

                <td align="right" valign="bottom" width="9%">
                  <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">3</font></div>
                </td>
              </tr><tr bgcolor="white">
                <td valign="bottom" width="3%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 2px solid"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;
      </font></td>
                <td valign="bottom" width="31%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 2px solid"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;
      </font></td>
                <td valign="bottom" width="8%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 2px solid"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;
      </font></td>
                <td valign="bottom" width="8%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 2px solid"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;
      </font></td>

      </font></td>
                <td valign="bottom" width="9%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 2px solid"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;
      </font></td>
                <td valign="bottom" width="9%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 2px solid"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;
      </font></td>
              </tr><tr bgcolor="white">
                <td colspan="7" valign="bottom" width="77%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">
                  <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(1)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Based
      on the maximum allowable operating pressure, our HIOS pipeline system can
      transport up to 1,800 MMcf/d of natural gas.&#160;&#160;On January 12,
      2010, we filed for FERC authority to reduce the firm certificated capacity
      on the HIOS pipeline system from 1,400 MMcf/d to 350 MMcf/d.</font></div>
                  <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(2)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Our
      ownership interests in the Green Canyon Laterals ranges from 2.7% to
      100%.</font></div>
                  <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(3)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Our
      ownership interest in these pipeline systems is held indirectly through
      our equity method investment in Neptune Pipeline Company, L.L.C.
      (&#8220;Neptune&#8221;).</font></div>
                  <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(4)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Our
      ownership interest in this system is held indirectly through our equity
      method investment in VESCO.</font></div>
                  <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(5)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Our
      ownership interest in this system is held indirectly through our equity
      method investment in Nemo Gathering Company, LLC (&#8220;Nemo&#8221;).</font></div>
                  <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(6)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Our
      50% joint control ownership interest in this pipeline is held indirectly

                  <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(7)&#160;&#160;

                  <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(8)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Our
      50% joint control ownership interest in this platform is held indirectly
      through our equity method investment in Deepwater Gateway, L.L.C.

                </td>
              </tr></table>

        <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We operate our offshore natural gas
pipelines, with the exception of the VESCO Gathering System, Manta Ray Offshore
Gathering System, Nautilus System, Nemo Gathering System and certain components
of the Green Canyon Laterals.&#160;&#160;On a weighted-average basis, aggregate
utilization rates for our offshore natural gas pipelines were approximately
22.3%, 22% and 24.1% during the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007,
respectively.&#160;&#160;For recently constructed assets, utilization rates
reflect the periods since such assets were placed into
service.</font></div>
