    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Petrochemical
&amp; Refined Products Services</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
Petrochemical &amp; Refined Products Services business segment consists of (i)
propylene fractionation plants and related activities, (ii) butane isomerization
facilities, (iii) an octane enhancement facility, (iv) refined products
pipelines, including our Products Pipeline System (as defined below), and
related activities and (v) marine transportation and other
services.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Propylene
fractionation and related activities</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">. </font>Our propylene fractionation
and related activities primarily consist of two propylene fractionation plants
(one located in Mont Belvieu, Texas and the other in Baton Rouge, Louisiana),
propylene pipeline systems aggregating approximately 670 miles in length and
related petrochemical marketing activities.&#160;&#160;This business includes an
export facility and associated above-ground polymer grade propylene storage
spheres located in Seabrook, Texas.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In general, propylene fractionation
plants separate refinery grade propylene, which is a mixture of propane and
propylene, into either polymer grade propylene or chemical grade propylene along
with by-products of propane and mixed butane.&#160;&#160;Polymer grade and
chemical grade propylene can also be produced as a by-product of ethylene
production.&#160;&#160;The demand for polymer grade propylene primarily relates
to the manufacture of polypropylene, which has a variety of end uses including
packaging film, fiber for carpets and upholstery and molded plastic parts for
appliances and automotive, houseware and medical products.&#160;&#160;Chemical
grade propylene is a basic petrochemical used in the manufacturing of plastics,
synthetic fibers and foams.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Results
of operations for our polymer grade propylene plants are generally dependent
upon toll processing arrangements and petrochemical marketing
activities.&#160;&#160;The toll processing arrangements typically include a
base-processing fee per gallon (or other unit of measurement) subject to
adjustment for changes in natural gas, electricity and labor costs, which are
the primary costs of propylene fractionation.&#160;&#160;Our petrochemical
marketing activities generate revenues from the purchase and fractionation of
refinery grade propylene in the open market and the sale and delivery of
products obtained through our propylene fractionation activities.&#160;&#160;In
general, we sell our petrochemical products at market-based prices, which may
include pricing differentials for such factors as delivery
location.&#160;&#160;The majority of revenues from our propylene pipelines are
based upon a transportation fee per unit of volume multiplied by the volume
delivered to the customer.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As part
of our petrochemical marketing activities, we have several long-term refinery
grade purchase and polymer grade propylene sales agreements.&#160;&#160;To limit
the exposure of our petrochemical marketing activities to commodity price risk,
we attempt to match the timing and price of our feedstock purchases with those
of the sales of end products.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Butane
isomerization</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.
</font>Our butane isomerization business includes three butamer reactor units
and eight associated deisobutanizer units located in Mont Belvieu, Texas, which
comprise the largest commercial isomerization facility in the United
States.&#160;&#160;In addition, this business includes a 70-mile pipeline system
used to transport high-purity isobutane from Mont Belvieu, Texas to Port Neches,
Texas.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our commercial isomerization units
convert normal butane into mixed butane, which is subsequently fractionated into
isobutane, high-purity isobutane and residual normal butane.&#160;&#160;The
primary uses of isobutane are for the production of propylene oxide, isooctane
and alkylate for motor gasoline.&#160;&#160;The demand for commercial
isomerization services depends upon the industry&#8217;s requirements for high purity
isobutane and isobutane in excess of naturally occurring isobutane produced from
NGL fractionation and refinery operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
results of operation of this business are generally dependent upon the volume of
normal and mixed butanes processed and the level of toll processing fees charged
to customers.&#160;&#160;These processing arrangements typically include a
base-processing fee per gallon (or other unit of measurement) subject
to</font></div>
    </div>

    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">adjustment
for changes in natural gas, electricity and labor costs, which are the primary
costs of isomerization.&#160;&#160;Our isomerization facility provides
processing services to meet the needs of third-party customers and our other
businesses, including our NGL marketing activities and octane enhancement
production facility.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Octane
enhancement</font>.&#160;&#160;We own and operate an octane enhancement
production facility located in Mont Belvieu, Texas that is designed to produce
isooctane, isobutylene and methyl tertiary butyl ether
(&#8220;MTBE&#8221;).&#160;&#160;These products are used in reformulated motor gasoline
blends to increase octane values.&#160;&#160;The high-purity isobutane
feedstocks consumed in the production of these products are supplied by our
isomerization units.&#160;&#160;To the extent that MTBE is produced at the
facility, it is sold into the export market.&#160;&#160;The results of
operations of this business are generally dependent upon the sale and delivery
of products produced.&#160;&#160;In general, we sell our octane enhancement
products at market-based prices, which may include pricing differentials for
such factors as delivery location.&#160;&#160;We attempt to mitigate price risk
by entering into certain commodity hedging transactions.&#160;&#160;This
facility undergoes an annual maintenance turnaround that generally occurs during
the first quarter of each year.&#160;&#160;During these periods of shutdown, the
plant may incur operating losses.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Refined
products pipelines and related activities</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>Our refined
products pipelines and related activities primarily consist of (i) a regulated
4,700-mile products pipeline system and related terminal operations (the
&#8220;Products Pipeline System&#8221;) that generally extends in a northeasterly direction
from the upper Texas Gulf Coast to the northeast United States and (ii) a 50%
joint venture interest in Centennial Pipeline LLC (&#8220;Centennial&#8221;), which owns a
794-mile refined products pipeline system that extends from the upper Texas Gulf
Coast to central Illinois (the &#8220;Centennial Pipeline&#8221;).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Products Pipeline System transports
refined products, and to a lesser extent, petrochemicals such as ethylene and
propylene and NGLs such as propane and normal butane.&#160;&#160;These refined
products are produced by refineries and include gasoline, diesel fuel, aviation
fuel, kerosene, distillates and heating oil.&#160;&#160;Refined products
also&#160;include blend stocks such as raffinate and naphtha.&#160; Blend stocks
are primarily used&#160;to produce gasoline or as a feedstock for certain
petrochemicals.&#160;&#160;The Centennial Pipeline intersects our Products
Pipeline System near Creal Springs, Illinois, and effectively loops the Products
Pipeline System between Beaumont, Texas and south Illinois.&#160;&#160;Looping
the Products Pipeline System permits effective supply of products to points
south of Illinois as well as incremental product supply capacity to other
Midcontinent markets.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
refined products pipelines and related activities include the distribution and
marketing operations we provide at our Aberdeen, Mississippi and Boligee,
Alabama river terminals.&#160;&#160;In the fourth quarter of 2009, we expanded
the terminaling and marketing operations associated with our refined products
pipeline business.&#160;&#160;These activities generated nominal amounts of
gross operating margin during 2009; however, we expect that our refined products
marketing activities will increase beginning in 2010 in an effort to increase
the utilization of our portfolio of refined products pipelines and terminal
assets.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
results of operations of our refined products pipelines are primarily dependent
on the tariffs charged to customers to transport products.&#160;&#160;The
tariffs charged for such services are either contractual or regulated by
governmental agencies, including the FERC.&#160;&#160;Our related marketing
activities generate revenues from the sale and delivery of refined products
obtained from third parties on the open market.&#160;&#160;In general, we sell
our refined products at market-based prices, which may include pricing
differentials for such factors as delivery location.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Marine
transportation and other services</font>.&#160;&#160;Our marine transportation
business consists of tow boats and tank barges that are used primarily to
transport refined products, crude oil, asphalt, condensate, heavy fuel oil and
other heated oil products along key inland and intercoastal U.S.
waterways.&#160;&#160;Our marine transportation assets service refinery and
storage terminal customers along the Mississippi, Illinois and Ohio rivers, the
Intracoastal Waterway between Texas and Florida and the Tennessee-Tombigbee
Waterway system.&#160;&#160;In addition, we provide marine vessel fueling
services for cruise liners and cargo ships as well as other ship-assist services
in Miami, Florida.&#160;&#160;Other non-marine services consist of
the</font></div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">26</font></div>
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">distribution
of lubrication oils and specialty chemicals and the bulk transportation of fuels
by truck, principally in Oklahoma, Texas, New Mexico and the Rocky Mountain
region of the United States.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
results of operations of our marine transportation business, which we entered
into in February 2008 upon the acquisition of tow boats, tank barges and related
assets from Cenac Towing Co., Inc. and affiliates (collectively, &#8220;Cenac&#8221;), are
generally dependent upon the level of fees charged to transport
cargo.&#160;&#160;Transportation services are typically provided under term
contracts (also referred to as affreightment contracts), which are agreements
with specific customers to transport cargo from within designated operating
areas at set day rates or a set fee per cargo movement.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
results of operations from the distribution of lubrication oils and specialty
chemicals and the bulk transportation of fuels are dependent on the sales price
or transportation fees that we charge our customers.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Seasonality</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>Overall,
the propylene fractionation business exhibits little seasonality.&#160;&#160;Our
isomerization operations experience slightly higher levels of demand in the
spring and summer months due to increased demand for isobutane-based fuel
additives used in the production of motor gasoline.&#160;&#160;Likewise, octane
additive prices have been stronger during the April to September period of each
year, which corresponds with the summer driving season, when motor gasoline
demand increases.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
refined products pipelines and related activities exhibit seasonality based upon
the mix of products delivered and the weather and economic conditions in the
geographic areas being served.&#160;&#160;Refined products volumes are generally
higher during the second and third quarters of each year because of greater
demand for motor gasoline during the spring and summer driving
seasons.&#160;&#160;NGL transportation volumes on the Products Pipeline System
are generally higher from October through March due to higher demand for propane
(for residential heating) and normal butane (for blending in motor
gasoline).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
marine transportation business exhibits some seasonal
variation.&#160;&#160;Demand for motor gasoline and asphalt is generally
stronger in the spring and summer months due to the summer driving season and
when weather allows for more efficient road construction.&#160;&#160;Weather
events, such as hurricanes and tropical storms in the Gulf of Mexico, can
adversely impact both the offshore and inland businesses.&#160;&#160;Generally
during the winter months, cold weather and ice can negatively impact the inland
operations on the upper Mississippi and Illinois rivers.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Competition</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">. </font>We compete with numerous
producers of polymer grade propylene, which include many of the major refiners
and petrochemical companies located along the Gulf Coast.&#160;&#160;Generally,
our propylene fractionation business competes in terms of the level of toll
processing fees charged and access to pipeline and storage
infrastructure.&#160;&#160;Our petrochemical marketing activities encounter
competition from fully integrated oil companies and various petrochemical
companies.&#160;&#160;Our petrochemical marketing competitors have varying
levels of financial and personnel resources and competition generally revolves
around price, quality of customer service, logistics and location.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">With
respect to our isomerization operations, we compete primarily with facilities
located in Kansas, Louisiana and New Mexico.&#160;&#160;Competitive factors
affecting this business include the level of toll processing fees charged, the
quality of isobutane that can be produced and access to pipeline and storage
supporting infrastructure.&#160;&#160;We compete with other octane additive
manufacturing companies primarily on the basis of price.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Products Pipeline System&#8217;s most significant competitors are third-party
pipelines in the areas where it delivers products.&#160;&#160;Competition among
common carrier pipelines is based primarily on transportation fees, quality of
customer service and proximity to end users.&#160;&#160;Trucks, barges and
railroads competitively deliver products into some of the areas served by our
Products Pipeline System and river terminals.&#160;&#160;The Products Pipeline
System faces competition from rail and pipeline movements of NGLs from Canada
and waterborne imports into terminals located along the upper East
Coast.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We produce polymer grade propylene at
our Mont Belvieu, Texas propylene fractionation facility and chemical grade
propylene at our BRPC facility located in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.&#160;&#160;The
primary purpose of the BRPC unit is to fractionate refinery grade propylene
produced by an affiliate of Exxon Mobil Corporation into chemical grade
propylene.&#160;&#160;The polymer grade propylene produced by our Mont Belvieu
facility is primarily for the benefit of our tolling customers and used in our
petrochemical marketing activities to service long-term third-party supply
contracts.&#160;&#160;On a weighted-average basis, aggregate utilization rates
of our propylene fractionation facilities were approximately 85%, 72.2% and 86%
during the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007,
respectively.&#160;&#160;As noted previously, this business includes an export
facility and above-ground polymer grade propylene storage
spheres.&#160;&#160;This facility, which is located on the Houston Ship Channel
in Seabrook, Texas, can load vessels at rates up to 5,000 barrels per
hour.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Lou-Tex Propylene pipeline is used to transport chemical grade propylene from
Sorrento, Louisiana to Mont Belvieu, Texas.&#160;&#160;The Sabine pipeline is
used to transport polymer grade propylene from Port Arthur, Texas to a
third-party pipeline interconnect located in Cameron Parish,
Louisiana.&#160;&#160;The North Dean Pipeline System transports refinery grade
propylene from Mont Belvieu, Texas, to Point Comfort, Texas.</font></div>

maximum number of barrels that our petrochemical pipelines can transport per day
depends upon the operating balance achieved at a given point in time between
various segments of the systems.&#160;&#160;Since the operating balance is
dependent upon the mix of products to be shipped and demand levels at various
delivery points, the exact capacities of our petrochemical pipelines cannot be
reliably determined.&#160;&#160;We measure the utilization rates of such
pipelines in terms of net throughput, which is based on our ownership
interest.&#160;&#160;Total net throughput volumes for these pipelines were 124
MBPD, 116 MBPD and 114 MBPD during the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and
2007, respectively.</font></div>

            <td>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
      <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Products Pipeline
      System</font> is a regulated pipeline system that transports refined
      products, petrochemicals and NGLs.&#160;&#160;This pipeline system
      includes receiving, storage and terminaling facilities and is present in
      12 states: Texas, Louisiana, Arkansas, Tennessee, Missouri, Illinois,
      Kentucky, Indiana, Ohio, West Virginia, Pennsylvania and New
      York.&#160;&#160;Our Products Pipeline System transports refined products
      from the upper Texas Gulf Coast, eastern Texas and southern Arkansas to
      the Central and Midwest regions of the United States with deliveries in
      Texas, Louisiana, Arkansas, Missouri, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio and
      Kentucky.&#160;&#160;At these points, refined products are delivered to
      terminals owned by us, connecting pipelines and customer-owned
      terminals.&#160;&#160;Petrochemicals are transported on our Products
      Pipeline System between Mont Belvieu, Texas and Port Arthur,
      Texas.&#160;&#160;Our Products Pipeline System transports NGLs from the
      upper Texas Gulf Coast to the Central, Midwest and Northeast regions of
      the United States and is</font></div>
            </td>

December 2006, we signed an agreement with Motiva Enterprises, LLC (&#8220;Motiva&#8221;) to
construct and operate a refined products storage facility to support an
expansion of Motiva&#8217;s refinery in Port Arthur, Texas.&#160;&#160;Under the terms
of the agreement, we will construct 20 storage tanks with a capacity of 5.4
MMBbls for gasoline and distillates, five 5-mile product pipelines connecting
the storage facility to Motiva&#8217;s refinery and distribution pipeline connections
to the Colonial, Explorer and Magtex pipelines.&#160;&#160;As part of a separate
but complementary initiative, we constructed an 11-mile pipeline to connect the
new storage facility in Port Arthur to our refined products terminal in
Beaumont, Texas.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
marine transportation industry uses tow boats as power sources and tank barges
for freight capacity.&#160;&#160;We refer to the combination of the power source
and freight capacity as a tow.&#160;&#160;Our inland tows generally consist of
one tow boat paired with up to four tank barges, depending upon the horsepower
of the tow boat, location, waterway conditions, customer requirements and
prudent operational considerations.&#160;&#160;Our offshore tows generally
consist of one tow boat and one ocean-certified tank barge.&#160;&#160;In June
2009, we expanded our marine transportation business with the acquisition of 19
tow boats and 28 tank barges from TransMontaigne Product Services Inc. for $50.0
million in cash.&#160;&#160;Our marine transportation business is subject to
regulation by the U.S. Department of Transportation (&#8220;DOT&#8221;), Department of
Homeland Security, Commerce Department and the U.S. Coast Guard (&#8220;USCG&#8221;) and
federal and state laws.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>ETP&#8217;s partnership agreement requires

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ETP is a
publicly traded partnership owning and operating a diversified portfolio of
midstream energy assets.&#160;&#160;ETP has pipeline operations in Arizona,
Colorado, Louisiana, New Mexico and Utah, and owns the largest intrastate
natural gas pipeline system in Texas.&#160;&#160;ETP&#8217;s natural gas operations
include natural gas gathering and transportation pipelines, natural gas treating
and processing assets and three natural gas storage facilities located in
Texas.&#160;&#160;ETP is also one of the three largest retail marketers of
propane in the United States, serving more than one million customers across the
country.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ETP
operates in four business lines: (i) Midstream; (ii) Intrastate Transportation
and Storage; (iii) Interstate Transportation and (iv) Retail
Propane.&#160;&#160;The following sections summarize the activities and
principal properties of each of these business lines.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Midstream</font>.&#160;&#160;This
business line includes ETP&#8217;s ownership and operation of approximately 7,000
miles of natural gas gathering pipelines, three natural gas processing plants,
11 natural gas treating facilities and 11 natural gas conditioning
facilities.&#160;&#160;These facilities are located primarily in Texas, Utah and
Colorado.&#160;&#160;The results of operations from this business line are
primarily dependent on the level of fees charged in connection with ETP&#8217;s
gathering, transportation and processing of natural gas and processing of
NGLs.&#160;&#160;In addition, ETP generates margins from the marketing of
natural gas to utilities, industrial consumers and other marketers and pipeline
companies.&#160;&#160;ETP also utilizes derivative instruments to</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Intrastate
Transportation and Storage</font>.&#160;&#160;This business line of ETP includes
approximately 7,800 miles of natural gas transportation pipelines and three
natural gas storage facilities.&#160;&#160;The results of operations from this
business line are primarily dependent on the level of transportation fees
charged by ETP and margins from natural gas sales made in connection with ETP&#8217;s
HPL System.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The key assets within this business
line are the HPL System and the ET Fuel System.&#160;&#160;The HPL System
consists of approximately 4,300 miles of intrastate natural gas pipeline with an
aggregate capacity of 5.5 Bcf/d and the Bammel underground storage reservoir and
related transportation assets.&#160;&#160;The HPL System has access to multiple
sources of historically significant natural gas supply reserves from south
Texas, the Gulf Coast of Texas, east Texas and the western Gulf of Mexico, and
is directly connected to major gas distribution, electric and industrial load
centers in Houston, Corpus Christi, Texas City and other cities located along
the Gulf Coast of Texas.&#160;&#160;The ET Fuel System is comprised of
approximately 2,570 miles of intrastate natural gas pipelines and related
storage facilities located in Texas.&#160;&#160;The ET Fuel System is located
near high-growth production areas and provides ETP access to the Waha Hub near
Midland, Texas, Katy Hub near Houston, Texas and Carthage Hub in east
Texas.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Interstate
Transportation</font>.&#160;&#160;This business line includes ETP&#8217;s Transwestern
pipeline and a 50% interest in two pipeline joint ventures with Kinder Morgan
Energy Partners L.P. (&#8220;Kinder Morgan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The results of operations
from ETP&#8217;s interstate pipelines are dependent on the level of natural gas
transportation fees charged and operational gas sales margins.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Transwestern pipeline is a FERC-regulated interstate natural gas pipeline
extending approximately 2,700 miles from the gas producing regions of west
Texas, east and northwest New Mexico, and south Colorado primarily to pipeline
interconnects off the east end of its system and pipeline interconnects at the
California border.&#160;&#160;The Transwestern pipeline has access to three
significant gas supply basins:&#160;&#160;the Permian Basin in west Texas and
east New Mexico; the San Juan Basin in northwest New Mexico and south Colorado
and the Anadarko Basin in the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles.&#160;&#160;Natural
gas sources from the San Juan Basin and surrounding producing areas can be
delivered eastward to Texas intrastate and mid-continent connecting pipelines
and natural gas market hubs as well as westward to markets in Arizona, Nevada
and California.&#160;&#160;Transwestern&#8217;s customers include local distribution
companies, producers, marketers, electric power generators and industrial
end-users.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>This business line also includes ETP&#8217;s
joint development with Kinder Morgan of the approximately 500-mile interstate
natural gas pipeline, the Midcontinent Express pipeline, which commenced service
in 2009.&#160;&#160;This new pipeline originates near Bennington, Oklahoma, is
routed through Perryville, Louisiana, and terminates at an interconnect with
Transco&#8217;s interstate natural gas pipeline in Butler, Alabama.&#160;&#160;The
Transco pipeline delivers natural gas to significant markets in the northeast
portion of the United States.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
October 2008, ETP entered into a 50/50 joint venture with Kinder Morgan for the
development of the Fayetteville Express pipeline, an approximately 187-mile,
42-inch pipeline that will originate in Conway County, Arkansas, continue
eastward through White County, Arkansas and terminate at an interconnect with
Trunkline Gas Company in Quitman County, Mississippi.&#160; The pipeline is
expected to have an initial capacity of 2.0 Bcf/d and is expected to be in
service by early 2011.&#160; FEP has secured binding 10-year commitments for
transportation of approximately 1.85 Bcf/d. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In January 2009, ETP announced that it
had entered into an agreement to construct the Tiger pipeline, a 178-mile
42-inch interstate natural gas pipeline.&#160;&#160;The Tiger pipeline will
connect to ETP&#8217;s dual 42-inch pipeline system near Carthage, Texas extend
through the heart of the Haynesville Shale and end near Delhi, Louisiana, with
interconnects to at least seven interstate pipelines at various points in
Louisiana.&#160;&#160;The Tiger pipeline will have an initial throughput
capacity of 2.0 Bcf/d, which may be increased to 2.4 Bcf/d with added
compression.&#160;&#160;ETP has secured binding long-term commitments for
transportation of 2.0 Bcf/d.&#160;&#160;The Tiger pipeline is expected to be in
service in early 2011.</font></div>

        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ETP&#8217;s
midstream, intrastate transportation and storage and interstate transportation
businesses experience little to no effects from seasonality.&#160;&#160;ETP
competes with other natural gas and NGL pipelines on the basis of location,
capacity, price and reliability.&#160;&#160;ETP&#8217;s competitors include major
integrated oil companies, interstate and intrastate pipelines and other
companies that gather, compress, treat, process, transport and market natural
gas.&#160;&#160;In marketing natural gas, ETP has numerous competitors,
including marketing affiliates of interstate pipelines, major integrated oil
companies, and local and national natural gas gatherers, brokers and marketers
of widely varying sizes, financial resources and experience.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Retail
Propane</font>.&#160;&#160;ETP, through its subsidiaries Heritage Operating,
L.P. and Titan Energy Partners, L.P., is one of the three largest retail propane
marketers in the United States based on gallons sold.&#160;&#160;ETP serves more
than one million customers from approximately 440 customer service locations in
approximately 40 states.&#160;&#160;ETP&#8217;s propane operations extend from
coast-to-coast with concentrations in the western, upper midwestern,
northeastern and southeastern regions of the United States.&#160;&#160;ETP&#8217;s
propane business has grown primarily through acquisitions of retail propane
operations and, to a lesser extent, through internal growth.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Retail propane is a margin-based
business in which gross profits depend on the excess of sales price over propane
supply cost.&#160;&#160;The market price of propane is often subject to volatile
changes as a result of supply or other market conditions over which ETP has no
control.&#160;&#160;Historically, ETP has generally been successful in
maintaining retail gross margins on an annual basis despite changes in the
wholesale cost of propane; however, there is no assurance that ETP will always
be able to fully pass on product cost increases, particularly when product costs
rise rapidly.&#160;&#160;Consequently, the profitability of ETP&#8217;s retail propane
business is sensitive to changes in wholesale propane prices.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>ETP&#8217;s propane business is seasonal and
dependent upon weather conditions in its market areas.&#160;&#160;Historically,
approximately two-thirds of ETP&#8217;s retail propane volume and substantially all of
its propane-related operating income, is attributable to sales during the
six-month peak-heating season of October through March.&#160;&#160;This pattern
generally results in higher operating revenues and net income for ETP&#8217;s retail
propane business line during the period October through March of each year, and
lower revenues and either net losses or lower net income during the period from
April through September of each year.&#160;&#160;ETP&#8217;s cash flow from operations
is generally greatest when customers pay for propane purchased during the
six-month peak heating season.&#160;&#160;Sales to commercial and industrial
customers are much less sensitive to changes in the weather.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Propane competes with other sources of
energy, some of which are less costly for equivalent energy
value.&#160;&#160;ETP competes for customers against suppliers of electricity,
natural gas and fuel oil.&#160;&#160;Competition from alternative energy sources
has been increasing as a result of reduced utility regulation.&#160;&#160;ETP
also competes with other companies engaged in the retail propane distribution
business.&#160;&#160;Competition in the propane industry is highly fragmented
and generally occurs on a local basis with other large multi-state propane
marketers, thousands of smaller local independent marketers and farm
cooperatives.&#160;&#160;The ability to compete effectively further depends on
the reliability of service, responsiveness to customers and the ability to
maintain competitive prices.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Title
to Properties</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Enterprise
Products Partners&#8217; real property holdings fall into two basic categories: (i)
parcels that it and its unconsolidated affiliates own in fee (e.g., Enterprise
Products Partners owns the land upon which its Mont Belvieu NGL fractionator is
constructed) and (ii) parcels in which Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; interests
and those of its affiliates are derived from leases, easements, rights-of-way,
permits or licenses from landowners or governmental authorities permitting the
use of such land for Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; operations.&#160;&#160;The
fee sites upon which Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; significant facilities are
located have been owned by them or their predecessors in title for many years
without any material challenge known to Enterprise Products Partners relating to
title to the land upon which the assets are located, and Enterprise Products
Partners believes that it has satisfactory title to such fee
sites.&#160;&#160;Enterprise Products Partners and its affiliates have no
knowledge of any challenge to the underlying fee title of any material lease,
easement, right-of-way, permit or license held by Enterprise Products Partners
or to its</font></div>

    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">rights

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Capital
Spending</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>For a discussion of our capital
spending programs, see &#8220;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#8221; included under Item 7
of this annual report.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Regulation</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Interstate
Pipelines</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Liquids
Pipelines</font>.&#160;&#160;Certain of our refined products, crude oil and NGL
pipeline systems (collectively referred to as &#8220;liquids pipelines&#8221;) are
interstate common carrier pipelines subject to regulation by the FERC under the
Interstate Commerce Act (&#8220;ICA&#8221;) and the Energy Policy Act of 1992 (&#8220;Energy
Policy Act&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The ICA prescribes that interstate tariffs must be just
and reasonable and must not be unduly discriminatory or confer any undue
preference upon any shipper.&#160;&#160;FERC regulations require that interstate
oil pipeline transportation rates and terms of service be filed with the FERC
and posted publicly.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The ICA
permits interested persons to challenge proposed new or changed rates or rules
and authorizes the FERC to investigate such changes and to suspend their
effectiveness for a period of up to seven months.&#160;&#160;If, upon completion
of an investigation, the FERC finds that the new or changed rate is unlawful, it
may require the carrier to refund the revenues together with interest in excess
of the prior tariff during the term of the investigation.&#160;&#160;The FERC
may also investigate, upon complaint or on its own motion, rates and related
rules that are already in effect and may order a carrier to change them
prospectively.&#160;&#160;Upon an appropriate showing, a shipper may obtain
reparations for damages sustained for a period of up to two years prior to the
filing of its complaint.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Energy Policy Act deems just and reasonable (i.e., deems &#8220;grandfathered&#8221;)
liquids pipeline rates that (i) were in effect for the 12 months preceding
enactment and (ii) that had not been subject to complaint, protest or
investigation.&#160;&#160;Some, but not all, of our interstate liquids pipeline
rates are considered grandfathered under the Energy Policy
Act.&#160;&#160;Certain other rates for our interstate liquids pipeline services
are charged pursuant to a FERC-approved indexing methodology, which allows a
pipeline to charge rates up to a prescribed ceiling that changes annually based
on the change from year-to-year in the Producer Price Index for finished goods
(&#8220;PPI&#8221;).&#160;&#160;A rate increase within the indexed rate ceiling is presumed
to be just and reasonable unless a protesting party can demonstrate that the
rate increase is substantially in excess of the pipeline&#8217;s
costs.&#160;&#160;Effective March 21, 2006, the FERC concluded that for the
five-year period commencing July 1, 2006, liquids pipelines charging indexed
rates may adjust their indexed ceilings annually by the PPI plus
1.3%.&#160;&#160;Prior to the end of that five year period, the FERC will once
again review the PPI to determine whether it continues to measure adequately the
cost changes in the liquids pipeline industry.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As an
alternative to using the indexing methodology, interstate liquids pipelines may
elect to support rate filings by using a cost-of-service methodology,
competitive market showings (&#8220;Market-Based Rates&#8221;) or agreements with all of the
pipeline&#8217;s shippers that the rate is acceptable.&#160;&#160;Our Products
Pipeline System has been granted permission by the FERC to utilize Market-Based
Rates for all of its refined products movements other than the Little Rock,
Arkansas, and the Arcadia destination within the Shreveport-Arcadia, Louisiana
destination markets, which are currently subject to the PPI.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Due to
the complexity of ratemaking, the lawfulness of any rate is never
assured.&#160;&#160;Prescribed rate methodologies for approving regulated tariff
rates may limit our ability to set rates based on our actual costs or may delay
the use of rates reflecting higher costs.&#160;&#160;Changes in the FERC&#8217;s
methodology for approving rates could adversely affect us.&#160;&#160;In
addition, challenges to our tariff rates could be filed with the FERC and
decisions by the FERC in approving our regulated rates could adversely affect
our cash flow.&#160;&#160;We believe the transportation rates currently charged
by our interstate common carrier liquids pipelines are</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Lou-Tex Propylene and Sabine Propylene pipelines are interstate common carrier
pipelines regulated under the ICA by the Surface Transportation Board
(&#8220;STB&#8221;).&#160;&#160;If the STB finds that a carrier&#8217;s rates are not just and
reasonable or are unduly discriminatory or preferential, it may prescribe a
reasonable rate.&#160;&#160;In determining a reasonable rate, the STB will
consider, among other factors, the effect of the rate on the volumes transported
by that carrier, the carrier&#8217;s revenue needs and the availability of other
economic transportation alternatives.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The STB
does not need to provide rate relief unless shippers lack effective competitive
alternatives.&#160;&#160;If the STB determines that effective competitive
alternatives are not available and a pipeline holds market power, then we may be
required to show that our rates are reasonable.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Natural
Gas Pipelines</font>. Our interstate natural gas pipelines and storage
facilities that provide services in interstate commerce are regulated by the
FERC under the Natural Gas Act of 1938 (&#8220;NGA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Under the NGA, the
rates for service on these interstate facilities must be just and reasonable and
not unduly discriminatory.&#160;&#160;We operate these interstate facilities
pursuant to tariffs which set forth rates and terms and conditions of
service.&#160;&#160;These tariffs must be filed with and approved by the FERC
pursuant to its regulations and orders.&#160;&#160;Our tariff rates may be
lowered on a prospective basis only by the FERC if it finds, on its own
initiative or as a result of challenges to the rates by third parties, that they
are unjust, unreasonable or otherwise unlawful.&#160;&#160;Unless the FERC
grants specific authority to charge market-based rates, our rates are derived
and charged based on a cost-of-service methodology.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
FERC&#8217;s authority over companies that provide natural gas pipeline transportation
or storage services in interstate commerce also includes: (i) certification,
construction, and operation of certain new facilities; (ii) the acquisition,
extension, disposition or abandonment of such facilities; (iii) the maintenance
of accounts and records; (iv) the initiation, extension and termination of
regulated services and (v) various other matters.&#160;&#160;The FERC&#8217;s rules
require interstate pipelines and their affiliates to adhere to Standards
of</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Conduct
that, among other things, require that transportation employees function
independently of marketing employees.&#160;&#160;The Energy Policy Act of 2005
amended the NGA to add an anti-manipulation provision.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to

manipulation.&#160;&#160;A violation of these rules may subject us to civil

imposed by the FERC.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Energy Policy Act of 2005
amended the NGA and the Natural Gas Policy Act of 1978 (&#8220;NGPA&#8221;) to increase
civil and criminal penalties for any violation of the NGA, NGPA and any rules,
regulations or orders of the FERC up to $1.0 million per day per
violation.</font></div>

2009, we submitted to the FERC a general rate change application under Section 4

LLC.&#160;&#160;On April 23, 2009, the FERC issued an order accepting the rates

reached an agreement in principle that, if filed as a formal settlement and

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

Pipelines</font>. Our offshore natural gas gathering pipelines and crude oil
pipeline systems are subject to federal regulation under the Outer Continental
Shelf Lands Act, which requires that all pipelines operating on or across the
outer continental shelf provide nondiscriminatory transportation
service.</font></div>

Pipelines</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Liquids
Pipelines</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.
</font>Certain of our pipeline systems operate within a single state and provide
intrastate pipeline transportation services.&#160;&#160;These pipeline systems
are subject to various regulations and statutes mandated by state regulatory
authorities.&#160;&#160;Although the applicable state statutes and regulations
vary widely, they generally require that intrastate pipelines publish tariffs
setting forth all rates, rules and regulations applying to intrastate service,
and generally require that pipeline rates and practices be reasonable and
nondiscriminatory.&#160;&#160;Shippers may challenge our intrastate tariff rates
and practices on our pipelines.&#160;&#160;Our intrastate liquids pipelines are
subject to regulation in many states, including Alabama, Colorado, Illinois,
Kansas, Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, New Mexico, Oklahoma and
Texas.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Natural
Gas Pipelines</font>. Our intrastate natural gas pipelines are subject to
regulation in many states, including Alabama, Colorado, Louisiana, Mississippi,
New Mexico and Texas.&#160;&#160;Certain of our intrastate natural gas pipelines
are also subject to limited regulation by the FERC under the NGPA because they
provide transportation and storage service pursuant to Section 311 of the NGPA
and Part 284 of the FERC&#8217;s regulations.&#160;&#160;Under Section 311 of the
NGPA, an intrastate pipeline may transport gas on behalf of an interstate
pipeline company or any local distribution company served by an interstate
pipeline without becoming subject to the FERC&#8217;s jurisdiction under the
NGA.&#160;&#160;However, such a pipeline is required to provide these services
on an open and nondiscriminatory basis, and to make certain rate and other
filings and reports in compliance with the FERC&#8217;s regulations.&#160;&#160;The
rates for Section 311 services may be established by the FERC or the respective
state agency, but such rates may not exceed a fair and equitable
rate.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
September 2007, the FERC approved an uncontested settlement establishing our
maximum firm and interruptible transportation rates for NGPA Section 311 service
on the Enterprise Texas Pipeline.&#160;&#160;In June and July 2008, we filed to
amend our Statement of Operating Conditions (&#8220;SOC&#8221;) for our transportation and
storage services, respectively.&#160;&#160;In September 2008, we submitted to
the FERC a new proposed Section 311 rate for service on our Sherman Extension
pipeline.&#160;&#160;On November 23, 2009, we filed an uncontested settlement
agreement, which, if approved, would resolve the Sherman Extension rate
issues.&#160;&#160;The other issues related to the SOC are reserved under the
settlement agreement for a decision by the FERC based on the
pleadings.&#160;&#160;Under the settlement agreement that resulted from the
September 2007 proceeding, we are required to file another rate petition on or
before April 2010 to justify our current rates or establish new rates for the
NGPA Section 311 service on the remainder of the system.&#160;&#160;The FERC
has</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In July
2009, we filed with the FERC proposed changes to our SOC and to increase our
interruptible transportation rates for NGPA Section 311 service for the Acadian
and Cypress pipelines, which are part of our Acadian Gas System.&#160;&#160;On
December 8, 2009, the FERC issued an order extending its review period to
encourage settlement discussions.&#160;&#160;Settlement negotiations are
on-going.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Sales
of Natural Gas</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt"></font>We are engaged in natural gas marketing
activities.&#160;&#160;The resale of natural gas in interstate commerce is
subject to FERC jurisdiction.&#160;&#160;However, under current federal rules
the price at which we sell natural gas is not regulated insofar as the
interstate market is concerned and, for the most part, is not subject to state
regulation.&#160;&#160;Our affiliates that engage in natural gas marketing are
considered marketing affiliates of certain of our interstate natural gas
pipelines.&#160;&#160;The FERC&#8217;s rules require pipelines and their marketing
affiliates who sell natural gas in interstate commerce subject to the FERC&#8217;s
jurisdiction to adhere to standards of conduct that, among other things, require
that their transportation and marketing employees function independently of each
other.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the Energy Policy Act of 2005, the FERC has also
established rules prohibiting energy market manipulation.&#160;&#160;A violation
of these rules by us or our employees or agents may subject us to civil
penalties, suspension or loss of authorization to perform such sales,
disgorgement of unjust profits or other appropriate non-monetary remedies
imposed by the FERC.&#160;&#160;The Federal Trade Commission and the Commodity
Futures Trading Commission also have issued rules and regulations prohibiting
market manipulation.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The FERC
is continually proposing and implementing new rules and regulations affecting
segments of the natural gas industry.&#160;&#160;For example, the FERC has
adopted new market monitoring and annual reporting regulations which are
applicable to many intrastate pipelines and other entities that are otherwise
not subject to the FERC&#8217;s NGA jurisdiction.&#160;&#160;The FERC also has
established rules requiring certain non-interstate pipelines to post daily
scheduled volume information and design capacity for certain points, and has
also required the annual reporting of gas sales information, in order to
increase transparency in natural gas markets.&#160;&#160;Non-interstate service
providers, which include NGPA Section 311 service providers, are required to
begin posting the information by June 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the
ultimate impact of these regulatory changes on our natural gas marketing
activities; however, we believe that any new regulations will also be applied to
other natural gas marketers with whom we compete.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Marine
Operations</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Maritime
Law</font>.&#160;&#160;The operation of tow boats, barges and marine equipment
create maritime obligations involving property, personnel and cargo under
General Maritime Law.&#160;&#160;These obligations can create risks which are
varied and include, among other things, the risk of collision and allision,
which may precipitate claims for personal injury, cargo, contract, pollution,
third-party claims and property damages to vessels and
facilities.&#160;&#160;Routine towage operations can also create risk of
personal injury under the Jones Act and General Maritime Law, cargo claims
involving the quality of a product and delivery, terminal claims, contractual
claims and regulatory issues.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Jones
Act</font>.&#160;&#160;The Jones Act is a federal law that restricts maritime
transportation between locations in the United States to vessels built and
registered in the United States and owned and manned by United States
citizens.&#160;&#160;As a result of our marine transportation business
acquisition on February 1, 2008, we now engage in coastwise maritime
transportation between locations in the United States, and as such, we
are</font></div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">
          </div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">subject
to the provisions of the Jones Act.&#160;&#160;As a result, we are responsible
for monitoring the ownership of our subsidiary that engages in maritime
transportation and for taking any remedial action necessary to insure that no
violation of the Jones Act ownership restrictions occurs.&#160;&#160;The Jones
Act also requires that all United States-flag vessels be manned by United States
citizens.&#160;&#160;Foreign seamen generally receive lower wages and benefits
than those received by United States citizen seamen.&#160;&#160;This requirement
significantly increases operating costs of United States-flag vessel operations
compared to foreign-flag vessel operations.&#160;&#160;Certain foreign
governments subsidize their nations&#8217; shipyards.&#160;&#160;This results in lower
shipyard costs both for new vessels and repairs than those paid by United
States-flag vessel owners.&#160;&#160;The USCG and American Bureau of Shipping
(&#8220;ABS&#8221;) maintain the most stringent regime of vessel inspection in the world,
which tends to result in higher regulatory compliance costs for United
States-flag operators than for owners of vessels registered under foreign flags
of convenience.&#160;&#160;Following Hurricane Katrina, and again after
Hurricane Rita, emergency suspensions of the Jones Act were effectuated by the
United States government.&#160;&#160;The last suspension ended on October 24,
2005.&#160;&#160;Future suspensions of the Jones Act or other similar actions
could adversely affect our cash flow.&#160;&#160;The Jones Act and General
Maritime Law also provide damage remedies for crew members injured in the
service of the vessel arising from employer negligence or vessel
unseaworthiness.&#160;&#160;In certain circumstances, a Jones Act seaman can
have dual employers under the borrowed servant doctrine.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Merchant
Marine Act of 1936</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>The Merchant
Marine Act of 1936 is a federal law that provides that, upon proclamation by the
president of the United States of a national emergency or a threat to the
national security, the United States Secretary of Transportation may requisition
or purchase any vessel or other watercraft owned by United States citizens
(including us, provided that we are considered a United States citizen for this
purpose).&#160;&#160;If one of our tow boats or barges were purchased or
requisitioned by the United States government under this law, we would be
entitled to be paid the fair market value of the vessel in the case of a
purchase or, in the case of a requisition, the fair market value of charter
hire.&#160;&#160;However, if one of our tow boats is requisitioned or purchased
and its associated barge or barges are left idle, we would not be entitled to
receive any compensation for the lost revenues resulting from the idled
barges.&#160;&#160;We also would not be entitled to be compensated for any
consequential damages we suffer as a result of the requisition or purchase of
any of our tow boats or barges.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
pipelines and other facilities are subject to multiple environmental obligations

Federal Water Pollution Control Act of 1972, renamed and amended as the Clean

quality, wastewater discharges and solid and hazardous waste

Emissions</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our operations are subject to the CAA
and comparable state laws and regulations.&#160;&#160;These laws and regulations
regulate emissions of air pollutants from various industrial sources, including
our facilities, and also impose various monitoring and reporting
requirements.&#160;&#160;Such laws and regulations may require that we obtain
pre-approval for the construction or modification of certain projects or
facilities expected to produce air emissions or result in the increase of
existing air emissions, obtain and strictly comply with air permits containing
various emissions and operational limitations, or utilize specific emission
control technologies to limit emissions.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our permits and related compliance
under the CAA, as well as recent or soon to be adopted changes to state
implementation plans for controlling air emissions in regional, non-attainment
areas, may require our operations to incur future capital expenditures in
connection with the addition or modification of existing air emission control
equipment and strategies.&#160;&#160;In addition, some of our facilities are
included within the categories of hazardous air pollutant sources, which are
subject to increasing regulation under the CAA.&#160;&#160;Our failure to comply
with these requirements could subject us to monetary penalties, injunctions,
conditions or restrictions on operations, and enforcement actions.&#160;&#160;We
may be required to incur certain capital expenditures in the future for air
pollution control equipment in connection with obtaining and maintaining
operating permits and approvals for air emissions.&#160;&#160;We believe,
however, that such requirements will not have a material adverse effect on our
operations, and the requirements are not expected to be any more burdensome to
us than any other similarly situated company.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
response to certain scientific studies suggesting that emissions of certain
gases, commonly referred to as &#8220;greenhouse gases&#8221; and including carbon dioxide
and methane, are contributing to the warming of the Earth&#8217;s atmosphere and other
climatic changes, the U.S. Congress has been actively considering legislation to
reduce such emissions.&#160;&#160;On June 26, 2009, the U.S. House of
Representatives passed the American Clean Energy and Security Act of 2009
(&#8220;ACESA&#8221;), which would establish an economy-wide cap-and-trade program intended
to reduce U.S. emissions of &#8220;greenhouse gases&#8221; including carbon dioxide and
methane that may contribute to warming of the Earth&#8217;s atmosphere and other
climatic changes.&#160;&#160;ACESA would require a 17% reduction in greenhouse
gas emissions from 2005 levels by 2020 and just over an 80% reduction of such
emissions by 2050.&#160;&#160;Under this legislation, the Environmental
Protection Agency (&#8220;EPA&#8221;) would issue a capped and steadily declining number of
tradable emissions allowances to major sources of greenhouse gas emissions so
that such sources could continue to emit greenhouse gases into the
atmosphere.&#160;&#160;The costs of these allowances would be expected to
escalate significantly over time.&#160;&#160;The U.S. Senate has begun work on
its own legislation for restricting domestic greenhouse gas emissions and
President Obama has indicated his support of legislation to reduce greenhouse
gas emissions through an emission allowance system.&#160;&#160;Although it is
not possible at this time to predict when the Senate may act on climate change
legislation or how any bill passed by the Senate would be reconciled with ACESA,
any future federal laws or implementing regulations that may be adopted to
address greenhouse gas emissions could require us to incur increased operating
costs and could adversely affect demand for the natural gas or other hydrocarbon
products that we transport, store or otherwise handle in connection with our
midstream services.</font></div>

addition, on December 7, 2009, the EPA announced its finding that emissions of
greenhouse gases presented an endangerment to human health and the
environment.&#160;&#160;These findings by the EPA allow the agency to proceed
with the adoption and implementation of regulations that would restrict
emissions of</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

could require us to incur costs to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases
associated with our operations or could adversely affect demand for the crude
oil, natural gas or other hydrocarbon products that we transport, store or

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
potential increase in the costs of our operations could include costs to operate
and maintain our facilities, install new emission controls on our facilities,
acquire allowances to authorize our greenhouse gas emissions, pay any taxes
related to our greenhouse gas emissions and administer and manage a greenhouse
