    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Corporate
Governance</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We are committed to sound principles of
governance.&#160;&#160;Such principles are critical for us to achieve our
performance goals and maintain the trust and confidence of investors, employees,
suppliers, business partners and stakeholders.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>A key element for strong governance is
independent members of the Board.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the NYSE listing
standards, a director will be considered independent if the Board determines
that he or she does not have a material relationship with EPE Holdings or us
(either directly or as a partner, unitholder or officer of an organization that
has a material relationship with EPE Holdings or us).&#160;&#160;Based on the
foregoing, the Board has affirmatively determined that Charles E. McMahen, Edwin
E. Smith, and Thurmon M. Andress are &#8220;independent&#8221; directors under the NYSE
rules.&#160;&#160;In making its determination, the Board&#8217;s consideration
included the fact that Mr. Andress&#8217; grandson is an employee of
EPCO.&#160;&#160;Mr. Andress&#8217; grandson does not live with Mr. Andress and is not
an executive officer of EPCO or any affiliate thereof.&#160;&#160;The amount of
compensation paid to Mr. Andress&#8217; grandson in 2009 in consideration for his
services to EPCO and its affiliates did not exceed $120,000.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Code
of Conduct and Ethics and Corporate Governance Guidelines</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>EPE Holdings has adopted a &#8220;Code of
Conduct&#8221; that applies to its directors, officers and employees.&#160;&#160;This
code sets out our requirements for compliance with legal and ethical standards
in the conduct of our business, including general business principles, legal and
ethical obligations, compliance policies for specific subjects, obtaining
guidance, the reporting of compliance issues and discipline for violations of
the code. The Code of Conduct also establishes policies applicable to our chief
executive officer, chief financial officer, principal accounting officer and
senior financial and other managers to prevent wrongdoing and to promote honest
and ethical conduct, including ethical handling of actual and apparent conflicts
of interest, compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, full, fair,
accurate, timely and understandable disclosure in public communications and
prompt internal reporting of violations of the code (and thus accountability for
adherence to the code).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Governance guidelines, together with
applicable committee charters, provide the framework for effective
governance.&#160;&#160;The Board has adopted the &#8220;Governance Guidelines of
Enterprise GP Holdings,&#8221; which address several matters, including qualifications
for directors, responsibilities of directors, retirement of directors, the
composition and responsibilities of the ACG Committee, the conduct and frequency
of Board and committee meetings, management succession plans, director access to
management and outside advisors, director compensation, director and executive
officer equity ownership, director orientation and continuing education, and
annual self-evaluation of the Board.&#160;&#160;The Board recognizes that
effective governance is an on-going process, and thus, it will review the
Governance Guidelines of Enterprise GP Holdings annually or more often as deemed
necessary.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
provide investors access to current information relating to our governance
procedures and principles, including the Code of Ethical Conduct for Senior
Financial Officers and Managers, the Governance Guidelines of Enterprise GP
Holdings and other matters, through our Internet website, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.enterprisegp.com</font>.&#160;&#160;You
may also contact our Investor Relations department at (866) 230-0745 for printed
copies of these documents free of charge.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ACG
Committee</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The sole committee of the Board is its
ACG Committee.&#160;&#160;In accordance with NYSE rules and Section 3(a)(58)(A)
of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Board has named three of its members
to serve on the ACG Committee.&#160;&#160;The members of the ACG Committee are
independent directors, free from any relationship with us or any of our
affiliates or subsidiaries that would interfere with the exercise of independent
judgment.</font></div><br>

approved by all of our partners and not a breach by EPE Holdings or the Board of
any duties it may owe us or our unitholders.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Pursuant to its formal written charter,
the ACG Committee has the authority to conduct any investigation appropriate to
fulfilling its responsibilities, and it has direct access to our independent
public accountants as well as any EPCO personnel whom it deems necessary in
fulfilling its responsibilities.&#160;&#160;The ACG Committee has the ability to
retain, at our expense, special legal, accounting or other consultants or
experts it deems necessary in the performance of its duties.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>From a governance standpoint, the
primary duties and responsibilities of the ACG Committee are to recommend to the
Board a set of governance principles applicable to us and review such guidelines
from time to time, making any changes that the ACG Committee deems
necessary.&#160;&#160;The ACG Committee assists the Board in fulfilling its
oversight responsibilities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A copy of
the ACG Committee charter is available on our Internet website, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.enterprisegp.com</font>.&#160;&#160;You
may also contact our Investor Relations department at (866) 230-0745 for a
printed copy of this document free of charge.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Executive
Sessions of Non-Management Directors</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Board holds regular executive
sessions in which non-management directors meet without any members of
management present.&#160;&#160;The purpose of these executive sessions is to
promote open and candid discussion among the non-management directors. During
such executive sessions, one director is designated as the &#8220;presiding director,&#8221;
who is responsible for leading and facilitating such executive
sessions.&#160;&#160;Currently, the presiding director is Mr.
McMahen.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
accordance with NYSE rules, we have established a toll-free, confidential
telephone hotline (the &#8220;Hotline&#8221;) so that interested parties may communicate
with the presiding director or with all the non-management directors as a
group.&#160;&#160;All calls to this Hotline are reported to the chairman of the
ACG Committee, who is responsible for communicating any necessary information to
the other non-management directors.&#160;&#160;The number of our confidential
Hotline is (877) 888-0002.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Dan L.
Duncan</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.</font> Mr.
Duncan was elected Chairman and a Director of EPGP in April 1998, Chairman and a
Director of the general partner (now the managing member) of EPO in December
2003, Chairman and a Director of EPE Holdings in August 2005 and Chairman and a
Director of DEP GP in October 2006.&#160;&#160;Mr. Duncan served as the sole
Chairman of EPCO from 1979 to December 2007.&#160;&#160;Mr. Duncan now serves as
Group Co-Chairman of EPCO with his daughter, Ms. Randa Duncan Williams, who is
also a Director of EPE Holdings.&#160;&#160;In December 2009, Mr. Duncan was
appointed as a Director of LE GP, the general partner of Energy Transfer
Equity.&#160;&#160;He also serves as an Honorary Trustee of the Board of
Trustees of the Texas Heart Institute at Saint Luke&#8217;s Episcopal Hospital and on
the Board of Trustees of the Baylor College of Medicine.</font></div><br>

contract and merger and acquisitions and, for over the last ten years, as a

Williams, legal and community involvement with numerous charitable
organizations, and active involvement in EPCO&#8217;s businesses, including ownership
and management of Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; businesses; for Mr. Andras, over
50 years of management and commercial roles in a number of midstream businesses,
including over 25 years as the former CEO of EPCO until 2003 and the initial CEO

Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; IPO until early 2005; for Mr. Creel, over 30 years

Enterprise Products Partners, including finance and accounting (certified public

16(a) Beneficial Ownership Reporting Compliance</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Under federal securities laws, EPE

officers, and any persons holding more than 10% of the Parent Company&#8217;s Units

their beneficial ownership levels to the Parent Company and the
SEC.&#160;&#160;Specific due dates for these reports have been established by
regulation, and the Parent Company is required to disclose in this annual report

timeframes.&#160;&#160;All such reporting was done in a timely manner in 2009,

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We do not directly employ any of the
persons responsible for managing our partnership. Instead, we are managed by our
general partner, the executive officers of which are employees of EPCO, a
privately held company controlled by Dan L. Duncan.&#160;&#160;Our management,
administrative and operating functions are primarily performed by employees of
EPCO pursuant to the ASA.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the ASA, we reimburse EPCO for
100% of EPCO&#8217;s compensation costs related to our partnership.&#160;&#160;For
additional information regarding the ASA, see Note 15 of the Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements included under Item 8 of this annual
report.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>With respect to our named executive
officers, compensation paid or awarded by us for the last three fiscal years
reflects only that portion of compensation paid by EPCO allocated to us pursuant
to the ASA, including an allocation of a portion of the cost of equity-based
long-term incentive plans of EPCO.&#160;&#160;Dan L. Duncan controls EPCO and
has ultimate decision-making authority with respect to the compensation of our
named executive officers.&#160;&#160;The following elements of compensation, and
EPCO&#8217;s decisions with respect to determination of payments, are not subject to
approvals by the Board or the ACG Committee of our general
partner.&#160;&#160;Equity awards under EPCO&#8217;s long-term incentive plans are
approved by the ACG Committee of the respective issuer.&#160;&#160;We do not
have a separate compensation committee.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>As discussed below, the elements of
EPCO&#8217;s compensation program, along with EPCO&#8217;s other rewards (e.g., benefits,
work environment and career development), are intended to provide a total
rewards package to employees.&#160;&#160;The objectives of EPCO&#8217;s compensation
program are to provide competitive compensation opportunities that will align
and drive employee performance toward the creation of sustained long-term
unitholder value.&#160;&#160;Our compensation program allows us to attract,
motivate and retain high quality talent with the skills and competencies we
require.&#160;&#160;The compensation package is designed to reward contributions
by employees in support of the business strategies of EPCO and its affiliates at
both the partnership and individual levels.&#160;&#160;With respect to the three
years ended December 31, 2009, EPCO&#8217;s compensation package for named executive
officers did not include any elements based on targeted performance-related
criteria.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div><br>

compensation program are a combination of annual cash and long-term equity-based
incentive compensation.&#160;&#160;For the three years ended December 31, 2009,
the elements of compensation for the named executive officers consisted of the
following:</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In order
to assist Mr. Duncan and EPCO with compensation decisions, Mr. Creel and Dr.
Cunningham (both Group Vice Chairmen for EPCO) and the senior vice president of
Human Resources for EPCO formulate preliminary compensation recommendations for
each of the named executive officers other than our CEO.&#160;&#160;Mr. Duncan,
after consulting with the senior vice president of Human Resources for EPCO,
independently makes compensation decisions with respect to the named executive
officers.&#160;&#160;In making these compensation decisions, EPCO considers
market data for determining relevant compensation levels and compensation
program elements through the review of and, in certain cases, participation in,
relevant compensation surveys and reports.&#160;&#160;These surveys and reports
are conducted and prepared by a third-party compensation
consultant.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Periodically, EPCO will engage a
third-party consultant to review compensation elements provided to our executive
officers.&#160;&#160;In 2009, EPCO engaged Hewitt &amp; Associates (&#8220;Hewitt&#8221;) to
review executive compensation relative to our industry.&#160;&#160;Hewitt
provided comparative market data on compensation practices and programs for
executive level positions based on an analysis of industry competitors and
external trends.&#160;&#160;Neither we, nor EPCO, which engages the consultant,
are aware of the identity of the companies whose data was used from the
consultant&#8217;s proprietary data base for specific positions.&#160;&#160;EPCO uses
the information provided in the Hewitt analysis to gauge whether compensation
levels reported by the consultant are within the general ranges of compensation
for EPCO employees in similar positions, but that comparison is only a factor
taken into consideration and may or may not impact compensation of our executive
officers, for which Dan L. Duncan has the ultimate decision-making
authority.&#160;&#160;EPCO does not otherwise engage in benchmarking for the
named executive officers&#8217; positions.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Mr. Duncan and EPCO do not use any
formula or specific performance-based criteria for our named executive officers
in connection with determining compensation for services performed for us;
rather, Mr. Duncan and EPCO determine an appropriate level and mix of
compensation on a case-by-case basis.&#160;&#160;Further, there is no
established policy or target for the allocation between either cash and non-cash
or short-term and long-term incentive compensation.&#160;&#160;However, some
considerations that Mr. Duncan may take into account in making the case-by-case
compensation determinations include total value of all elements of compensation
and the appropriate balance of internal pay equity among executive
officers.&#160;&#160;Mr. Duncan and EPCO also consider individual performance,
levels of responsibility and value to the organization.&#160;&#160;All
compensation determinations are discretionary and, as noted above, subject to
Mr. Duncan&#8217;s ultimate decision-making authority, except for equity awards under
EPCO&#8217;s long-term incentive plans, as discussed below.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We believe the absence of specific
performance-based criteria associated with our cash compensation and equity
awards, and the long-term nature of our equity awards, has the effect of
discouraging excessive risk taking by our executive officers in order to reach
certain targets.&#160;&#160;Further, the practice of making compensation
decisions on a case-by-case basis permits consideration of flexible criteria,
including current overall market conditions.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The discretionary cash bonus awards
paid to each of our named executive officers were determined by consultation, as
appropriate, among Mr. Duncan, Mr. Creel, Dr. Cunningham, Mr. Bachmann and the
senior vice president of Human Resources for EPCO, subject to Mr. Duncan&#8217;s final
determination.&#160;&#160;These cash bonus awards, in combination with annual
base salaries, are intended to yield</font></div><br>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

total cash compensation levels for the named executive officers and drive
performance in support of our business strategies, as well as the performance of
other EPCO affiliates for which the named executive officers perform
services.&#160;&#160;It is EPCO&#8217;s general policy to pay these awards in February
of the following year.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The awards granted under EPCO&#8217;s
long-term incentive plans to our named executive officers were determined by
consultation among Mr. Duncan, Mr. Creel and the senior vice president of Human
Resources for EPCO, and were approved by the ACG Committee of the respective
issuer.&#160;&#160;In addition, our named executive officers are Class B limited
partners in certain of the Employee Partnerships.&#160;&#160;Mr. Duncan approves
the issuance of all limited partnership interests in the Employee Partnerships
to our named executive officers.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Summary of Long-Term Incentive
Arrangements Underlying 2009 Award Grants&#8221; below for information regarding
EPCO&#8217;s long-term incentive plans.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>EPCO generally does not pay for
perquisites for any of our named executive officers, other than reimbursement of
certain parking expenses, and expects to continue its policy of covering limited
perquisites allocable to our named executive officers.&#160;&#160;EPCO also
makes matching contributions under its defined contribution plans for the
benefit of our named executive officers in the same manner as it does for other
EPCO employees.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>EPCO does not offer our named executive
officers a defined benefit pension plan.&#160;&#160;Also, none of our named
executive officers had nonqualified deferred compensation during the three years
ended December 31, 2009.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In December 2009, EPCO and the partners
of each of the Employee Partnerships amended the partnership agreement of each
of the Employee Partnerships to provide that the expected liquidation date for
such Employee Partnership will be in February 2016.&#160;&#160;The extensions of
the expected liquidation dates were intended to align the interests of the
employee partners of the Employee Partnerships with the long-term interests of
EPCO and other unitholders in the relevant underlying publicly traded
partnerships, which also hold indirectly a significant ownership interest in
both us and our subsidiaries.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Also in December 2009, the Board
implemented certain equity ownership guidelines for directors and executive
officers of our general partner in order to further align their interests and
actions with the interests of our partnership and its
unitholders.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Security Ownership of Management&#8221; within Item 12 of
this annual report for additional information.&#160;&#160;Our compensation
practices for our named executive officers are not expected to be impacted by
this new policy.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We believe that each of the base
salary, cash bonus awards, and long-term incentive awards fit the overall
compensation objectives of us and of EPCO and are designed to avoid risks that
are likely to conflict with the partnership&#8217;s risk management
policies.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Summary
of Long-Term Incentive Arrangements Underlying 2009 Award Grants</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The following information summarizes
the principal types of awards granted to our named executive officers under
EPCO&#8217;s long-term incentive plans.&#160;&#160;These plans provide for incentive
awards to EPCO&#8217;s key employees who perform management, administrative or
operational functions for us or our affiliates.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Awards granted under the 1998 Plan may
be in the form of unit options, restricted units, phantom units, unit
appreciation rights (&#8220;UARs&#8221;) and distribution equivalent rights
(&#8220;DERs&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Awards granted under the 2008 Plan may be in the form of
unit options, restricted units, phantom units, UARs and DERs.&#160;&#160;As of
December 31, 2009, no phantom unit awards, UARs or associated DERs have been
granted under the EPCO plans to the named executive officers.&#160;&#160;No
awards with respect to the Parent Company&#8217;s Units or Enterprise Products
Partners common units have been granted in connection with these long-term
incentive plans.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>As additional long-term incentive
arrangements, EPCO granted its key employees who perform services on behalf of
us, EPCO and other affiliated companies &#8220;profits interests&#8221; in the Employee
Partnerships, which are privately held affiliates of EPCO.&#160;&#160;The
employees were issued Class B limited partner interests and admitted as Class B
limited partners in the Employee Partnerships without any capital
contributions.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Restricted
unit awards</font>. Restricted unit awards allow recipients to acquire common
units of Enterprise Products Partners (at no cost to the recipient) once a
defined vesting period expires, subject to customary forfeiture
provisions.&#160;&#160;For awards granted prior to 2010, the restrictions on
such awards generally lapse four years from the date of
grant.&#160;&#160;Beginning in 2010, new restricted unit grants will vest at a
rate of 25% per year beginning one year after the grant date.&#160;&#160;The
fair value of restricted units is based on the market price per unit of the
underlying security on the date of grant.&#160;&#160;Compensation expense is
recognized based on the grant date fair value, net of an allowance for estimated
forfeitures.&#160;&#160;Each recipient is also entitled to cash distributions
equal to the product of the number of restricted units outstanding for the
participant and the cash distribution per unit paid by the respective
issuer.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Unit
option awards</font>. Under the EPCO plans, non-qualified incentive options to
purchase a fixed number of common units of Enterprise Products Partners may be
granted to key employees of EPCO.&#160;&#160;When issued, the exercise price of
each option grant is equivalent to the market price of the underlying equity on
the date of grant.&#160;&#160;In general, options granted under the EPCO plans
have a vesting period of four years and remain exercisable for five to ten
years, as applicable, from the date of grant.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The fair value of each unit option is
estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option pricing model,
which incorporates various assumptions including expected life of the options,
risk-free interest rates, expected distribution yield on common units of
Enterprise Products Partners, and expected unit price volatility of common units
of Enterprise Products Partners.&#160;&#160;In general, our assumption of
expected life of the options represents the period of time that the options are
expected to be outstanding based on an analysis of historical option
activity.&#160;&#160;Our selection of the risk-free interest rate is based on
published yields for U.S. government securities with comparable
terms.&#160;&#160;The expected distribution yield and unit price volatility is
estimated based on several factors, which include an analysis of Enterprise
Products Partners&#8217; historical unit price volatility and distribution yield over
a period equal to the expected life of the option.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Profits
interests awards</font>. Profits interest awards entitle each holder to
participate in the expected long-term appreciation in value of the equity
securities owned by each Employee Partnership.&#160;&#160;The Employee
Partnerships in which the named executive officers participate own either units
of The Parent Company or Enterprise Products Partners or a combination of
both.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Each Employee Partnership has a single
Class A limited partner, which is a privately held indirect subsidiary of EPCO,
and a varying number of Class B limited partners.&#160;&#160;At formation, the
Class A limited partner either contributes cash or limited partner units it owns
to the Employee Partnership.&#160;&#160;If cash is</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">contributed,
the Employee Partnership uses these funds to acquire limited partner units on
the open market.&#160;&#160;In general, the Class A limited partner earns a
preferred return (either fixed or variable depending on the partnership
agreement) on its investment (&#8220;Capital Base&#8221;) in the Employee Partnership and
residual quarterly cash amounts, if any, are distributed to the Class B limited
partners.&#160;&#160;Upon liquidation, Employee Partnership assets having a fair
market value equal to the Class A limited partner&#8217;s Capital Base, plus any
preferred return for the period in which liquidation occurs, will be distributed
to the Class A limited partner.&#160;&#160;Any remaining assets will be
distributed to the Class B limited partner(s) as a residual profits
interest.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The estimated grant date fair values of
the profits interests awards were determined using a Black-Scholes option
pricing model and reflect adjustments for forfeitures, regrants and other
modifications.&#160;&#160;The profits interests awards are subject to
forfeiture.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Compensation
Committee Report</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We do not have a separate compensation
committee. In addition, we do not directly employ or compensate our named
executive officers. Rather, under the ASA, we reimburse EPCO for the
compensation of our executive officers.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, to the extent
that decisions are made regarding the compensation policies pursuant to which
our named executive officers are compensated, they are made by Mr. Duncan and
EPCO alone (except for equity awards, as previously noted), and not by our
Board.</font></div>

Ownership of Management</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
following sets forth certain information regarding the beneficial ownership of
the Parent Company&#8217;s Units and the common units of Enterprise Products Partners
and Duncan Energy Partners as of February 1, 2010 by (i) our named executive
officers; (ii) the current directors of EPE Holdings; and (iii) the current
directors and executive officers of EPE Holdings as a
group.&#160;&#160;Enterprise Products Partners is a consolidated subsidiary of
the Parent Company and Duncan Energy Partners is a consolidated subsidiary of
Enterprise Products Partners.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>All information with respect to
beneficial ownership has been furnished by the respective directors or
officers.&#160;&#160;Each person has sole voting and dispositive power over the
securities shown unless otherwise indicated below.&#160;&#160;The beneficial
ownership amounts of certain individuals include options to acquire common units
of Enterprise Products Partners that are exercisable within 60 days of the
filing date of this annual report.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Mr. Duncan owns 50.4% of the voting
stock of EPCO and, accordingly, exercises sole voting and dispositive power with
respect to the securities beneficially owned by affiliates of
EPCO.&#160;&#160;The remaining shares of EPCO capital stock are owned primarily
by trusts for the benefit of members of Mr. Duncan&#8217;s family.&#160;&#160;The
address of EPCO is 1100 Louisiana Street, 10<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">th</font>
Floor, Houston, Texas 77002.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Essentially
all of the ownership interests in the Parent Company and Enterprise Products
Partners that are owned or controlled by EPCO are pledged as security under the
credit facility of an EPCO affiliate.&#160;&#160;This credit facility contains
customary and other events of default relating to EPCO and certain of its
affiliates, including us.&#160;&#160;In the event of a default under this credit
facility, a change in control of us or Enterprise Products Partners could occur,
including a change in control of our respective general partners.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Borrowings under the EPE Revolver, Term
Loan A and Term Loan B are secured by the Parent Company&#8217;s ownership of (i)
20,242,179 common units of Enterprise Products Partners, (ii) 100% of the
membership interests in EPGP and (iii) 38,976,090 common units of Energy
Transfer Equity.&#160;&#160;See Note 12 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements included under Item 8 of this annual report for information regarding
our consolidated debt obligations.</font></div><br>

Ownership Guidelines</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
December 31, 2009, the ACG Committee recommended to the Board, and effective on
January 1, 2010, the Board adopted and approved, new equity ownership guidelines
for our general partner&#8217;s directors and executive officers in order to further
align their interests and actions with the interests of our general partner, us
and our unitholders.&#160;&#160;Under the new guidelines:</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div>

      non-management director of our general partner is required to own our
      Units having an aggregate value (as defined in the guidelines) of three
      times the dollar amount of such non-management director&#8217;s aggregate annual
      cash retainer for service on the Board paid for the most recently
      completed calendar year; and</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>

Authorized for Issuance Under Equity Compensation Plans</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
November 2005, the Parent Company filed a registration statement covering the
potential future issuance of up to 250,000 of its Units in connection with the
Enterprise Products Company 2005 EPE Long-Term Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2005
Plan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Units issued under this plan can be in the form of unit
options, restricted units, phantom units and UARs.&#160;&#160;With the exception
of the 90,000 UARs issued to independent directors of EPE Holdings, no other
awards have been issued under the 2005 Plan.&#160;&#160;EPE Holdings has the
option of issuing Units or making cash payments when the UARs
vest.&#160;&#160;The 2005 Plan is effective until the earlier of (i) all
available Units under the plan have been issued to participants, (ii) early
termination of the 2005 Plan by EPCO or (iii) the tenth anniversary of the 2005
Plan, which is August 2015.&#160;&#160;Compensation expense associated with
these awards is recognized by EPE Holdings, and not included in our consolidated
compensation expense.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Business

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 11.5pt"></font>The ASA also addresses potential
conflicts that may arise among the Parent Company (including EPE Holdings),
Enterprise Products Partners (including EPGP), Duncan Energy Partners (including
DEP GP), and the EPCO Group with respect to business opportunities with third
parties.&#160;&#160;The EPCO Group includes EPCO and its other affiliates, but
excludes the Parent Company, Enterprise Products Partners, Duncan Energy
Partners and their respective general partners.&#160;&#160;With respect to
potential conflicts regarding third-party business opportunities, the ASA
provides, among other things, that:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

              <td width="1183">
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If
      a business opportunity to acquire &#8220;equity securities&#8221; (as defined
      below)<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>is
      presented to the EPCO Group, or to the Parent Company (including EPE
      Holdings), Enterprise Products Partners (including EPGP), or Duncan Energy
      Partners (including DEP GP), then the Parent Company will have the first
      right to pursue such opportunity.&#160;&#160;The term &#8220;equity securities&#8221;
      is defined to include:</font></div>

      partner interests (or securities which have characteristics similar to

                      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
      Parent Company will be presumed to want to acquire the equity securities
      until such time as EPE Holdings advises the EPCO Group, EPGP and DEP GP
      that it has abandoned the pursuit of such business
      opportunity.&#160;&#160;In the event that the purchase price of the equity
      securities is reasonably likely to equal or exceed $100.0&#160;million,
      the decision to decline the acquisition will be made by the CEO of EPE
      Holdings after consultation with and subject to the approval of the ACG
      Committee of EPE Holdings.&#160;&#160;If the purchase price is reasonably
      likely to be less than $100.0 million, the CEO of EPE Holdings may make
      the determination to decline the acquisition without consulting the ACG
      Committee of EPE Holdings.</font></div>
                      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
                      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
      the event that the Parent Company abandons the acquisition and so notifies
      the EPCO Group, and EPGP and DEP GP, then Enterprise Products Partners
      will have the second right to pursue such
      acquisition.&#160;&#160;Enterprise Products Partners will be presumed to
      want to acquire the equity securities until such time as EPGP advises the
      EPCO Group and DEP GP that Enterprise Products Partners has abandoned the
      pursuit of such acquisition.&#160;&#160;In determining whether or not to
      pursue the acquisition, Enterprise Products Partners will follow the same
      procedures applicable to the Parent Company, as described above but
      utilizing EPGP&#8217;s CEO and ACG Committee.</font></div>
                      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
                      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
      its sole discretion, Enterprise Products Partners may affirmatively direct
      such acquisition opportunity to Duncan Energy Partners.&#160;&#160;In the
      event this occurs, Duncan Energy Partners may pursue such
      acquisition.</font></div>
                    </div>

      any business opportunity not covered by the preceding bullet point (i.e.,
      not involving equity securities) is presented to the EPCO Group, or to the
      Parent Company (including EPE Holdings), Enterprise Products Partners
      (including EPGP), or Duncan Energy Partners (including DEP GP), Enterprise
      Products Partners will have the first right to pursue such opportunity
      either for itself or, if desired by Enterprise Products Partners in its
      sole discretion, for the benefit of Duncan Energy Partners.&#160;&#160;It
      will be presumed that Enterprise Products Partners will pursue the
      business opportunity until such time as its general partner advises the

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Partnership
Agreement Standards for ACG Committee Review</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Under our partnership agreement,
whenever a potential conflict of interest exists or arises between our general
partner or any of its affiliates and us, any of our subsidiaries or any partner,
any resolution or course of action by our general partner or its affiliates in
respect to such conflict of interest is permitted and deemed approved by all of
our partners, and will not constitute a breach of our partnership agreement or
any agreement contemplated by such agreement, or of any duty stated or implied
by law or equity, if the resolution or course of action is or, by operation of
the partnership agreement is deemed to be, fair and reasonable to us; provided
that, any conflict of interest and any resolution of such conflict of interest
will be conclusively deemed fair and reasonable to us if such conflict of
interest or resolution is (i)&#160;approved by a majority of the members of our
general partner&#8217;s ACG Committee (&#8220;Special Approval&#8221;) or (ii)&#160;on terms
objectively demonstrable to be no less favorable to us than those generally
being provided to or available from unrelated third parties.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The ACG Committee (in connection with
Special Approval) is authorized in connection with its resolution of any
conflict of interest to consider:</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div>

              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">the
      relative interests of any party to such conflict, agreement, transaction
      or situation and the benefits and burdens relating to such
      interest;</font></div>
            </td>

      other transactions that may be particularly favorable or advantageous to

contained in the partnership agreement requires the ACG Committee to consider

absence of bad faith by the ACG Committee or our general partner, the
resolution, action or terms so made, taken or provided (including granting
Special Approval) by the ACG Committee or our general partner with respect to
such matter are conclusive and binding on all persons (including all of our
partners) and do not constitute a breach of the partnership agreement, or any
other agreement contemplated thereby, or a breach of any standard of care or
duty imposed in the partnership agreement or under the Delaware Revised Uniform
Limited Partnership Act or any other law, rule or regulation.&#160;&#160;The
partnership agreement provides that it is presumed that the resolution, action
or terms made, taken or provided by the ACG Committee or our general partner
were not made, taken or provided in bad faith, and in any proceeding brought by
any limited partner or by or on behalf of such limited partner or any other
limited partner or us challenging such resolution, action or terms, the person
bringing or prosecuting such proceeding will have the burden of overcoming such
presumption.</font></div>

standards applicable to the Board and factors considered by the Board in making
its independence determinations, please refer to &#8220;Corporate Governance&#8221; and &#8220;ACG
Committee&#8221; under Item 10 of this annual report.</font></div>

            <td colspan="8" valign="bottom" style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(1)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Audit
      fees represent amounts billed for each of the years presented for
      professional services rendered in connection with (i) the audit of our
      annual financial statements and internal controls over financial
      reporting, (ii) the review of our quarterly financial statements or (iii)
      those services normally provided in connection with statutory and
      regulatory filings or engagements including comfort letters, consents and
      other services related to SEC matters.&#160;This information is presented
      as of the latest practicable date for this annual report.</font></div>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(2)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Audit-related
      fees represent amounts we were billed in each of the years presented for
      assurance and related services that are reasonably related to the
      performance of the annual audit or quarterly reviews.&#160;This category
      primarily includes services relating to internal control assessments and
      accounting-related consulting.</font></div>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(3)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Tax
      fees represent amounts we were billed in each of the years presented for
      professional services rendered in connection with tax compliance, tax
      advice, and tax planning.&#160;This category primarily includes services
      relating to the preparation of unitholder annual K-1 statements and
      partnership tax planning.&#160;In 2008, PricewaterhouseCoopers
      International Limited was engaged to perform the majority of our tax
      related services.</font></div>
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(4)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">All
      other fees represent amounts we were billed in each of the years presented
      for services not classifiable under the other categories listed in the
      table above.&#160;No such services were rendered by Deloitte &amp; Touche
      during the last two years.</font></div>
            </td>
            <td nowrap valign="bottom" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The ACG
Committee of our general partner has approved the use of Deloitte &amp; Touche
as our independent principal accountant.&#160;&#160;In connection with its
oversight responsibilities, the ACG Committee has adopted a pre-approval policy
regarding any services proposed to be performed by Deloitte &amp;
Touche.&#160;&#160;The pre-approval policy includes four primary service
categories: Audit, Audit-related, Tax and Other.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
general, as services are required, management and Deloitte &amp; Touche submit a
detailed proposal to the ACG Committee discussing the reasons for the request,
the scope of work to be performed, and an estimate of the fee to be charged by
Deloitte &amp; Touche for such work.&#160;&#160;The ACG Committee discusses the
request with management and Deloitte &amp; Touche, and if the work is deemed
necessary and appropriate for Deloitte &amp; Touche to perform, approves the
request subject to the fee amount presented (the initial &#8220;pre-approved&#8221; fee
amount).&#160;&#160;As part of these discussions, the ACG Committee must
determine whether or not the proposed services are permitted under the rules and
regulations concerning auditor independence under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002
as well as rules of the American Institute of Certified Public
Accountants.&#160;&#160;If at a later date, it appears that the initial
pre-approved fee amount may be insufficient to complete the work, then
management and Deloitte &amp; Touche must present a request to the ACG Committee
to increase the approved amount and the reasons for the increase.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under the
pre-approval policy, management cannot act upon its own to authorize an
expenditure for services outside of the pre-approved amounts.&#160;&#160;On a
quarterly basis, the ACG Committee is provided a schedule showing Deloitte &amp;
Touche&#8217;s pre-approved amounts compared to actual fees billed for each of the
primary service categories.&#160;&#160;The ACG Committee's pre-approval process
helps to ensure the independence of our principal accountant from
management.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In order
for Deloitte &amp; Touche to maintain its independence, we are prohibited from
using them to perform general bookkeeping, management or human resource
functions, and any other service not permitted by the Public Company Accounting
Oversight Board.&#160;&#160;The ACG Committee&#8217;s pre-approval policy also
precludes Deloitte &amp; Touche from performing any of these services for
us.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We have audited the accompanying
consolidated balance sheets of Enterprise GP Holdings L.P. and subsidiaries (the
&#8220;Company&#8221;) as of December 31, 2009 and 2008, and the related statements of
consolidated operations, comprehensive income, cash flows, and equity for each
of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;These
financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#8217;s
management.&#160;&#160;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the
financial statements based on our audits.&#160;&#160;We did not audit the
financial statements of Energy Transfer Equity L.P., an investment of the
Company, which is accounted for by the use of the equity method.&#160;&#160;The
Company&#8217;s equity in Energy Transfer Equity L.P.&#8217;s net income of $77.7 million
and $65.6 million (with both amounts prior to the Company&#8217;s excess cost
amortization &#8211; see Note 9) for the years ended December 31, 2009 and 2008,
respectively,&#160;is included in the accompanying consolidated financial
statements.&#160;&#160;Energy Transfer Equity L.P.&#8217;s financial statements were
audited by other auditors whose report has been furnished to us, and our
opinion, insofar as it relates to the amounts included for Energy Transfer
Equity L.P., is based solely on the report of the other auditors.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We conducted our audits in accordance
with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United
States).&#160;&#160;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit
to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free
of material misstatement.&#160;&#160;An audit includes examining, on a test
basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial
statements.&#160;&#160;An audit also includes assessing the accounting
principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as
evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.&#160;&#160;We believe
that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In our opinion, such consolidated
financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial
position of Enterprise GP Holdings L.P. and subsidiaries at December 31, 2009
and 2008, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of
the three years in the period ended December 31, 2009, in conformity with
accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of
America.</font></div>

also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting
Oversight Board (United States), the Company's internal control over financial
reporting as of December 31, 2009, based on the criteria established in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Internal Control&#8212;Integrated

    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">the
midstream energy industry and related businesses.&#160;&#160;Our goal is to
increase cash distributions to unitholders.&#160;&#160;The Parent Company is
owned 99.99% by its limited partners and 0.01% by its general partner, EPE
Holdings.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Basis
of Presentation</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
consolidated financial statements and business segments were recast in
connection with the TEPPCO Merger. On October 26, 2009, the related mergers of
wholly owned subsidiaries of Enterprise Products Partners with TEPPCO and TEPPCO
GP were completed.&#160;&#160;Under terms of the merger agreements, TEPPCO and
TEPPCO GP became wholly owned subsidiaries of Enterprise Products Partners, and
each of TEPPCO&#8217;s unitholders, except for a privately held affiliate of EPCO,
were entitled to receive 1.24 common units of Enterprise Products Partners for
each TEPPCO unit.&#160;&#160;In total, Enterprise Products Partners issued an
aggregate of 126,932,318 common units and 4,520,431 Class B units (described
below) as consideration in the TEPPCO Merger for both TEPPCO units and the
TEPPCO GP membership interests.&#160;&#160;TEPPCO&#8217;s units, which had been
trading on the NYSE under the ticker symbol &#8220;TPP,&#8221; have been delisted and are no
longer publicly traded.&#160;&#160;On October 27, 2009, the TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP
equity interests were contributed by Enterprise Products Partners to EPO, and
TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP became wholly owned subsidiaries of EPO.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A
privately held affiliate of EPCO exchanged a portion of its TEPPCO units, based
on the 1.24 exchange rate, for 4,520,431 Class B units of Enterprise Products
Partners in lieu of common units.&#160;&#160;The Class B units are not entitled
to regular quarterly cash distributions for the first sixteen quarters following
the closing date of the merger.&#160;&#160;The Class B units automatically
convert into the same number of common units on the date immediately following
the payment date for the sixteenth quarterly distribution following the closing
date of the merger.&#160;&#160;The Class B units are entitled to vote together
with the common units as a single class on partnership matters and, except for
the payment of distributions, have the same rights and privileges as Enterprise
Products Partners&#8217; common units.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under the
terms of the TEPPCO Merger agreements, the Parent Company received 1,331,681
common units of Enterprise Products Partners and an increase in the capital
account of EPGP to maintain its 2% general partner interest in Enterprise
Products Partners as consideration for 100% of the membership interests of
TEPPCO GP.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Since
Enterprise Products Partners, TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP are under common control of
EPCO and its affiliates, the TEPPCO Merger was accounted for at historical costs
as a reorganization of entities under common control in a manner similar to a
pooling of interests.&#160;&#160;The inclusion of TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP in our
consolidated financial statements was effective January 1, 2005 since an
affiliate of EPCO under common control with Enterprise Products Partners
originally acquired ownership interests in TEPPCO GP in February
2005.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
consolidated financial statements prior to the TEPPCO Merger reflect the
combined financial information of Enterprise Products Partners, TEPPCO and
TEPPCO GP on a 100% basis.&#160;&#160;Third-party and related party ownership
interests in TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP are reflected as &#8220;Former owners of TEPPCO,&#8221; a
component of noncontrolling interest.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
financial statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally
accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The financial statements of
TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP were prepared from the separate accounting records
maintained by TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP.&#160;&#160;All intercompany balances and
transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
revised our business segments and related disclosures to reflect the TEPPCO
Merger.&#160;&#160;Our reorganized business segments reflect the manner in which
these businesses are managed and reviewed by the chief executive officer of our
general partner.&#160;&#160;Under our new business segment structure, we have
six reportable business segments: (i) NGL Pipelines &amp; Services; (ii) Onshore
Natural Gas Pipelines &amp; Services; (iii) Onshore Crude Oil Pipelines &amp;
Services; (iv) Offshore Pipelines &amp; Services; (v) Petrochemical &amp;
Refined Products Services and (vi) Other Investments.</font></div>

    <div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">General
Purpose Consolidated and Parent Company-Only Information</font>.&#160;&#160;In
accordance with rules and regulations of the U.S Securities and Exchange
Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;) and various other accounting standard-setting organizations,
our general purpose financial statements reflect the consolidation of the
financial information of businesses that we control through the ownership of
general partner interests (e.g., Enterprise Products Partners).&#160;&#160;Our
general purpose consolidated financial statements present those investments in
which we do not have a controlling interest as unconsolidated affiliates (e.g.,
Energy Transfer Equity and LE GP).&#160;&#160;As presented in our consolidated
financial statements, noncontrolling interest reflects third-party and related
party ownership of our consolidated subsidiaries, which include the third-party
and related party unitholders of Enterprise Products Partners and Duncan Energy
Partners other than the Parent Company.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In order
for the unitholders of Enterprise GP Holdings L.P. and others to more fully
understand the Parent Company&#8217;s business and financial statements on a
standalone basis, Note 22 includes information devoted exclusively to the Parent
Company apart from that of our consolidated Partnership.&#160;&#160;A key
difference between the non-consolidated Parent Company financial information and
those of our consolidated Partnership is that the Parent Company views each of
its investments (e.g., in Enterprise Products Partners and Energy Transfer
Equity) as unconsolidated affiliates and records its share of the net income of
each as equity income in the Parent Company income information.&#160;&#160;In
accordance with GAAP, we eliminate the equity income related to Enterprise
Products Partners in the preparation of our consolidated financial
statements.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Presentation
of Investments</font>.&#160;&#160;The Parent Company owns common units of
Enterprise Products Partners and 100% of the membership interests of EPGP, which
is entitled to 2% of the cash distributions paid by Enterprise Products Partners
as well as the associated incentive distribution rights (&#8220;IDRs&#8221;) of Enterprise
Products Partners.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009 and 2008, the Parent Company
owned 21,167,783 and 13,670,925 common units, respectively, of Enterprise
Products Partners.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Parent Company owns 38,976,090 common units of Energy Transfer
Equity.&#160;&#160;In addition, at December 31, 2009 and 2008, the Parent
Company owned approximately 40.6% and 34.9%, respectively, of the membership
interests of LE GP.&#160;&#160;Energy Transfer Equity owns limited partner
interests and the general partner interest of ETP.&#160;&#160;We account for our
investments in Energy Transfer Equity and LE GP using the equity method of
accounting.&#160;&#160;See Note 9 for additional information regarding these
unconsolidated affiliates.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In May
2007, private company affiliates of EPCO contributed equity interests in TEPPCO
and TEPPCO GP to the Parent Company.&#160;&#160;As a result of such
contributions, the Parent Company owned 4,400,000 units of TEPPCO and all of the
membership interests of TEPPCO GP, which was entitled to 2% of the cash
distributions of TEPPCO as well as the IDRs of TEPPCO.&#160;&#160;On October 26,
2009, the TEPPCO Merger was completed and TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP became wholly
owned subsidiaries of Enterprise Products Partners.&#160;&#160;As a result, the
Parent Company&#8217;s ownership interests in the TEPPCO units were converted to
5,456,000 common units of Enterprise Products Partners.&#160;&#160;In addition,
the Parent Company&#8217;s membership interests in TEPPCO GP were exchanged for (i)
1,331,681 common units of Enterprise Products Partners and (ii) EPGP (on behalf
of the Parent Company as a wholly owned subsidiary of the Parent Company) was
credited in its Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; capital account an amount to
maintain its 2% general partner interest in Enterprise Products
Partners.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="n2">Note 2.</a>&#160;&#160;Summary of Significant Accounting
Policies</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Allowance
for Doubtful Accounts</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
allowance for doubtful accounts is determined based on specific identification
and estimates of future uncollectible accounts.&#160;&#160;Our procedure for
determining the allowance for doubtful accounts is based on: (i) historical
experience with customers, (ii) the perceived financial stability of customers
based on our research and (iii) the levels of credit we grant to
customers.&#160;&#160;In addition, we may increase the allowance account in
response to the specific identification of customers involved in
bankruptcy</font></div><br>

              <td align="right" valign="bottom" width="1%" style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 2px"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>

              <td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>
