      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>See &#8220;Credit Risk Due to Industry
Concentrations&#8221; in Note 19 for additional information.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cash
and Cash Equivalents</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cash and
cash equivalents represent unrestricted cash on hand and highly liquid
investments with original maturities of less than three months from the date of
purchase.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Consolidation
Policy</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
consolidated financial statements include our accounts and those of our
majority-owned subsidiaries in which we have a controlling interest, after the
elimination of all intercompany accounts and transactions.&#160;&#160;We also
consolidate other entities and ventures in which we possess a controlling
financial interest as well as partnership interests where we are the sole
general partner of the partnership.&#160;&#160;We evaluate our financial
interests in business enterprises to determine if they represent variable
interest entities where we are the primary beneficiary.&#160;&#160;If such
criteria are met, we consolidate the financial statements of such businesses
with those of our own.&#160;&#160;Third-party or affiliate ownership interests
in our controlled subsidiaries are presented as noncontrolling
interests.&#160;&#160;See Note 13 for information regarding noncontrolling
interest.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If the
entity is organized as a limited partnership or limited liability company and
maintains separate ownership accounts, we account for our investment using the
equity method if our ownership interest is between 3% and 50% and we exercise
significant influence over the entity&#8217;s operating and financial
policies.&#160;&#160;For all other types of investments, we apply the equity
method of accounting if our ownership interest is between 20% and 50% and we
exercise significant influence over the entity&#8217;s operating and financial
policies.&#160;&#160;In consolidation, we eliminate our proportionate share of
profits and losses from transactions with equity method unconsolidated
affiliates to the extent such amounts remain on our Consolidated Balance Sheets
(or those of our equity method investments) in inventory or similar
accounts.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If our
ownership interest in an entity does not provide us with either control or
significant influence we account for the investment using the cost
method.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Contingencies</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certain
conditions may exist as of the date our financial statements are issued, which
may result in a loss to us but which will only be resolved when one or more
future events occur or fail to occur.&#160;&#160;Our management and its legal
counsel assess such contingent liabilities, and such assessment inherently
involves an exercise in judgment.&#160;&#160;In assessing loss contingencies
related to legal proceedings that are pending against us or unasserted claims
that may result in proceedings, our management and legal counsel evaluate the
perceived merits of any legal proceedings or unasserted claims as well as the
perceived merits of the amount of relief sought or expected to be sought
therein.</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">

        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If the
assessment of a contingency indicates that it is probable that a material loss
has been incurred and the amount of liability can be estimated, then the
estimated liability would be accrued in our financial statements.&#160;&#160;If
the assessment indicates that a potentially material loss contingency is not
probable but is reasonably possible, or is probable but cannot be estimated,
then the nature of the contingent liability, together with an estimate of the
range of possible loss (if determinable and material), is
disclosed.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loss
contingencies considered remote are generally not disclosed unless they involve
guarantees, in which case the guarantees would be disclosed.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Current
Assets and Current Liabilities</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
present, as individual captions in our Consolidated Balance Sheets, all
components of current assets and current liabilities that exceed 5% of total
current assets and liabilities, respectively.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Deferred
Revenues</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Amounts
billed in advance of the period in which the service is rendered or product
delivered are recorded as deferred revenue.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009 and
2008, deferred revenues totaled $106.8 million and $118.5 million, respectively,
and were recorded as a component of other current and long-term liabilities, as
appropriate, on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;See Note 4 for
information regarding our revenue recognition policies.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Derivative
Instruments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We use
derivative instruments such as swaps, forwards and other contracts to manage
price risks associated with inventories, firm commitments, interest rates,
foreign currency and certain anticipated transactions.&#160;&#160;To qualify for
hedge accounting, the item to be hedged must expose us to risk and the related
derivative instrument must reduce that exposure and meet specific documentation
requirements.&#160;&#160;We formally designate a derivative instrument as a
hedge and document and assess the effectiveness of the hedge at inception and
thereafter on a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;We also apply the normal
purchases/normal sales exception for certain of our derivative instruments,
which precludes the recognition of changes in mark-to-market value for these
items on the balance sheet or income statement.&#160; Revenues and costs for
these transactions are recognized when volumes are physically delivered or
received.&#160;&#160;See Note 6 for additional information regarding our
derivative instruments and related hedging activities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Earnings
Per Unit</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Earnings
per unit (&#8220;EPU&#8221;) is based on the amount of income allocated to limited partners
and the weighted-average number of units outstanding during the
period.&#160;&#160;See Note 17 for additional information regarding our earnings
per unit.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Environmental
Costs</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Environmental
costs for remediation are accrued based on estimates of known remediation
requirements.&#160; Such accruals are based on management&#8217;s best estimate of the
ultimate cost to remediate a site and are adjusted as further information and
circumstances develop.&#160; Those estimates may change substantially depending
on information about the nature and extent of contamination, appropriate
remediation technologies and regulatory approvals.&#160; Expenditures to
mitigate or prevent future environmental contamination are capitalized.&#160;
Ongoing environmental compliance costs are charged to expense as incurred.&#160;
In accruing for environmental remediation liabilities, costs of future
expenditures for environmental remediation are not discounted to their present
value, unless the amount and timing of the expenditures are fixed or reliably
determinable.&#160; At December 31, 2009, none of our estimated environmental
remediation liabilities were discounted to present value since the ultimate
amount and timing of cash payments for such liabilities were not readily
determinable.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At
December 31, 2009 and 2008, $6.4 million and $5.3 million, respectively, of our
environmental reserves were classified as current liabilities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Equity
Awards</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">See Note
5 for information regarding our accounting for equity awards.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Estimates</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Preparing
our financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make
estimates and assumptions that affect amounts presented in the financial
statements (i.e. assets, liabilities, revenue and expenses) and disclosures
about contingent assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;Our actual results could
differ from these estimates.&#160;&#160;On an ongoing basis, management reviews
its estimates based on currently available information.&#160;&#160;Changes in
facts and circumstances may result in revised estimates.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Exchange
Contracts</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Exchanges
are contractual agreements for the movements of natural gas liquids (&#8220;NGLs&#8221;) and
certain petrochemical products between parties to satisfy timing and logistical
needs of the parties.&#160;&#160;Net exchange volumes borrowed from us under
such agreements are valued at market-based prices and included in accounts
receivable.&#160;&#160;Net exchange volumes loaned to us under such agreements
are valued at market-based prices and accrued as a liability in accrued product
payables.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Receivables and payables arising from
exchange transactions are settled with movements of products rather than with
cash.&#160;&#160;When payment or receipt of monetary consideration is required
for product differentials and service costs, such items are recognized in our
consolidated financial statements on a net basis.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Fair
Value Information</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cash and
cash equivalents and restricted cash, accounts receivable, accounts payable and
accrued expenses, and other current liabilities are carried at amounts which
reasonably approximate their fair values due to their short-term
nature.&#160;&#160;The estimated fair values of our fixed-rate debt are based on
quoted market prices for such debt or debt of similar terms and
maturities.&#160;&#160;The carrying amounts of our variable-rate debt
obligations reasonably approximate their fair values due to their variable
interest rates.&#160;&#160;See Note 6 for fair value information associated with
our derivative instruments.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Foreign
Currency Translation</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We own an
NGL marketing business located in Canada.&#160;&#160;The financial statements of
this foreign subsidiary are translated into U.S. dollars from the Canadian
dollar, which is the subsidiary&#8217;s functional currency, using the current rate
method.&#160;&#160;Its assets and liabilities are translated at the rate of
exchange in effect at the balance sheet date, while revenue and expense items
are translated at average rates of exchange during the reporting
period.&#160;&#160;Exchange gains and losses arising from foreign currency
translation adjustments are reflected as separate components of accumulated
other comprehensive loss (&#8220;AOCI&#8221;) in the accompanying Consolidated Balance
Sheets.&#160;&#160;Our net cash flows from this Canadian subsidiary may be
adversely affected by changes in foreign currency exchange rates.&#160;&#160;See
Note 6 for information regarding our foreign currency derivative
instruments.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Impairment
Testing for Goodwill</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
goodwill amounts are assessed for impairment (i) on a routine annual basis or
(ii) when impairment indicators are present.&#160;&#160;If such indicators occur
(e.g., the loss of a significant customer, economic obsolescence of plant
assets, etc.), the estimated fair value of the reporting unit to which the
goodwill is assigned is determined and compared to its book value.&#160;&#160;If
the fair value of the reporting unit exceeds its book value including associated
goodwill amounts, the goodwill is considered to be unimpaired and no impairment
charge is required.&#160;&#160;If the fair value of the reporting unit is less
than its book value including associated goodwill amounts, a charge to earnings
is recorded to reduce the carrying value of the goodwill to its implied fair
value.&#160;&#160;See Note 6 for information regarding impairment charges
related to goodwill during 2009.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Impairment
Testing for Long-Lived Assets</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Long-lived
assets (including intangible assets with finite useful lives and property, plant
and equipment) are reviewed for impairment when events or changes in
circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of such assets may not be
recoverable.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Long-lived
assets with carrying values that are not expected to be recovered through future
cash flows are written-down to their estimated fair values.&#160;&#160;The
carrying value of a long-lived asset is deemed not recoverable if it exceeds the
sum of undiscounted cash flows expected to result from the use and eventual
disposition of the asset.&#160;&#160;If the asset carrying value exceeds the sum
of its undiscounted cash flows, a non-cash asset impairment charge equal to the
excess of the asset&#8217;s carrying value over its estimated fair value is
recorded.&#160;&#160;Fair value is defined as the amount at which an asset or
liability could be bought or settled in an arm&#8217;s length
transaction.&#160;&#160;We measure fair value using market price indicators or,
in the absence of such data, appropriate valuation techniques.&#160;&#160;See
Note 6 for information regarding impairment charges related to long-lived assets
during 2009.</font></div>

      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Impairment
Testing for Unconsolidated Affiliates</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
evaluate our equity method investments for impairment when events or changes in
circumstances indicate that there is a loss in value of the investment
attributable to an other than temporary decline.&#160;&#160;Examples of such
events or changes in circumstances include continuing operating losses of the
entity and/or long-term negative changes in the entity&#8217;s industry.&#160;&#160;In
the event we determine that the loss in value of an investment is other than a
temporary decline, we record a charge to equity earnings to adjust the carrying
value of the investment to its estimated fair value.&#160;&#160;See Note 9 for
information regarding impairment charges related to our unconsolidated
affiliates during 2007.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Income
Taxes</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Provision
for income taxes is primarily applicable to our state tax obligations under the
Revised Texas Franchise Tax and certain federal and state tax obligations of
Seminole Pipeline Company (&#8220;Seminole&#8221;) and Dixie Pipeline Company (&#8220;Dixie&#8221;),
both of which are consolidated subsidiaries of ours.&#160;&#160;Deferred income
tax assets and liabilities are recognized for temporary differences between the
assets and liabilities of our tax paying entities for financial reporting and
tax purposes.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Since we
are structured as a pass-through entity, we are not subject to federal income
taxes.&#160;&#160;As a result, our partners are individually responsible for
paying federal income taxes on their share of our taxable
income.&#160;&#160;Since we do not have access to information regarding each
partner&#8217;s tax basis, we cannot readily determine the total difference in the
basis of our net assets for financial and tax reporting purposes.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We must
recognize the tax effects of any uncertain tax positions we may adopt, if the
position taken by us is more likely than not sustainable.&#160;&#160;If a tax
position meets such criteria, the tax effect to be recognized by us would be the
largest amount of benefit with more than a 50% chance of being realized upon
settlement.&#160;&#160;See Note 16 for additional information regarding our
income taxes.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Inventories</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Inventories
primarily consist of natural gas, NGLs, crude oil, refined products, lubrication
oils and certain petrochemical products that are valued at the lower of average
cost or market (&#8220;LCM&#8221;).&#160;&#160;We capitalize, as a cost of inventory,
shipping and handling charges associated with such purchase volumes, terminal
storage fees, vessel inspection costs, demurrage charges and other related
costs.&#160;&#160;As volumes are sold and delivered out of inventory, the cost
of these volumes (including freight-in charges that have been capitalized as
part of inventory cost) are charged to operating costs and
expenses.&#160;&#160;Shipping and handling fees associated with products we sell
and deliver to customers are charged to operating costs and expenses as
incurred.&#160;&#160;See Note 7 for additional information regarding our
inventories.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Natural
Gas Imbalances</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In the
natural gas pipeline transportation business, imbalances frequently result from
differences in natural gas volumes received from and delivered to our
customers.&#160;&#160;Such differences occur when a customer delivers more or
less gas into our pipelines than is physically redelivered back to them during a
particular time period.&#160;&#160;We have various fee-based agreements with
customers to transport their natural gas through our pipelines.&#160;&#160;Our
customers retain ownership of their natural gas shipped through our
pipelines.&#160;&#160;As such, our pipeline transportation activities are not
intended to create physical volume differences that would result in significant
accounting or economic events for either our customers or us during the course
of the arrangement.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We settle
pipeline gas imbalances through either (i) physical delivery of in-kind gas or
(ii) in cash.&#160;&#160;These settlements follow contractual guidelines or
common industry practices.&#160;&#160;As imbalances occur, they may be settled:
(i) on a monthly basis, (ii) at the end of the agreement or (iii) in accordance
with industry practice, including negotiated settlements.&#160;&#160;Certain of
our natural gas pipelines have a regulated tariff rate mechanism requiring
customer imbalance settlements each month at current market
prices.</font></div><br>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">However,
the vast majority of our settlements are through in-kind arrangements whereby
incremental volumes are delivered to or received from a
customer.&#160;&#160;Such in-kind deliveries are ongoing and take place over
several periods.&#160;&#160;In some cases, settlements of imbalances built up
over a period of time are ultimately cashed out and are generally negotiated at
values which approximate average market prices over a period of
time.&#160;&#160;For those gas imbalances that are ultimately settled over
future periods, we estimate the value of such current assets and liabilities
using average market prices, which we believe is representative of the value of
the imbalances upon final settlement.&#160;&#160;Changes in natural gas prices
may impact our estimates.</font></div>

            </tr><tr bgcolor="white">
              <td colspan="8" valign="bottom">
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(1)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Reflected
      as a component of &#8220;Accounts and notes receivable &#8211; trade&#8221; on our
      Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(2)&#160;&#160;
      </font></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Reflected
      as a component of &#8220;Accrued product payables&#8221; on our Consolidated Balance
      Sheets.</font></div>
              </td>
              <td nowrap valign="bottom" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>
            </tr></table>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Property,
Plant and Equipment</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Property,
plant and equipment is recorded at cost.&#160;&#160;Expenditures for additions,
improvements and other enhancements to property, plant and equipment are
capitalized and minor replacements, maintenance, and repairs that do not extend
asset life or add value are charged to expense as incurred.&#160;&#160;When
property, plant and equipment assets are retired or otherwise disposed of, the
related cost and accumulated depreciation is removed from the accounts and any
resulting gain or loss is included in the results of operations for the
respective period.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
general, depreciation is the systematic and rational allocation of an asset&#8217;s
cost, less its residual value (if any), to the periods it
benefits.&#160;&#160;The majority of our property, plant and equipment is
depreciated using the straight-line method, which results in depreciation
expense being incurred evenly over the life of the assets.&#160;&#160;Our
estimate of depreciation incorporates assumptions regarding the useful economic
lives and residual values of our assets.&#160;&#160;At the time we place our
assets in service, we believe such assumptions are reasonable.&#160;&#160;Under
our depreciation policy for midstream energy assets, the remaining economic
lives of such assets are limited to the estimated life of the natural resource
basins (based on proved reserves at the time of the analysis) from which such
assets derive their throughput or processing volumes.&#160;&#160;Our forecast of
the remaining life for the applicable resource basins is based on several
factors, including information published by the U.S. Energy Information
Administration.&#160;&#160;Where appropriate, we use other depreciation methods
(generally accelerated) for tax purposes.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Leasehold
improvements are recorded as a component of property, plant and
equipment.&#160;&#160;The cost of leasehold improvements is charged to earnings
using the straight-line method over the shorter of the remaining lease term or
the estimated useful lives of the improvements.&#160;&#160;We consider renewal
terms that are deemed reasonably assured when estimating remaining lease
terms.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our assumptions regarding the useful
economic lives and residual values of our assets may change in response to new
facts and circumstances, which would change our depreciation amounts
prospectively.&#160;&#160;Examples of such circumstances include, but are not
limited to: (i) changes in laws and regulations that limit the estimated
economic life of an asset; (ii)&#160;changes in technology that render an asset
obsolete; (iii)&#160;changes in expected salvage values; or (iv) significant
changes in the forecast life of proved reserves of applicable resource basins,
if any.&#160;&#160;See Note 8 for additional information regarding our property,
plant and equipment.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt"></font>Certain of our plant operations entail
periodic planned outages for major maintenance activities.&#160;&#160;These
planned shutdowns typically result in significant expenditures, which are
principally comprised of amounts paid to third parties for materials, contract
services and related items.&#160;&#160;We use the expense-as-</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">

        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">incurred
method for our planned major maintenance activities; however, the cost of annual
planned major maintenance projects are deferred and recognized ratably over the
remaining portion of the calendar year in which such projects
occur.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Asset retirement obligations (&#8220;AROs&#8221;)
are legal obligations associated with the retirement of tangible long-lived
assets that result from their acquisition, construction, development and/or
normal operation.&#160;&#160;When an ARO is incurred, we record a liability for
the ARO and capitalize an equal amount as an increase in the carrying value of
the related long-lived asset.&#160;&#160;Over time, the liability is accreted to
its present value (accretion expense) and the capitalized amount is depreciated
over the remaining useful life of the related long-lived asset.&#160;&#160;We
will incur a gain or loss to the extent that our ARO liabilities are not settled
at their recorded amounts.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Restricted
Cash</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Restricted
cash represents amounts held in connection with our commodity derivative
instruments portfolio and related physical natural gas and NGL
purchases.&#160;&#160;Additional cash may be restricted to maintain this
portfolio as commodity prices fluctuate or deposit requirements
change.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009 and 2008, our restricted cash amounts
were $63.6 million and $203.8 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;See Note 6 for
information regarding derivative instruments and hedging
activities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Revenue
Recognition</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In general, we recognize revenue from
our customers when all of the following criteria are met:&#160;&#160;(i)
persuasive evidence of an exchange arrangement exists, (ii) delivery has
occurred or services have been rendered, (iii) the buyer&#8217;s price is fixed or
determinable and (iv) collectability is reasonably assured.&#160;&#160;See Note
4 for additional information regarding our revenue recognition
policies.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="n3">Note 3.&#160;</a>&#160;Recent Accounting Developments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
accounting standard setting bodies have recently issued the following guidance
that will or may affect our future financial statements:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Fair
Value Measurements</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.</font>&#160; In January 2010, the
Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued new guidance to improve
disclosures about fair value measurements.&#160; This new guidance requires the
following:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div>
        <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Consolidation

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="n4">Note 4.&#160;&#160;</a>Revenue Recognition</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
following information provides a general description of our underlying revenue
recognition policies by business segment:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NGL
Pipelines &amp; Services</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our NGL
Pipelines &amp; Services include our (i) natural gas processing business and
related NGL marketing activities; (ii) NGL pipelines aggregating approximately
16,300 miles; (iii) NGL and related product storage and terminal facilities and
(iv) NGL fractionation facilities.&#160;&#160;This segment also includes our
import and export terminal operations.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In our natural gas processing business,
we enter into percent-of-liquids contracts, percent-of-proceeds contracts,
fee-based contracts, hybrid-contracts (i.e. a combination of percent-of-liquids
and fee-based contract terms), keepwhole contracts and margin-band
contracts.&#160;&#160;Under keepwhole and margin-band contracts, we take
ownership of mixed NGLs extracted from the producer&#8217;s natural gas stream and
recognize revenue when the extracted NGLs are delivered and sold to customers
under NGL marketing sales contracts.&#160;&#160;In the same way, revenue is
recognized under our percent-of-liquids contracts except that the volume of NGLs
we extract and sell is less than the total amount of NGLs extracted from the
producers&#8217; natural gas.&#160;&#160;Under a percent-of-liquids contract, the
producer retains title to the remaining percentage of mixed NGLs we
extract.&#160;&#160;Under a percent-of-proceeds contract, we share in the
proceeds generated from the sale of the mixed NGLs we extract on the producer&#8217;s
behalf.&#160;&#160;If a cash fee for natural gas processing services is
stipulated by the contract, we record revenue when the natural gas has been
processed and delivered to the producer.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our NGL
marketing activities generate revenues from the sale and delivery of NGLs
obtained through our processing activities and spot and contract purchases from
third parties.&#160;&#160;Revenues from these sales contracts are recognized
when the NGLs are delivered to customers.&#160;&#160;In general, sales prices
referenced in these contracts are market-based and may include pricing
differentials for such factors as delivery location.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under our
NGL pipeline transportation contracts and tariffs, revenue is recognized when
volumes have been delivered to customers.&#160;&#160;Revenue from these
contracts and tariffs is generally based upon a fixed fee per gallon of liquids
transported multiplied by the volume delivered.&#160;&#160;Transportation fees
charged under these arrangements are either contractual or regulated by
governmental agencies such as the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
(&#8220;FERC&#8221;).</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
collect storage revenues under our NGL and related product storage contracts
based on the number of days a customer has volumes in storage multiplied by a
storage rate (as defined in each contract).&#160;&#160;Under these contracts,
revenue is recognized ratably over the length of the storage
period.&#160;&#160;With respect to capacity reservation agreements, we collect a
fee for reserving storage capacity for certain customers in our underground
storage wells.&#160;&#160;Under these agreements, revenue is recognized ratably
over the specified reservation period.&#160;&#160;Excess storage fees are
collected when customers exceed their reservation amounts and are recognized in
the period of occurrence.&#160;&#160;In addition, we charge other customers
throughput fees based on volumes delivered into and subsequently withdrawn from
storage, which are recognized as the service is provided.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We enter
into fee-based arrangements and percent-of-liquids contracts for the NGL
fractionation services we provide to customers.&#160;&#160;Under such fee-based
arrangements, revenue is recognized in the period services are
provided.&#160;&#160;Such fee-based arrangements typically include a
base-processing fee (usually stated in cents per gallon) that is contractually
subject to adjustment for changes in certain fractionation expenses (e.g.
natural gas fuel costs).&#160;&#160;Certain of our NGL fractionation facilities
generate revenues using percent-of-liquids contracts.&#160;&#160;Such contracts
allow us to retain a contractually determined percentage of the customer&#8217;s
fractionated NGL products as payment for services rendered.&#160;&#160;Revenue
is recognized from such arrangements when we sell and deliver the retained NGLs
to customers.</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">
          </div>

          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">F-18</font></div>

            <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
          </div>

        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Revenues
from product terminaling activities are recorded in the period such services are
provided.&#160;&#160;Customers are typically billed a fee per unit of volume
loaded or unloaded.&#160;&#160;With respect to our export terminal operations,
revenues may also include demand payments charged to customers who reserve the
use of our export facilities and later fail to use them.&#160;&#160;Demand fee
revenues are recognized when the customer fails to utilize the specified export
facility as required by contract.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Onshore Natural Gas Pipelines &amp;
Services</font></font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our Onshore Natural Gas Pipelines &amp;
Services include approximately 19,200 miles of onshore natural gas pipeline
systems that provide for the gathering and transportation of natural gas in
Alabama, Colorado, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico, Texas and
Wyoming.&#160;&#160;We own two salt dome natural gas storage facilities located
in Mississippi and lease natural gas storage facilities located in Texas and
Louisiana.&#160;&#160;This segment also includes our natural gas marketing
activities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our onshore natural gas pipelines
typically generate revenues from transportation agreements where shippers are
billed a fee per unit of volume transported (typically per million British
thermal units, or &#8220;MMBtu&#8221;) multiplied by the volume gathered or
delivered.&#160;&#160;The transportation fees charged under these arrangements
are either contractual or regulated by governmental agencies, including the
FERC.&#160;&#160;Certain of our onshore natural gas pipelines offer firm
capacity reservation services whereby the shipper pays a contractually stated
fee based on the level of throughput capacity reserved in our pipelines whether
or not the shipper actually utilizes such capacity.&#160;&#160;Revenues under
firm capacity reservation agreements are recognized in the period the services
are provided.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Revenues
from natural gas storage contracts typically have two components: (i) monthly
demand payments, which are associated with a customer&#8217;s storage capacity
reservations, and (ii) storage fees per unit of volume stored at our
facilities.&#160;&#160;Revenues from demand payments are recognized during the
period the customer reserves capacity.&#160;&#160;Revenues from storage fees are
recognized in the period the services are provided.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
natural gas marketing activities generate revenues from the sale and delivery of
natural gas purchased from third parties on the open market.&#160;&#160;Revenues
from these sales contracts are recognized when the natural gas is delivered to
customers.&#160;&#160;In general, sales prices referenced in these contracts are
market-based and may include pricing differentials for such factors as delivery
location.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Onshore
Crude Oil Pipelines &amp; Services</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
Onshore Crude Oil Pipelines &amp; Services include approximately 4,400 miles of
onshore crude oil pipelines and 10.5 million barrels (&#8220;MMBbls&#8221;) of above-ground
storage tank capacity.&#160;&#160;This segment includes our crude oil marketing
activities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Revenue from crude oil transportation
is generally based upon a fixed fee per barrel transported multiplied by the
volume delivered.&#160;&#160;The transportation fees charged under these
arrangements are either contractual or regulated by governmental agencies,
including the FERC.&#160;&#160;Revenues associated with these arrangements are
recognized when volumes have been delivered.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under our
crude oil terminaling agreements, we charge customers for crude oil storage
based on the number of days a customer has volumes in storage multiplied by a
contractual storage rate.&#160;&#160;Under these contracts, revenue is
recognized ratably over the length of the storage period.&#160;&#160;With
respect to storage capacity reservation agreements, we collect a fee for
reserving storage capacity for customers at our terminals.&#160;&#160;Under
these agreements, revenue is recognized ratably over the specified reservation
period.&#160;&#160;In addition, we charge our customers throughput (or
&#8220;pumpover&#8221;) fees based on volumes withdrawn from our terminals.&#160;&#160;Crude
oil storage revenues are recognized ratably over the length of the storage
period.&#160;&#160;Revenues are also generated from fee-based trade
documentation services and are recognized as services are
completed.</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">F-19</font></div>
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our crude oil marketing activities
generate revenues from the sale and delivery of crude oil obtained from
producers or on the open market.&#160;&#160;These sales contracts generally
settle with the physical delivery of crude oil to customers.&#160;&#160;In
general, the sales prices referenced in these contracts are market-based and may
include pricing differentials for such factors as delivery
location.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Offshore
Pipelines &amp; Services</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our Offshore Pipelines &amp; Services
include our (i) offshore natural gas pipelines, (ii) offshore Gulf of Mexico
crude oil pipeline systems and (iii) six multi-purpose offshore hub platforms
which serve production areas including some of the most active drilling and
development regions in the Gulf of Mexico.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Revenues
from our offshore pipelines are derived from fee-based agreements whereby the
customer is charged a fee per unit of volume gathered or transported (typically
per MMBtu of natural gas or per barrel of crude oil) multiplied by the volume
delivered.&#160;&#160;Revenues associated with these fee-based contracts and
tariffs are recognized when volumes have been delivered.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Revenues
from offshore platform services generally consist of demand fees and commodity
charges.&#160;&#160;Revenues from platform services are recognized in the period
the services are provided.&#160;&#160;Demand fees represent charges to customers
served by our offshore platforms regardless of the volume the customer actually
delivers to the platform.&#160;&#160;Revenues from commodity charges are based
on a fixed-fee per unit of volume delivered to the platform (typically per
million cubic feet of natural gas or per barrel of crude oil) multiplied by the
total volume of each product delivered.&#160;&#160;Contracts for platform
services often include both demand fees and commodity charges, but demand fees
generally expire after a contractually fixed period of time and in some
instances may be subject to cancellation by customers.&#160;&#160;Our
Independence Hub offshore platform earns a significant amount of demand
revenues.&#160;&#160;The Independence Hub platform will earn $54.6 million of
demand fees annually through March 2012.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Petrochemical
&amp; Refined Products Services</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our Petrochemical &amp; Refined
Products Services consist of (i) propylene fractionation plants and related
activities, (ii) butane isomerization facilities, (iii) an octane enhancement
facility, (iv) refined products pipelines, including our Products Pipeline
System, and related activities and (v) marine transportation assets and other
services.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
propylene fractionation and butane isomerization facilities generate revenues
through fee-based arrangements, which typically include a base-processing fee
per gallon (or other unit of measurement) subject to adjustment for changes in
natural gas, electricity and labor costs, which are the primary costs of
propylene fractionation and butane isomerization.&#160;&#160;Revenues resulting
from such agreements are recognized in the period the services are
provided.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
petrochemical marketing activities generate revenues from the sale and delivery
of products obtained through our propylene fractionation activities and
purchases of petrochemical products from third parties on the open
market.&#160;&#160;Revenues from these sales contracts are recognized when such
products are delivered to customers.&#160;&#160;In general, we sell our
petrochemical products at market-based prices, which may include pricing
differentials for such factors as delivery location.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
refined products pipelines, including our Products Pipeline System, generate
revenues through fee-based contracts or tariffs as customers are billed a fixed
fee per barrel of liquids transported multiplied by the volume
delivered.&#160;&#160;Transportation fees charged under these arrangements are
either contractual or regulated by governmental agencies, including the
FERC.&#160;&#160;Revenues associated with these fee-based contracts and tariffs
are recognized when volumes have been delivered.&#160;&#160;Revenues from our
refined products storage facilities are based on the number of days a customer
has volumes in storage multiplied by a contractual storage
rate.&#160;&#160;Under these contracts, revenue is recognized ratably over the
length of the storage period.&#160;&#160;Revenues from product terminaling
activities are recorded in the period such services are
provided.&#160;&#160;Customers are typically billed a fee per unit of volume
loaded.</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">
          </div>

          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Revenue
is also generated from the provision of inland and offshore transportation of
refined products, crude oil, condensate, asphalt, heavy fuel oil and other
heated oil products via tow boats and tank barges.&#160;&#160;Under our marine
services transportation contracts, revenue is recognized over the transit time
of individual tows as determined on an individual contract basis, which is
generally less than ten days in duration.&#160;&#160;Revenue from these
contracts is typically based on set day rates or a set fee per cargo
movement.&#160;&#160;Most of the marine services transportation contracts
include escalation provisions to recover increased operating costs such as
incremental increases in labor.&#160;&#160;The costs of fuel, substantially all
of which is a pass through expense, and other specified operational fees and
costs are directly reimbursed by the customer under most of the
contracts.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
results of operations from the distribution of lubrication oils and specialty
chemicals and the bulk transportation of fuels are dependent on the sales price
or transportation fees that we charge our customers.&#160;&#160;Revenue is
recognized for sales transactions and transportation arrangements when the
product is delivered.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The fair value of an equity-classified
award (e.g., a restricted unit award) is amortized to earnings on a
straight-line basis over the requisite service or vesting
period.&#160;&#160;Compensation expense for liability-classified awards (e.g.,
unit appreciation rights (&#8220;UARs&#8221;)) is recognized over the requisite service or
vesting period of an award based on the fair value of the award remeasured at
each reporting period.&#160;&#160;Liability-classified awards are settled in
cash upon vesting.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At
December 31, 2009, our active long-term incentive plans are the Enterprise
Products 1998 Long-Term Incentive Plan (&#8220;1998 Plan&#8221;), the TEPPCO 1999 Phantom
Unit Retention Plan (&#8220;1999 Plan&#8221;), the Enterprise Products 2006 TPP Long-Term
Incentive Plan (&#8220;2006 Plan&#8221;) and the Amended and Restated 2008 Enterprise
Products Long-Term Incentive Plan (&#8220;2008 Plan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Two plans were
dissolved during 2009:&#160;&#160;TEPPCO 2000 Long-Term Incentive Plan (&#8220;2000
Plan&#8221;) and TEPPCO 2005 Phantom Unit Plan (&#8220;2005 Plan&#8221;).</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The 1998
Plan provides for awards of Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; common units and other
rights to our non-employee directors and to employees of EPCO and its affiliates
providing services to us.&#160;&#160;Awards under the 1998 Plan may be granted
in the form of unit options, restricted units, phantom units, UARs and
distribution equivalent rights (&#8220;DERs&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Up to 7,000,000 of
Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; common units may be issued as awards under the
1998 Plan.&#160;&#160;After giving effect to awards granted under the plan
through December 31, 2009, a total of 652,543 additional common units could be
issued.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The 1999
Plan provided key employees of EPCO who work on our behalf with phantom unit

exchange ratio.&#160;&#160;The vesting terms of each award and other provisions
of the plan remain unchanged.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">An
allocated portion of the fair value of these long-term incentive plan
equity-based awards is charged to us under the administrative services agreement
(&#8220;ASA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;See Note 15 for a general description of the ASA with
EPCO.&#160;&#160;With the exception of certain amounts recorded in connection
with EPCO Unit, as defined later in this note, we are not responsible for
reimbursing EPCO for any expenses associated with such awards.&#160;&#160;We
recognize an expense for our allocated share of the grant date fair value of
such awards, with an offsetting amount recorded in equity.&#160;&#160;Beginning
in February 2009, the ASA was amended to provide that we and other affiliates of
EPCO will reimburse EPCO for our allocated share of distributions of cash or
securities made to the Class B limited partners of EPCO Unit.&#160;&#160;Our
reimbursements to EPCO during 2009 in connection with EPCO Unit were $0.7
million.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
December&#160;10, 2009, the board of directors of DEP GP unanimously approved a
resolution adopting both the 2010 Duncan Energy Partners L.P. Long-Term
Incentive Plan (&#8220;2010 Plan&#8221;) and the DEP Unit Purchase Plan (&#8220;DEP EUPP&#8221;).&#160;
The 2010 Plan provides for awards of options to purchase Duncan Energy Partners&#8217;
common units, restricted common units, UARs, phantom units and DERs to
employees, directors or consultants providing services to Duncan Energy
Partners.&#160; The DEP EUPP provides eligible employees the opportunity to
purchase common units at a discount through withholdings from eligible
compensation.&#160;&#160;On December&#160;30, 2009, the action taken by the
board of directors of DEP GP regarding the plans was approved by written consent
of EPO, which held approximately 58.6% of Duncan Energy Partners&#8217; outstanding
common units as of that date.&#160;&#160;Because EPO held a majority of Duncan
Energy Partners&#8217; common units as of December 30, 2009, no other votes were
necessary to adopt the plans.&#160; In February 2010, Duncan Energy Partners
filed a registration statement with the SEC authorizing the issuance of up to
500,000 common units in connection with the 2010 Plan and 500,000 common units
in connection with the DEP EUPP.&#160; The plans became effective on February
11, 2010.&#160;</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Restricted
Unit Awards</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Restricted
unit awards allow recipients to acquire common units of Enterprise Products
Partners (at no cost to the recipient) once a defined vesting period expires,
subject to customary forfeiture provisions.&#160;&#160;The restrictions on such
awards generally lapse four years from the date of grant.&#160;&#160;The fair
value of restricted units is based on the market price per unit of the
underlying security on the date of grant. Compensation expense is recognized
based on the grant date fair value, net of an allowance for estimated
forfeitures.&#160;&#160;As used in the context of our long-term incentive plans,
the term &#8220;restricted unit&#8221; represents a time-vested unit.&#160;&#160;Such awards
are non-vested until the required service period expires.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Unit
Option Awards</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certain
of our long-term incentive plans provide for the issuance of non-qualified
incentive options to purchase a fixed number of Enterprise Products Partners&#8217;
common units.&#160;&#160;When issued, the exercise price of each option grant
may be no less than the market price of the underlying security on the date of
grant.&#160;&#160;In general, options granted under the EPCO plans have a
vesting period of four years and remain exercisable for five to ten years, as
applicable, from the date of grant.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The fair
value of each unit option is estimated on the date of grant using the
Black-Scholes option pricing model, which incorporates various assumptions
including expected life of the options, risk-free interest rates, expected
distribution yield on Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; common units, and expected
unit price volatility of Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; common
units.&#160;&#160;In general, our assumption of expected life of the options
represents the period of time that the options are expected to be outstanding
based on an analysis of historical option activity.&#160;&#160;Our selection of
the risk-free interest rate is based on published yields for U.S. government
securities with comparable terms.&#160;&#160;The expected distribution yield and
unit price volatility is estimated based on several factors, which include an
analysis of Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; historical unit price volatility and
distribution yield over a period equal to the expected life of the
option.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
2008, in response to changes in the federal tax code applicable to certain types
of equity awards, Enterprise Products Partners amended the terms of certain of
its outstanding unit options.&#160; In general, the expiration dates of these
awards were modified from May and August 2017 to December 2012.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In order
to fund its unit option-related obligations, EPCO may purchase common units at
fair value either in the open market or directly from Enterprise Products
Partners.&#160;&#160;When employees exercise unit options, Enterprise Products
Partners reimburses EPCO for the cash difference between the strike price paid
by the employee and the actual purchase price paid by EPCO for the units issued
to the employee.</font></div>

compensation cost for these awards over a weighted-average period of 2.9
years.</font></div><br>

          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
