      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Profits
Interests Awards</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As
long-term incentive arrangements, EPCO has granted its key employees who perform
services on behalf of us, EPCO and other affiliated companies, &#8220;profits
interests&#8221; in several limited partnerships (the &#8220;Employee Partnerships&#8221;), all of
which are private company affiliates of EPCO.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009,
the Employee Partnerships are EPE Unit I, EPE Unit II, EPE Unit III, Enterprise
Unit and EPCO Unit.&#160;&#160;TEPPCO Unit L.P. and TEPPCO Unit II L.P. were
dissolved during 2009.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Profits
interests awards entitle each holder to participate in the expected long-term
appreciation in value of the equity securities owned by each Employee
Partnership.&#160;&#160;The Employee Partnerships in which our named executive
officers participate own either units of the Parent Company or Enterprise
Products Partners or a combination of both.&#160;&#160;The profits interests
awards are subject to customary forfeiture provisions.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Each
Employee Partnership has a single Class A limited partner, which is a privately
held indirect subsidiary of EPCO, and a varying number of Class B limited
partners.&#160;&#160;At formation, the Class A limited partner either
contributes cash or limited partner units it owns to the Employee
Partnership.&#160;&#160;If cash is contributed, the Employee Partnership uses
these funds to acquire limited partner units on the open market.&#160;&#160;In
general, the Class A limited partner earns a preferred return (either fixed or
variable depending on the partnership agreement) on its investment (or &#8220;Capital
Base&#8221;) in the Employee Partnership and residual quarterly cash amounts, if any,
are distributed to the Class B limited partners.&#160;&#160;Upon liquidation,
Employee Partnership assets having a fair market value equal to the Class A
limited partner&#8217;s Capital Base, plus any preferred return for the period in
which liquidation occurs, will be distributed to the Class A limited
partner.&#160;&#160;Any remaining assets will be distributed to the Class B
limited partner(s) as a residual profits interest and are a factor of the
appreciation in value of the partnership&#8217;s assets since its formation
date.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The grant
date fair value of each Employee Partnership is based on (i) the estimated value
of the remaining assets, as determined using a Black-Scholes option pricing
model, that would be distributed to the Class B limited partners upon
dissolution of the Employee Partnership and (ii) the value, based on a
discounted cash flow analysis using appropriate discount rates, of the residual
quarterly cash amounts that the Class B limited partners are expected to receive
over the life of the Employee Partnership.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
following table summarizes key elements of each Employee Partnership as of
December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;As used in the table in reference to the
description of assets, &#8220;EPE&#8221; means Enterprise GP Holdings L.P. and &#8220;EPD&#8221; means
Enterprise Products Partners L.P.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The total
unrecognized compensation cost of the profits interests awards was $55.0 million
at December 31, 2009 of which our share is currently estimated to be $47.6
million.&#160;&#160;We expect to recognize our share of the unrecognized
compensation cost for these awards over a weighted-average period of 6.1
years.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
December 2009, the expected liquidation date for each Employee Partnership was
extended to February 2016.&#160;&#160;This modification follows a similar set of
modifications made in July 2008 for EPE Unit I, EPE Unit II and EPE Unit III
that extended liquidation dates as well as reduced the Class A limited partner&#8217;s
preferred return rates.&#160;&#160;These modifications are intended to align the
interests of the employee partners of the Employee Partnerships with the
long-term interests of EPCO and other unitholders in the relevant underlying
publicly traded partnerships, which also hold indirectly a significant ownership
interest in both us and our subsidiaries.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Phantom
Units</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certain
of our long-term incentive plans provide for the issuance of phantom unit
awards.&#160;&#160;These awards are automatically redeemed for cash based on the
fair value of the vested portion of phantom units at redemption dates in each
award.&#160;&#160;The fair value of each phantom unit award is equal to the
closing market price of the underlying security on the redemption
date.&#160;&#160;Each participant is required to redeem their phantom units as
they vest, which typically is three to four years from the date the award is
granted.&#160;&#160;Our phantom units are accounted for as liability
awards.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certain
of our long-term incentive plans also provide for the award of DERs in tandem
with phantom unit awards.&#160;&#160;A DER entitles the participant to cash
distributions equal to the product of the number of awards outstanding for the
participant and the cash distribution rate per unit paid by the issuer to its
unitholders.&#160;&#160;Such amounts are expensed when paid.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">UARs

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="n6">Note 6.&#160;&#160;</a>Derivative Instruments, Hedging Activities and
Fair Value Measurements</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In the
course of our normal business operations, we are exposed to certain risks,
including changes in interest rates, commodity prices and, to a limited extent,
foreign exchange rates.&#160;&#160;In order to manage risks associated with
certain identifiable and anticipated transactions, we use derivative
instruments.&#160;&#160;Derivatives are instruments whose fair value is
determined by changes in a specified benchmark such as interest rates, commodity
prices or currency values.&#160;&#160;Fair value is generally defined as the
amount at which a derivative instrument could be exchanged in a current
transaction between willing parties, not in a forced sale.&#160;&#160;Typical
derivative instruments include futures, forward contracts, swaps, options and
other instruments with similar characteristics.&#160;&#160;Substantially all of
our derivatives are used for non-trading activities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We are required to recognize derivative
instruments at fair value as either assets or liabilities on the balance
sheet.&#160;&#160;While all derivatives are required to be reported at fair
value on the balance sheet, changes in fair value of the derivative instruments
are reported in different ways depending on the nature and effectiveness of the
hedging activities to which they are related.&#160;&#160;After meeting specified
conditions, a qualified derivative may be specifically designated as a total or
partial hedge of:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div>
        <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
              <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
                <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
              </td>
              <td>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Changes
      in the fair value of a recognized asset or liability, or an unrecognized
      firm commitment - In a fair value hedge, gains and losses for both the
      derivative instrument and the hedged item are recognized in income during
      the period of change.</font></div>
              </td>
            </tr></table>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div>
        <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
              <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
                <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
              </td>
              <td>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Variable
      cash flows of a forecasted transaction - In a cash flow hedge, the
      effective portion of the hedge is reported in other comprehensive income
      or loss (&#8220;OCI&#8221;) and is reclassified into earnings when the forecasted
      transaction affects earnings.</font></div>
              </td>
            </tr></table>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div>
        <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
              <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
                <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
              </td>
              <td>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Foreign
      currency exposure - A foreign currency hedge can be treated as either a
      fair value hedge or a cash flow hedge depending on the risk being
      hedged.</font></div>
              </td>
            </tr></table>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>An effective hedge relationship is one
in which the change in fair value of a derivative instrument can be expected to
offset 80% to 125% of changes in the fair value of a hedged item at inception
and throughout the life of the hedging relationship.&#160;&#160;The effective
portion of a hedge relationship is the amount by which the derivative instrument
exactly offsets the change in fair value of the hedged item during the reporting
period.&#160;&#160;Conversely, ineffectiveness represents the change in the fair
value of the derivative instrument that does not exactly offset the change in
the fair value of the hedged item.&#160;&#160;Any
ineffectiveness</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">F-29</font></div>
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">associated
with a hedge relationship is recognized in earnings
immediately.&#160;&#160;Ineffectiveness can be caused by, among other things,
changes in the timing of forecasted transactions or a mismatch of terms between
the derivative instrument and the hedged item.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A
contract designated as a cash flow hedge of an anticipated transaction that is
probable of not occurring is immediately recognized in earnings.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Interest
Rate Derivative Instruments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

treasury locks and similar derivative instruments to manage our exposure to
changes in the interest rates of certain consolidated debt
agreements.&#160;&#160;This strategy is a component in controlling our cost of
capital associated with such borrowings.</font></div>

      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In August
2009, two of the Parent Company&#8217;s floating-to-fixed interest rate swaps
associated with its variable-interest rate borrowings expired.&#160;&#160;Such
swaps had a notional amount of $250.0 million.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Changes
in the fair value of the interest rate swaps and the related hedged items were
recorded on the balance sheet with the offset recorded as interest expense.
&#160;Cash flow hedges fix the interest rate paid on floating rate debt with the
difference between the floating rate and fixed rate being recorded as an
increase or decrease to interest expense. &#160;This combined activity resulted
in an increase of interest expense of $16.2 million and $6.4 million for the
years ended December 31, 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At times,
we may use treasury lock derivative instruments to hedge the underlying U.S.
treasury rates related to forecasted issuances of debt.&#160;&#160;As cash flow
hedges, gains or losses on these instruments are recorded in OCI and amortized
into earnings using the effective interest method over the estimated term of the
underlying fixed-rate debt.&#160;&#160;During 2008, we terminated treasury locks
with a combined notional amount of $1.2 billion and recognized an aggregate loss

                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(1)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Volume

      amount of volumes hedged whereas volume for derivatives not designated as

      maximum term for derivatives included in the long-term column is December
      2012.</font></div>

      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">PTR
      represents the British thermal unit equivalent of the NGLs extracted from
      natural gas by a processing plant, and includes the natural gas used as
      plant fuel to extract those liquids, plant flare and other
      shortages.&#160;&#160;See the discussion below for the primary objective
      of this strategy.</font></div>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(4)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Excludes
      5.4 MMBbls of additional hedges executed under contracts that have been
      designated as normal sales agreements under the FASB&#8217;s derivative and
      hedging guidance.&#160;&#160;The combination of these volumes with the 2.4
      MMBbls reflected as derivatives in the table above results in a total of
      7.8 MMBbls of hedged forecasted NGL sales volumes, which corresponds to
      the 17.8 Bcf of forecasted natural gas purchase volumes for
      PTR.</font></div>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(5)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Current
      and long-term volumes include approximately 109.5 and 12.6 billion cubic
      feet (&#8220;Bcf&#8221;), respectively, of physical derivative instruments that are
      predominantly priced at an index plus a premium or minus a
      discount.</font></div>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(6)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Reflects

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Certain of our derivative instruments
do not meet hedge accounting requirements; therefore, they are accounted for
using mark-to-market accounting.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our three predominant hedging
strategies are hedging natural gas processing margins, hedging anticipated
future sales of NGLs, refined products and crude oil associated with volumes
held in inventory</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">and
hedging the fair value of natural gas in inventory.&#160;&#160;The objective of
our natural gas processing strategy is to hedge an amount of gross margin
associated with the gas processing activities. We achieve this by using physical
and financial instruments to lock in the prices of natural gas purchases used
for PTR and NGL sales.&#160;&#160;This program consists of (i) the forward sale
of a portion of our expected equity NGL production at fixed prices through
December 2010, achieved through the use of forward physical sales and commodity
derivative instruments and (ii) the purchase of commodity derivative instruments
with a notional amount determined by the amount of natural gas expected to be
consumed as PTR in the production of such equity NGL production.&#160;&#160;The
objective of our NGL, refined products and crude oil sales hedging program is to
hedge anticipated future sales of inventory by locking in the sales price
through the use of forward physical sales and commodity derivative
instruments.&#160;&#160;The objective of our natural gas inventory hedging
program is to hedge the fair value of natural gas currently held in inventory by
locking in the sales price of the inventory through the use of commodity
derivative instruments.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Foreign
Currency Derivative Instruments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We are exposed to a nominal amount of
foreign currency exchange risk in connection with our NGL and natural gas
marketing activities in Canada.&#160;&#160;As a result, we could be adversely
affected by fluctuations in currency rates between the U.S. dollar and Canadian
dollar.&#160;&#160;In order to manage this risk, we may enter into foreign
exchange purchase contracts to lock in the exchange rate.&#160;&#160;Prior to
2009, these derivative instruments were accounted for using mark-to-market
accounting.&#160;&#160;Beginning with the first quarter of 2009, the long-term
transactions (more than two months) are accounted for as cash flow
hedges.&#160;&#160;Shorter term transactions are accounted for using
mark-to-market accounting.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In 2008 and 2009 we were exposed to
foreign currency exchange risk in connection with a term loan denominated in
Japanese yen (see Note 12).&#160;&#160;We entered into this loan agreement in
November 2008 and the loan matured in March 2009.&#160;&#160;The derivative
instrument used to hedge this risk was accounted for as a cash flow hedge and
was settled upon repayment of the loan.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At
December 31, 2009, we had foreign currency derivative instruments outstanding
with a notional amount of $4.1 million Canadian dollars.&#160;&#160;The fair
market value of these instruments was an asset of $0.2 million at December 31,
2009.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Credit-Risk
Related Contingent Features in Derivative Instruments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
A limited number of our commodity derivative instruments include provisions
related to credit ratings and/or adequate assurance clauses.&#160;&#160;A credit
rating provision provides for a counterparty to demand immediate full or partial
payment to cover a net liability position upon the loss of a stipulated credit
rating.&#160;&#160;An adequate assurance clause provides for a counterparty to
demand immediate full or partial payment to cover a net liability position
should reasonable grounds for insecurity arise with respect to contractual
performance by either party.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009, the aggregate fair
value of our over-the-counter derivative instruments in a net liability position
was $7.7 million, approximately $6.1 million of which was subject to a credit
rating contingent feature.&#160;&#160;If our credit ratings were downgraded to
Ba2/BB, approximately $1.1 million would be payable as a margin deposit to the
counterparties, and if our credit ratings were downgraded to Ba3/BB- or below,
approximately $6.1 million would be payable as a margin deposit to the
counterparties.&#160;&#160;Currently, no margin is required to be
deposited.&#160;&#160;The potential for derivatives with contingent features to
enter a net liability position may change in the future as positions and prices
fluctuate.&#160;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

next twelve months, we expect to reclassify $21.3 million of AOCI attributable
to interest rate derivative instruments into earnings as an increase to interest
expense.&#160;&#160;Likewise, we expect to reclassify $0.8 million of AOCI
attributable to commodity derivative instruments into earnings, $0.2 million as
an increase in operating costs and expenses and $1.0 million as an increase in
revenues.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Fair
Value Measurements</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Fair
value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to
transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at a
specified measurement date.&#160;&#160;Our fair value estimates are based on
either (i) actual market data or (ii) assumptions that other market
participants</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">F-34</font></div>
          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">would use
in pricing an asset or liability, including estimates of
risk.&#160;&#160;Recognized valuation techniques employ inputs such as product
prices, operating costs, discount factors and business growth
rates.&#160;&#160;These inputs may be either readily observable, corroborated by
market data or generally unobservable.&#160;&#160;In developing our estimates of
fair value, we endeavor to utilize the best information available and apply
market-based data to the extent possible.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we utilize
valuation techniques (such as the market approach) that maximize the use of
observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A
three-tier hierarchy has been established that classifies fair value amounts
recognized or disclosed in the financial statements based on the observability
of inputs used to estimate such fair values.&#160;&#160;The hierarchy considers
fair value amounts based on observable inputs (Levels 1 and 2) to be more
reliable and predictable than those based primarily on unobservable inputs
(Level 3).&#160;&#160;At each balance sheet reporting date, we categorize our
financial assets and liabilities using this hierarchy.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
characteristics of fair value amounts classified within each level of the
hierarchy are described as follows:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div>
        <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
              <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
                <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
              </td>
              <td>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Level
      1 fair values are based on quoted prices, which are available in active
      markets for identical assets or liabilities as of the measurement
      date.&#160;&#160;Active markets are defined as those in which transactions
      for identical assets or liabilities occur with sufficient frequency so as
      to provide pricing information on an ongoing basis (e.g., the New York
      Mercantile Exchange).&#160;&#160;Our Level 1 fair values primarily consist
      of financial assets and liabilities such as exchange-traded commodity
      derivative instruments.</font></div>
              </td>
            </tr></table>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div>
        <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
              <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
                <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
              </td>
              <td>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Level
      2 fair values are based on pricing inputs other than quoted prices in
      active markets (as reflected in Level 1 fair values) and are either
      directly or indirectly observable as of the measurement
      date.&#160;&#160;Level 2 fair values include instruments that are valued
      using financial models or other appropriate valuation
      methodologies.&#160;&#160;Such financial models are primarily
      industry-standard models that consider various assumptions, including
      quoted forward prices for commodities, the time value of money, volatility
      factors, current market and contractual prices for the underlying
      instruments and other relevant economic measures.&#160;&#160;Substantially
      all of these assumptions are: (i) observable in the marketplace throughout
      the full term of the instrument, (ii) can be derived from observable data
      or (iii) are validated by inputs other than quoted prices (e.g., interest
      rate and yield curves at commonly quoted intervals).&#160;&#160;Our Level
      2 fair values primarily consist of commodity derivative instruments such
      as forwards, swaps and other instruments transacted on an exchange or over
      the counter.&#160;&#160;The fair values of these derivatives are based on
      observable price quotes for similar products and locations.&#160;&#160;The
      value of our interest rate derivatives are valued by using appropriate
      financial models with the implied forward London&#160;&#160;Interbank
      Offered Rate (&#8220;LIBOR&#8221;) yield curve for the same period as the future
      interest swap settlements.</font></div>
              </td>
            </tr></table>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div>
        <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
              <td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
                <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Wingdings">&#167;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
              </td>
              <td>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Level
      3 fair values are based on unobservable inputs.&#160;&#160;Unobservable
      inputs are used to measure fair value to the extent that observable inputs
      are not available, thereby allowing for situations in which there is
      little, if any, market activity for the asset or liability at the
      measurement date.&#160;&#160;Unobservable inputs reflect the reporting
      entity&#8217;s own ideas about the assumptions that market participants would
      use in pricing an asset or liability (including assumptions about
      risk).&#160;&#160;Unobservable inputs are based on the best information
      available in the circumstances, which might include the reporting entity&#8217;s
      internally developed data.&#160;&#160;The reporting entity must not ignore
      information about market participant assumptions that is reasonably
      available without undue cost and effort.&#160;&#160;Level 3 inputs are
      typically used in connection with internally developed valuation
      methodologies where management makes its best estimate of an instrument&#8217;s
      fair value.&#160;&#160;Our Level 3 fair values largely consist of ethane,
      normal butane and natural gasoline-based contracts with a range of two to
      12 months in term.&#160;&#160;We rely on price quotes from reputable
      brokers in the marketplace who publish price quotes on certain
      products.&#160;&#160;Whenever possible, we compare these prices to other
      reputable brokers for the same product in the same
      market.&#160;&#160;These prices, combined with our forward transactions,
      are used in our model to determine the fair value of such
      instruments.</font></div>
              </td>
            </tr></table>
      </div><br>

appropriate valuation techniques, we adjusted the carrying value of certain
assets to $31.4 million and recorded non-cash impairment charges of $33.5
million during 2009. These charges are reflected in operating costs and expenses
for the year ended December 31, 2009 and have been allocated to property, plant
and equipment, intangible assets, goodwill and other current
assets.&#160;&#160;During 2009, impairments primarily resulted from (i) reduced
levels of throughput volumes at certain river terminals and the indefinite
suspension of three new proposed river terminals, (ii) reduced throughput levels
at a natural gas processing plant, (iii) the cancellation of a compressor
station project and (iv) the determination that a storage cavern and certain
marine barges were obsolete.&#160;&#160;Our fair value estimates were based
primarily on an evaluation of the future cash flows associated with each
asset.</font></div>

              <td valign="bottom" width="9%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 2px solid; TEXT-ALIGN: right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>
              <td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 2px; BORDER-BOTTOM: black 2px solid; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>
            </tr><tr bgcolor="white">
              <td colspan="8" valign="bottom" style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify">
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(1)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Working
      inventory is comprised of inventories of natural gas, NGLs, crude oil,
      refined products, lubrication oils and certain petrochemical products that
      are either available-for-sale or used in the provision for
      services.</font></div>
                <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(2)&#160;&#160;
      </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Forward
      sales inventory consists of identified natural gas, NGL, refined product
      and crude oil volumes dedicated to the fulfillment of forward sales
      contracts.&#160;In general, the increase in volumes dedicated to forward
      physical sales contracts improves the overall utilization and
      profitability of our fee-based assets.&#160;The cash invested in forward
      sales NGL inventories is expected to be recovered within the next twelve
      months as physical delivery from inventory occurs.</font></div>
              </td>
              <td nowrap valign="bottom" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>
            </tr></table>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In those
instances where we take ownership of inventory volumes through
percent-of-liquids contracts and similar arrangements (as opposed to actually
purchasing volumes for cash from third parties, see Note 4), these volumes are
valued at market-based prices during the month in which they are
acquired.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Due to
fluctuating commodity prices, we recognize LCM adjustments when the carrying
value of our inventories exceeds their net realizable value.&#160;&#160;These
non-cash charges are a component of cost of sales in the period they are
recognized and generally affect our segment operating results in the following
manner:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div>

      of NGL inventories are recorded as an expense related to our NGL marketing
      activities within our NGL Pipelines &amp; Services business
      segment;</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In August
2008, our wholly owned subsidiaries, together with Oiltanking Holding Americas,
Inc. (&#8220;Oiltanking&#8221;) formed the Texas Offshore Port System partnership
(&#8220;TOPS&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Effective April 16, 2009, our wholly owned subsidiaries
dissociated from TOPS.&#160;&#160;As a result, operating costs and expenses and
net income for the year ended December 31, 2009 include a non-cash charge of
$68.4 million.&#160;&#160;This loss represents the forfeiture of our cumulative
investment in TOPS through the date of dissociation and reflects our capital
contributions to TOPS for construction in progress
amounts.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

a consolidated subsidiary of ours prior to the dissociation.&#160;&#160;The
effect of deconsolidation was to remove the accounts of TOPS, including
Oiltanking&#8217;s noncontrolling interest of $33.4 million, from our books and
records, after reflecting the $68.4 million aggregate write-off of the
investment.&#160;&#160;See Note 18 for information regarding expense amounts
recognized during 2009 in connection with a settlement agreement involving
TOPS.</font></div>

recorded $21.0 million, $4.3 million and $4.1 million of non-cash impairment
charges within our Petrochemical &amp; Refined Products Services segment,
Onshore Natural Gas Pipelines &amp; Services segment and NGL Pipelines &amp;
Services segment, respectively, related to plant, property and equipment during
the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;See Note 6 for additional
information regarding impairment charges.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
reviewed assumptions underlying the estimated remaining useful lives of certain
of our assets during the first quarter of 2008.&#160;&#160;As a result of our
review, effective January 1, 2008, we revised the remaining useful lives of
these assets, most notably the assets that constitute our Texas Intrastate
System.&#160;&#160;This revision increased the remaining useful life of such
assets to incorporate recent data showing that natural gas reserves supporting
throughput and processing volumes for these assets have changed since our
original determination made in September 2004.&#160;&#160;These revisions will
prospectively reduce our depreciation expense on assets having carrying values
totaling $2.72 billion as of January 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;On average, we extended
the life of these assets by 3.1 years.&#160;&#160;As a result of this change in
estimate, depreciation expense included in operating income and net income for
the year ended December 31, 2008 decreased by approximately $20.0
million.&#160;&#160;&#160;Of this amount, $19.0 million was attributed to
noncontrolling interest.&#160;&#160;The impact of this change on our earnings
per unit was immaterial.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Asset
Retirement Obligations</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have
recorded AROs related to legal requirements to perform retirement activities as
specified in contractual arrangements and/or governmental
regulations.&#160;&#160;In general, our AROs primarily result from (i)
right-of-way agreements associated with our pipeline operations, (ii) leases of
plant sites and (iii) regulatory requirements triggered by the abandonment or
retirement of certain underground storage assets and offshore
facilities.&#160;&#160;In addition, our AROs may result from the renovation or
demolition of certain assets containing hazardous substances such as
asbestos.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We own

Great Divide Gathering System, located in the Piceance Basin of northwest
Colorado.&#160;&#160;The Great Divide Gathering System extends from the southern
portion of the Piceance Basin, including production from EnCana&#8217;s Mamm Creek
field, to a pipeline interconnection with our Piceance Basin Gathering
System.&#160;&#160;Volumes of natural gas originating on the Great Divide
Gathering System are transported through our Piceance Creek Gathering System to
our 1.7 Bcf/d Meeker natural gas treating and processing complex.&#160;&#160;A
significant portion of these volumes are produced by EnCana and are dedicated to
the Great Divide and Piceance Creek Gathering Systems for the life of the
associated lease holdings.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Cenac
and Horizon Acquisitions</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.</font>&#160;&#160;In February
2008, TEPPCO entered the marine transportation business for refined products,
crude oil and condensate through the purchase of assets from Cenac Towing Co.,
Inc., Cenac Offshore, L.L.C. and Mr. Arlen B. Cenac, Jr. (collectively
&#8220;Cenac&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The aggregate value of total consideration TEPPCO paid or
issued to complete this business combination was $444.7 million, which consisted
of $258.1 million in cash and 4,854,899 newly issued TEPPCO
units.&#160;&#160;Additionally, TEPPCO assumed approximately $63.2 million of
Cenac&#8217;s debt in the transaction.&#160;&#160;TEPPCO acquired 42 tow boats, 89
tank barges and the economic benefit of certain related commercial
agreements.&#160;&#160;This business serves refineries and storage terminals
along the Mississippi, Illinois and Ohio rivers and the Intracoastal Waterway
between Texas and Florida.&#160;&#160;These assets also gather crude oil from
production facilities and platforms along the U.S. Gulf Coast.&#160;&#160;TEPPCO
used a short-term credit facility to finance the cash portion of the acquisition
price and to repay the $63.2 million of debt assumed in this
transaction.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Also in
February 2008, TEPPCO purchased related marine assets from Horizon Maritime,
L.L.C. (&#8220;Horizon&#8221;), a privately held Houston-based company and an affiliate of
Cenac, for $80.8 million in cash.&#160;&#160;In this transaction, TEPPCO
acquired seven tow boats, 17 tank barges, rights to two tow boats under
construction and the economic benefit of certain related commercial
agreements.&#160;&#160;In April 2008, TEPPCO paid an additional $3.0 million to
Horizon pursuant to the purchase agreement upon delivery of one of the tow boats
under construction, and in June 2008, TEPPCO paid an additional $3.8 million
upon delivery of the second tow boat.&#160;&#160;These vessels transport
asphalt, heavy fuel oil and other heated oil products to
storage</font></div><br>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
general, our intangible assets fall within two categories &#8211; customer
relationship and contract-based intangible assets.&#160;&#160;The values
assigned to such intangible assets are amortized to earnings using either (i) a
straight-line approach or (ii) other methods that closely resemble the pattern
in which the economic benefits of associated resource bases are estimated to be
consumed or otherwise used, as appropriate.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Customer
relationship intangible assets</font>.&#160;&#160;Customer relationship
intangible assets represent the estimated economic value assigned to certain
relationships acquired in connection with business combinations and asset
purchases whereby (i) we acquired information about or access to customers and
now have regular contact with them and (ii) the customers now have the ability
to make direct contact with us.&#160;&#160;Customer relationships may arise from
contractual arrangements (such as supplier contracts and service contracts) and
through means other than contracts, such as through regular contact by sales or
service representatives.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;&#160;
Our goodwill impairment testing involves the determination of a reporting unit&#8217;s
fair value, which is predicated based on our assumptions regarding the future
economic prospects of the reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Such assumptions include
(i) discrete financial forecasts for the assets contained within the reporting
unit, which rely on management&#8217;s estimates of operating margins and
transportation volumes; (ii) long-term growth rates for cash flows beyond the
discrete forecast period; and (iii) appropriate discount rates.&#160; Based on
our most recent goodwill impairment testing, each reporting unit&#8217;s fair value
was substantially in excess (a minimum of 10%) of its carrying
value.&#160;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Goodwill
attributable to the acquisition of ownership interests in
TEPPCO</font>.&#160;&#160;As a result of our ownership of 100% of the limited
and general partner interests of TEPPCO following the recently completed TEPPCO
Merger, we applied push down accounting to the $1.2 billion of goodwill recorded
by affiliates of EPCO (which are under common control with us) when they
acquired 100% of the membership interests of TEPPCO GP and 4,400,000 TEPPCO
limited partner units from a third-party in February 2005.&#160;&#160;The $1.2
billion in push down goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price paid
by such affiliates to acquire ownership interests in TEPPCO in February 2005
over the respective fair value of assets acquired and liabilities assumed in the
February 2005 transaction.&#160;&#160;Management attributes the $1.2 billion of
goodwill to the future economic benefits we may realize from our ownership of
TEPPCO, including anticipated commercial synergies and cost
savings.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">TEPPCO
owns and operates an extensive network of assets that facilitate the movement,
marketing, gathering and storage services of various commodities and
energy-related products.&#160;&#160;TEPPCO&#8217;s pipeline network is comprised of
approximately 12,500 miles of pipelines that gather and transport refined
products, crude oil, natural gas and NGLs, including one of the largest common
carrier pipelines for refined products in the United States.&#160;&#160;TEPPCO
also owns a marine services business that transports refined products, crude
oil, asphalt, condensate, heavy fuel oil and other heated oil products via tow
boats and tank barges.&#160;&#160;In addition, TEPPCO owns interests in the
Seaway and Centennial pipeline systems.</font></div>

attributable to GulfTerra Merger</font>.&#160;&#160;Goodwill recorded in
connection with the GulfTerra Merger can be attributed to our belief (at the
time the merger was consummated) that the combined</font></div><br>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">partnerships
would benefit from the strategic location of each partnership&#8217;s assets and the
industry relationships that each possessed.&#160;&#160;In addition, we expected
that various operating synergies could develop (such as reduced general and
administrative costs and interest savings) that would result in improved
financial results for the merged entity.&#160;&#160;Based on miles of pipelines,
GulfTerra was one of the largest natural gas gathering and transportation
companies in the United States, serving producers in the central and western
Gulf of Mexico and onshore in Texas and New Mexico.&#160;&#160;These regions
offer us significant growth potential through the acquisition and construction
of additional pipelines, platforms, processing and storage facilities and other
midstream energy infrastructure.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Acquisition
of Encinal</font>.&#160;&#160;Management attributes goodwill recorded in
connection with the Encinal acquisition to potential future benefits we may
realize from our other south Texas processing and NGL businesses as a result of
acquiring the Encinal business.&#160;&#160;Specifically, our acquisition of the
long-term dedication rights associated with the Encinal business is expected to
add value to our south Texas processing facilities and related NGL businesses
due to increased volumes.&#160;&#160;The Encinal goodwill is recorded as part of
the NGL Pipelines &amp; Services business segment due to management&#8217;s belief
that such future benefits will accrue to businesses classified within this
segment.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Acquisition
of Dixie and Great Divide</font>.&#160;&#160;In 2008, we recorded goodwill in
connection with our acquisition of the remaining third-party interest in Dixie
and with the acquisition of Great Divide.&#160;&#160;The remaining ownership
interests in Dixie were acquired from Amoco Pipeline Holding Company in August
2008.&#160;&#160;Management attributes the goodwill to future earnings growth on
the Dixie Pipeline.&#160;&#160;Specifically, a 100% ownership interest in the
Dixie Pipeline will increase our flexibility to pursue future
opportunities.&#160;&#160;Great Divide was acquired from EnCana in December
2008.&#160;&#160;The Great Divide goodwill is attributable to management&#8217;s
expectations of future economics benefits derived from incremental natural gas
processing margins and other downstream activities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Dixie
and Great Divide goodwill amounts are recorded as part of the NGL Pipelines
&amp; Services business segment due to management&#8217;s belief that such future
benefits will accrue to businesses classified within this segment.</font></div>

connection with our acquisition of marine services businesses, which are
recorded as a part of the Petrochemical &amp; Refined Products Services business
segment due to management&#8217;s belief of potential future economic benefits we
expect to realize as a result of acquiring these assets.</font></div>

of Credit</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At

do not reduce the amount available for borrowing under EPO&#8217;s credit
facilities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Subsidiary
Guarantor Relationships</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Enterprise
Products Partners acts as guarantor of the consolidated debt obligations of EPO
with the exception of the DEP Revolving Credit Facility and the DEP Term Loan
Agreement.&#160;&#160;If EPO were to default on any of its guaranteed debt,
Enterprise Products Partners L.P. would be responsible for full repayment of
that obligation.&#160;&#160;Additionally, TEPPCO&#8217;s remaining debt obligations
are non-recourse to Enterprise Products Partners.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Parent
Company&#8217;s Debt Obligations</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Parent Company consolidates the debt obligations of Enterprise Products
Partners; however, the Parent Company does not have the obligation to make
interest or debt payments with respect to such consolidated debt
obligations.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">EPE
Interim Credit Facility</font>.&#160;&#160;In May 2007, the Parent Company
executed a $1.9 billion interim credit facility (the &#8220;EPE Interim Credit
Facility&#8221;) in connection with its acquisition of equity interests in Energy
Transfer Equity and LE GP.&#160;&#160;The EPE Interim Credit Facility provided
for a $200.0&#160;million revolving credit facility and $1.7 billion of term
loans.&#160;&#160;In August 2007, the Parent Company refinanced the $1.2 billion
then outstanding under the EPE Interim Credit Facility using proceeds from its
EPE August 2007 Credit Agreement.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">EPE
August 2007 Credit Agreement</font>.&#160;&#160;The $1.2 billion EPE August 2007
Credit Agreement provided for a $200.0 million revolving credit facility (the
&#8220;EPE Revolver&#8221;), a $125.0 million term loan (&#8220;Term Loan A&#8221;) and an $850.0
million term loan (the &#8220;Term Loan A-2&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The EPE Revolver replaced
the $200.0 million revolver associated with the EPE Interim Credit Facility and
Term Loan A and Term Loan A-2 refinanced amounts then outstanding under the term
loans associated with the EPE Interim Credit Facility.&#160;&#160;Amounts
borrowed under the EPE Revolver and Term Loan A mature in September
2012.&#160;&#160;Amounts borrowed under Term Loan A-2 were refinanced in
November 2007 with proceeds from a term loan (Term Loan B &#8211; described below) due
November 2014.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Borrowings under the EPE August 2007
Credit Agreement are secured by the Parent Company&#8217;s ownership of (i) 20,242,179
common units of Enterprise Products Partners, (ii) 100% of the membership
interests in EPGP and (iii) 38,976,090 common units of Energy Transfer
Equity.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The EPE
Revolver may be used by the Parent Company to fund working capital and other
capital requirements and for general partnership purposes.&#160;&#160;The EPE
Revolver offers secured ABR loans (&#8220;ABR Loans&#8221;) and Eurodollar loans
(&#8220;Eurodollar Loans&#8221;) each having different interest requirements.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ABR Loans
bear interest at an alternative base rate (the &#8220;Alternative Base Rate&#8221;) plus an
applicable rate (the &#8220;Applicable Rate&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Alternative Base Rate is
a rate per annum equal to the greater of:&#160;&#160;(i) the annual interest
rate publicly announced by Citibank, N.A. as its base rate in effect at its
principal office in New York, New York (the &#8220;Prime Rate&#8221;) in effect on such day
and (ii) the federal funds effective rate in effect on such day plus
0.50%.&#160;&#160;The Applicable Rate for ABR Loans will be increased by an
applicable margin ranging from 0% to 1.0% per annum.&#160;&#160;The Eurodollar
Loans bear interest at a &#8220;LIBOR rate&#8221; (as defined in the August 2007 Credit
Agreement) plus the Applicable Rate.&#160;&#160;The Applicable Rate for
Eurodollar Loans will be increased by an applicable margin ranging from 1.00% to
2.50% per annum.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">All
borrowings outstanding under Term Loan A will, at the Parent Company&#8217;s option,
be made and maintained as ABR Loans or Eurodollar Loans, or a combination
thereof.&#160;&#160;Any amount repaid under</font></div><br>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">the Term
Loan A may not be reborrowed.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;&#160;In
November 2007, the Parent Company executed a seven-year, $850 million senior
secured term loan (&#8220;Term Loan B&#8221;) in the institutional leveraged loan
market.&#160;&#160;Proceeds from the Term Loan B were used to permanently
refinance borrowings outstanding under the partnership&#8217;s $850 million Term Loan
A-2.&#160;&#160;The Term Loan B generally bears interest at LIBOR plus 2.25% and
is scheduled to mature in November 2014.&#160;&#160;The Term Loan B is callable
by the partnership at par.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The EPE August 2007 Credit Agreement
contains various covenants related to the Parent Company&#8217;s ability to incur
certain indebtedness, grant certain liens, make fundamental structural changes,
make distributions following an event of default and enter into certain
restricted agreements.&#160;&#160;The credit agreement also requires the Parent
Company to satisfy certain quarterly financial covenants.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">EPO&#8217;s
Debt Obligations</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Multi-Year
Revolving Credit Facility</font>.&#160;&#160;EPO has in place a $1.75 billion
unsecured revolving credit facility, including the issuance of letters of credit
(&#8220;Multi-Year Revolving Credit Facility&#8221;), which matures in November
2012.&#160;&#160;This credit facility has a term-out option that allows for EPO
on the maturity date to convert the principal balance of all revolving loans
then outstanding into a non-revolving one-year term loan. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>The credit facility
allows EPO to request unlimited one-year extensions of the maturity date,
subject to lender approval. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>The total amount of the
bank commitments may be increased, without the consent of the lenders, by an
amount not exceeding $500.0&#160;million by adding one or more lenders to the
facility and/or requesting that the commitments of existing lenders be
increased.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As
defined by the credit agreement, variable interest rates charged under this
facility bear interest at a Eurodollar rate plus an applicable
margin.&#160;&#160;In addition, EPO is required to pay a quarterly facility fee
on each lender&#8217;s commitment irrespective of commitment usage.&#160;&#160;The
applicable margins will be increased by 0.1% per annum for each day that the
total outstanding loans and letter of credit obligations under the facility
exceeds 50% of the total lender commitments.&#160;&#160;Also, if EPO exercises
its term-out option at the maturity date, the applicable margin will increase by
0.125% per annum and, if immediately prior to such election, the total amount of
outstanding loans and letter of credit obligations under the facility exceeds
50% of the total lender commitments, the applicable margin with respect to the
term loan will increase by an additional 0.1% per annum.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Multi-Year Revolving Credit Facility contains certain financial and other
customary affirmative and negative covenants.&#160;&#160;The credit agreement
also restricts EPO&#8217;s ability to pay cash distributions to Enterprise Products
Partners if a default or an event of default (as defined in the credit
agreement) has occurred and is continuing at the time such distribution is
scheduled to be paid.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">EPO&#8217;s
borrowings under this agreement are unsecured general obligations that are
non-recourse to EPGP.&#160;&#160;Enterprise Products Partners has guaranteed
repayment of amounts due under this revolving credit agreement through an
unsecured guarantee.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Pascagoula
MBFC Loan</font>.&#160;&#160;This loan, from the Mississippi Business Finance
Corporation (&#8220;MBFC&#8221;), matured on March 1, 2010 and was repaid.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Petal GO
Zone Bonds</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>In August 2007,
Petal Gas Storage, L.L.C. (&#8220;Petal&#8221;), a wholly owned subsidiary of EPO,
borrowed&#160;$57.5 million from the MBFC pursuant to a loan agreement and
promissory note between Petal and the MBFC.&#160;&#160;The promissory note
between Petal and MBFC is guaranteed by EPO and supported by a letter of credit
issued by a bank that expires in August 2014.&#160;&#160;On the same date, the
MBFC issued $57.5 million in Gulf Opportunity Zone Tax-Exempt (&#8220;GO Zone&#8221;) bonds
to various third parties.&#160;&#160;The&#160;promissory note and the GO Zone
bonds have identical terms including floating interest rates and maturities of
30 years.&#160;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Petal
MBFC Loan</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>In August 2007,
Petal entered into a loan agreement and a promissory note with the MBFC under
which Petal may borrow up to $29.5 million.&#160; On the same date, the MBFC
issued</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">
