      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">taxable
bonds to EPO in the maximum amount of $29.5 million.&#160; At December 31, 2009,
there was $8.9 million outstanding under the loan and the bonds.
&#160;The&#160;promissory note and the taxable bonds have
identical&#160;terms.&#160; The loan and bonds and the related interest expense
and income amounts are netted in preparing our consolidated financial
statements.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Japanese
Yen Term Loan</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>In November
2008, EPO executed the Yen Term Loan in the amount of approximately 20.7 billion
yen (approximately $217.6 million U.S. Dollar equivalent on the closing
date).&#160;&#160;EPO entered into foreign exchange currency swaps that
effectively converted the loan into a U.S. Dollar loan with a fixed interest
rate of approximately 4.93%.&#160;&#160;The Yen Term Loan matured on March 30,
2009.&#160;&#160;Additionally, EPO executed a forward purchase exchange (yen
principal and interest due) at an exchange rate of 94.515 to eliminate foreign
exchange risk, resulting in a payment of US$221.6 million on March 30,
2009.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">364-Day
Revolving Credit Facility</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font><a name="item_1_31_1"><!--EFPlaceholder-->
 </a>From November 2008 through June 2009,
EPO had a $375.0 million standby credit facility.&#160;&#160;The facility was
never utilized and was terminated in June 2009 under its terms as a result of
issuing senior notes.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Senior
Notes</font>.&#160;&#160;EPO&#8217;s senior fixed-rate notes are unsecured obligations
of EPO and rank equally with its existing and future unsecured and
unsubordinated indebtedness.&#160;&#160;They are senior to any future
subordinated indebtedness.&#160;&#160;EPO&#8217;s borrowings under these notes are
non-recourse to EPGP.&#160;&#160;Enterprise Products Partners has guaranteed
repayment of amounts due under these notes through an unsecured and
unsubordinated guarantee.&#160;&#160;Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; guarantee of
such notes is non-recourse to EPGP.&#160;&#160;EPO&#8217;s senior notes are subject to
make-whole redemption rights and were issued under indentures containing certain
covenants, which generally restrict EPO&#8217;s ability, with certain exceptions, to
incur debt secured by liens and engage in sale and leaseback
transactions.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In June
2009, EPO issued $500.0 million in principal amount of 3-year senior unsecured
notes (Senior Notes P) at 99.95% of their principal amount.&#160;&#160;In
October 2009, EPO issued: (i) $500.0 million in principal amount of 10-year
unsecured notes (Senior Notes Q) at 99.355% of their principal amount and (ii)
$600.0 million in principal amount of 30-year unsecured notes (Senior Notes R)
at 99.386% of their principal amount.&#160;&#160;Net proceeds from the issuance
of these senior notes were used (i) to repay amounts borrowed under a $200.0
million term loan that EPO entered into during April 2009, (ii) to repay $500.0
million in aggregate principal amount of Senior Notes F that matured in October
2009, (iii) to temporarily reduce borrowings outstanding under EPO&#8217;s Multi-Year
Revolving Credit Facility and (iv) for general partnership
purposes.</font></div>

Enterprise Products Partners nor EPO can declare or make any distributions to

ranked equally with each other.&#160;&#160;Generally, each series of junior
subordinated notes are not redeemable by EPO without payment of a make-whole
premium while the notes bear interest at a fixed annual rate.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The terms
and provisions of the TEPPCO&#8217;s Junior Subordinated Notes are similar to each
series of EPO&#8217;s junior subordinated notes.&#160;&#160;For example, they: (i) are
general unsecured subordinated obligations, (ii) allow interest payments to be
deferred for multiple periods of up to ten consecutive years and (iii) are
subordinated in right of payment to all existing and future senior
indebtedness.&#160;&#160;The maturity date, the interest rate and the interest
payment due dates are the identical to EPO&#8217;s Junior Subordinated Notes C as
discussed above.</font></div>

connection with the issuance of the TEPPCO Junior Subordinated Notes, TEPPCO and
its Subsidiary Guarantors entered into a Replacement Capital Covenant in favor
of the covered debt holders (as defined in the underlying documents) pursuant to
which TEPPCO agreed for the benefit of such debt holders that it would not
redeem or repurchase such junior notes unless such redemption or repurchase is
made using proceeds from the issuance of certain securities.&#160;&#160;The
Replacement Capital Covenant is not a term of the governing indenture or the

Revolving Credit Facility</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.</font>&#160;&#160;Duncan Energy
Partners has in place a $300 million unsecured revolving credit facility, all of
which may be used for letters of credit, with a $30.0 million sublimit for
Swingline loans.&#160;&#160;This credit facility will be used by Duncan Energy
Partners in the future to fund working capital and other capital requirements
and for general partnership purposes.&#160;&#160;Duncan Energy Partners may make
up to two requests for one-year extensions of the maturity date, which is
February 2011 (subject to certain restrictions).&#160;&#160;The revolving credit
facility is available to pay distributions to its partners, fund working
capital, make acquisitions and provide payment for general
purposes.&#160;&#160;Duncan Energy Partners can increase the revolving credit
facility, without consent of the lenders, by an amount not to exceed
$150.0&#160;million, by adding to the facility one or more new lenders and/or
requesting that the commitments of existing lenders be increased.</font></div>

the following unsecured loans, each having different interest requirements: (i)
a Eurodollar rate, plus the applicable Eurodollar margin (as defined in the
credit agreement), (ii) Base Rate loans bear interest at a rate per annum equal
to the higher of (a) the rate of interest publicly announced by the
administrative agent, Wachovia Bank, National Association, as its Base Rate and
(b) 0.5% per annum above the Federal Funds Rate in effect on such date and (iii)
Swingline loans bear interest at a rate per annum equal to LIBOR plus an
applicable LIBOR margin.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
credit agreements of these unconsolidated affiliates include customary
covenants, including financial covenants.&#160;&#160;These businesses were in
compliance with such financial covenants at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The
credit agreements of these unconsolidated affiliates restrict their ability to
pay cash dividends or distributions if a default or an event of default (as
defined in each credit agreement) has occurred and is continuing at the time
such dividend or distribution is scheduled to be paid.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
following information summarizes the significant terms of the debt obligations
of these unconsolidated affiliates at December 31, 2009:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Poseidon.</font>&#160;&#160;At
December 31, 2009, Poseidon&#8217;s debt obligations consisted of $92.0 million
outstanding under its $150.0 million variable-rate revolving credit
facility.&#160;&#160;Amounts borrowed under this facility mature in May 2011 and
are secured by substantially all of Poseidon&#8217;s assets.&#160;&#160;The
weighted-average variable interest rates charged on this debt at December 31,
2009 and 2008 were 1.88% and 4.31%, respectively.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt"></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Evangeline.</font>&#160;&#160;At
December 31, 2009, Evangeline&#8217;s debt obligations consisted of: (i) $3.2 million
in principal amount of 9.90% fixed-rate Series B senior secured notes due
December 2010 and (ii) a $7.5 million subordinated note payable due in
2011.&#160;&#160;The Series B senior secured notes are collateralized by
Evangeline&#8217;s property, plant and equipment; proceeds from a gas sales contract
and by a debt service reserve requirement.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Evangeline
incurred the subordinated note payable as a result of its acquisition of a
contract-based intangible asset in the early 1990s.&#160;&#160;This note is
subject to a subordination agreement which prevents the</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

of principal and accrued interest on the subordinated note until such time as
the Series B noteholders are either fully cash secured through debt service
accounts or have been completely repaid.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Variable-rate
interest accrues on the subordinated note at LIBOR plus 0.5%.&#160;&#160;The
weighted-average variable interest rates charged on this note at December 31,
2009 and 2008 were 1.59% and 3.62%, respectively.&#160;&#160;Accrued interest
payable related to the subordinated note was $10.2 million and $9.8 million at
December 31, 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Centennial</font>.&#160;&#160;At
December 31, 2009, Centennial&#8217;s debt obligations consisted of $120.0 million
borrowed under a master shelf loan agreement through two private placements,
with interest rates ranging from 7.99% to 8.09%.&#160;&#160;Borrowings under the
master shelf agreement mature in May 2024 and are collateralized by
substantially all of Centennial&#8217;s assets and severally guaranteed by
Centennial&#8217;s owners.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We and
our joint venture partner in Centennial have each guaranteed one-half of
Centennial&#8217;s debt obligations.&#160;&#160;If Centennial were to default on its
debt obligations, the estimated payment obligation would be $60.0 million based
on amounts outstanding at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;We recognized a
liability of $8.4 million for our share of the Centennial debt guaranty at
December 31, 2009.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="n13">Note 13.</a>&#160;&#160;Equity and Distributions</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our Units
represent limited partner interests, which give the holders thereof the right to
participate in cash distributions and to exercise the other rights or privileges
available to them under our First Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited
Partnership (as amended from time to time, the &#8220;Partnership
Agreement&#8221;).</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
accordance with the Partnership Agreement, capital accounts are maintained for
our general partner and limited partners.&#160;&#160;The capital account
provisions of the Partnership Agreement incorporate principles established for
U.S. Federal income tax purposes and are not comparable to GAAP-based equity
amounts presented in our consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;Earnings
and cash distributions are allocated to holders of our Units in accordance with
their respective percentage interests.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Registration
Statement</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt"></font>The Parent Company has a universal
shelf registration statement on file with the SEC that allows it to issue an
unlimited amount of debt and equity securities for general partnership
purposes.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009, the Parent Company had not issued
any securities under its registration statement.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Class
B and C Units</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In May
2007, we issued an aggregate of 14,173,304 Class B Units and 16,000,000 Class C
Units to private company affiliates of EPCO in connection with their
contribution of 4,400,000 common units representing limited partner interest of
TEPPCO and 100% of the general partner interest of TEPPCO GP.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On July
12, 2007, all of the outstanding 14,173,304 Class B Units were converted into
Units on a one-to-one basis.&#160;&#160;On February 1, 2009, all of the
outstanding 16,000,000 Class&#160;C Units were converted to Units on a
one-to-one basis.&#160;&#160;For financial accounting purposes, the Class C
Units were not allocated any portion of net income until their conversion into
Units.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Class C Units were non-participating in
current or undistributed earnings prior to conversion.&#160;&#160;The Units into
which the Class C Units were converted were eligible to receive cash
distributions beginning with the distribution paid in May 2009.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Prior to
February 1, 2009, the Class&#160;C Units (i)&#160;entitled the holder to the
allocation of taxable income, gain, loss, deduction and credit to the same
extent as such tax amounts were allocated to the holder if the Class C Units
were converted and outstanding Units and (ii)&#160; were non-voting, except
that, the Class&#160;C Units were entitled to vote as a separate class on any
matter that adversely affected the rights or</font></div><br>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Accumulated
Other Comprehensive Loss</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">AOCI
primarily includes the effective portion of the gain or loss on derivative
instruments designated and qualified as a cash flow hedge, foreign currency
adjustments and minimum pension liability adjustments.&#160;&#160;Amounts
accumulated in OCI from cash flow hedges are reclassified into earnings in the
same period(s) in which the hedged forecasted transactions (such as a forecasted
forward sale of NGLs) affect earnings.&#160;&#160;If it becomes probable that
the forecasted transaction will not occur, the net gain or loss in AOCI must be
immediately reclassified.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Noncontrolling
Interest</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Prior to
the completion of the TEPPCO Merger, effective October 26, 2009, we accounted
for the former owners&#8217; interest in TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP as noncontrolling
interest.&#160;&#160;Under this method of presentation, all pre-merger revenues
and expenses of TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP are included in net income, and the former
owners&#8217; share of the income of TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP is allocated to net income
attributable to noncontrolling interest.&#160;&#160;In addition, the former
owners&#8217; share of the net assets of TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP are presented as
noncontrolling interest, a component of equity, on our Consolidated Balance
Sheets.</font></div><br></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB2" style="LETTER-SPACING: 9pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
Contributions received from limited partners of Enterprise Products Partners,
Duncan Energy Partners and TEPPCO primarily represent net cash proceeds each
entity received from common unit offerings and distribution reinvestment plans,
excluding those received from the Parent Company.&#160;&#160;During 2009,
Enterprise Products Partners issued an aggregate of 36,950,014 of its common
units, which generated net cash proceeds of approximately $911.0
million.&#160;&#160;Additionally, during 2009 Duncan Energy Partners issued an
aggregate 8,943,400 of its common units, which generated net cash proceeds of
approximately $137.4 million.&#160;&#160;During 2007, Duncan Energy Partners
received approximately $291.0 million of net cash proceeds in connection with
its initial public offering.&#160;&#160;During 2008, TEPPCO sold 9,200,000 of
its units in an underwritten equity offering, which generated net cash proceeds
of $257.0 million.</font></font></div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="n14">Note 14.</a>&#160;&#160;Business Segments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have
six reportable business segments: NGL Pipelines &amp; Services, Onshore Natural
Gas Pipelines &amp; Services, Onshore Crude Oil Pipelines &amp; Services,
Offshore Pipelines &amp; Services, Petrochemical &amp; Refined Products Services
and Other Investments.&#160;&#160;Our business segments are generally organized
and managed according to the type of services rendered (or technologies
employed) and products produced and/or sold.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
evaluate segment performance based on the non-GAAP financial measure of gross
operating margin.&#160;&#160;Gross operating margin (either in total or by
individual segment) is an important performance measure of the core
profitability of our operations.&#160;&#160;This measure forms the basis of our
internal financial reporting and is used by our management in deciding how to
allocate capital resources among business segments.&#160;&#160;We believe that
investors benefit from having access to the same financial measures that our
management uses in evaluating segment results.&#160;&#160;The GAAP financial
measure most directly comparable to total segment gross operating margin is
operating income.&#160;&#160;Our non-GAAP financial measure of total segment
gross operating margin should not be considered an alternative to GAAP operating
income.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We define
total segment gross operating margin as operating income before: (i)
depreciation, amortization and accretion expense; (ii) non-cash consolidated
asset impairment charges; (iii) operating lease expenses for which we do not
have the payment obligation; (iv) gains and losses from asset sales and related
transactions; and (v) general and administrative costs.&#160;&#160;Gross
operating margin by segment is calculated by subtracting segment operating costs
and expenses (net of the adjustments noted above) from segment revenues, with
both segment totals before the elimination of intercompany
transactions.&#160;&#160;In accordance with GAAP, intercompany accounts and
transactions are eliminated in consolidation.&#160;&#160;Gross operating margin
is exclusive of other income and expense transactions, provision for income
taxes, the cumulative effect of changes in accounting principles and
extraordinary charges.&#160;&#160;Gross operating margin is presented on a 100%
basis before the allocation of earnings to noncontrolling
interests.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Segment
revenues include intersegment and intrasegment transactions, which are generally
based on transactions made at market-based rates.&#160;&#160;Our consolidated
revenues reflect the elimination of intercompany (both intersegment and
intrasegment) transactions.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
include equity in income of unconsolidated affiliates in our measurement of
segment gross operating margin and operating income.&#160;&#160;Our equity
investments with industry partners are a vital component of our business
strategy.&#160;&#160;They are a means by which we conduct our operations to
align our interests with those of our customers and/or
suppliers.&#160;&#160;This method of operation enables us to achieve favorable
economies of scale relative to the level of investment and business risk assumed
versus what we could accomplish on a standalone basis.&#160;&#160;Many of these
businesses perform supporting or complementary roles to our other business
operations.</font></div><br>
      <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
        <div id="FTR">
          <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center">

          <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
            <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">

        <div id="HDR">
          <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
integrated midstream energy asset system (including the midstream energy assets
of our equity method investees) provides services to producers and consumers of
natural gas, NGLs, crude oil, refined products and certain
petrochemicals.&#160;&#160;In general, hydrocarbons enter our asset system in a
number of ways, such as an offshore natural gas or crude oil pipeline, an
offshore platform, a natural gas processing plant, an onshore natural gas
gathering pipeline, an NGL fractionator, an NGL storage facility or an NGL
transportation or distribution pipeline.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Many of
our equity investees are included within our integrated midstream asset
system.&#160;&#160;For example, we have ownership interests in several offshore
natural gas, refined products and crude oil pipelines.&#160;&#160;Other examples
include our use of the Promix NGL fractionator to process mixed NGLs extracted
by our gas plants.&#160;&#160;The fractionated NGLs we receive from Promix can
then be sold in our NGL marketing activities.&#160;&#160;Additionally, our use
of the Centennial pipeline, which loops the refined products pipeline system
between Beaumont, Texas and southern Illinois, permits effective supply of
product to points south of Illinois as well as incremental product supply
capacity to mid-continent markets downstream of southern
Illinois.&#160;&#160;Given the integral nature of our equity method investees to
our operations, we believe the presentation of earnings from such investees as a
component of gross operating margin and operating income is meaningful and
appropriate.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Substantially
all of our consolidated revenues are earned in the United States and derived
from a wide customer base.&#160;&#160;The majority of our plant-based operations
are located in Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico, Colorado and
Wyoming.&#160;&#160;Our natural gas, NGL, refined products and crude oil
pipelines are located in a number of regions of the United States including (i)
the Gulf of Mexico offshore Texas, Louisiana, and onshore in Colorado; (ii) the
south and southeastern United States (primarily in Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi
and Alabama); (iii) the Midwestern and northeastern United States; and (iv)
certain regions of the central and western United States, including the Rocky
Mountains.&#160;&#160;Our marketing activities are headquartered in Houston,
Texas and Oklahoma City, Oklahoma and serve customers in a number of regions of
the United States including the Gulf Coast, West Coast and Mid-Continent
areas.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Segment
assets consist of property, plant and equipment, investments in unconsolidated
affiliates, intangible assets and goodwill.&#160;&#160;The carrying values of
such amounts are assigned to each segment based on each asset&#8217;s or investment&#8217;s
principal operations and contribution to the gross operating margin of that
particular segment.&#160;&#160;Since construction-in-progress amounts (which are
a component of property, plant and equipment) generally do not contribute to
segment gross operating margin, such amounts are excluded from segment asset
totals until they are placed in service.&#160;&#160;Consolidated intangible
assets and goodwill are assigned to each segment based on the classification of
the assets to which they relate.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We consolidate the financial statements
of Enterprise Products Partners with those of our own.&#160;&#160;As a result,
our consolidated gross operating margin amounts include 100% of the gross
operating margin amounts of Enterprise Products Partners.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Substantially all of the ownership
interests in Enterprise Products Partners that are owned or controlled by the
Parent Company are pledged as security under its credit facility.&#160;&#160;In
addition, substantially all of the ownership interests in the Parent Company and
Enterprise Products Partners that are owned or controlled by EPCO and its
affiliates, other than those interests owned by the Parent Company, Dan Duncan
LLC and certain trusts affiliated with Dan L. Duncan, are pledged as security
under the credit facility of a privately held affiliate of EPCO.&#160;&#160;This
credit facility contains customary and other events of default relating to EPCO
and certain affiliates, including the Parent Company and Enterprise Products
Partners.</font></div>

of NGLs and other products.&#160;&#160;We also lease office space in various

agreements approximate market rates.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">EPCO
ASA</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have
no employees.&#160;&#160;All of our operating functions and general and
administrative support services are provided by employees of EPCO pursuant to
the ASA or by other service providers.&#160;&#160;The Parent Company, Enterprise
Products Partners, Duncan Energy Partners and their respective general partners
are parties to the ASA.&#160;&#160;The significant terms of the ASA are as
follows:</font></div>

employees.&#160;&#160;In general, our reimbursement to EPCO for administrative

our behalf (e.g., the purchase of office supplies) or (ii) based on an

estimated use of such services by each party (e.g., the allocation of general
legal or accounting salaries based on estimates of time spent on each entity&#8217;s

expenses are representative of what the amounts would have been on a standalone
basis.&#160;&#160;With respect to allocated costs, we believe that the
proportional direct allocation method employed by EPCO is reasonable and
reflective of the estimated level of costs we would have incurred on a
standalone basis.</font></div>

also addresses potential conflicts that may arise among the Parent Company
(including EPE Holdings), Enterprise Products Partners (including EPGP), Duncan
Energy Partners (including DEP GP), and the EPCO Group with respect to business
opportunities (as defined within the ASA) with third parties.&#160;&#160;The
EPCO Group includes EPCO and its other affiliates, but excludes the Parent
Company, Enterprise Products Partners, Duncan Energy Partners and their
respective general partners.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Duncan
Energy Partners was formed in September 2006 and did not acquire any assets
prior to February 5, 2007, which was the date it completed its initial public
offering and acquired controlling interests in five midstream energy businesses
from EPO in a drop down transaction.&#160;&#160;On December 8, 2008, through a
second drop down transaction, Duncan Energy Partners acquired controlling
interests in three additional midstream energy businesses from
EPO.&#160;&#160;The business purpose of Duncan Energy Partners is to acquire,
own and operate a diversified portfolio of midstream energy assets and to
support the growth objectives of EPO and other affiliates under common
control.&#160;&#160;Duncan Energy Partners is engaged in (i) the gathering,
transportation and storage of natural gas; (ii) NGL transportation and
fractionation; (iii) the storage of NGL and petrochemical products; (iv) the
transportation of petrochemical products and (v) the marketing of NGLs and
natural gas.</font></div>

December 31, 2009, Duncan Energy Partners is owned 99.3% by its limited partners
and 0.7% by its general partner, DEP GP, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of
EPO.&#160;&#160;DEP GP is responsible for managing the business and operations
of Duncan Energy Partners.&#160;&#160;DEP Operating Partnership L.P., a wholly
owned subsidiary of Duncan Energy Partners, conducts substantially all of Duncan
Energy Partners&#8217; business.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009, EPO owned 58.6% of
Duncan Energy Partners&#8217; limited partner interests and 100% of its general
partner.&#160;&#160;Due to Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; control of Duncan
Energy Partners, its financial statements are consolidated with those of
Enterprise Products Partners and Enterprise Products Partners&#8217; transactions with
Duncan Energy Partners are eliminated in consolidation.</font></div>

        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
connection with our marine services acquisition in February 2008, Cenac and
affiliates became a related party of ours.&#160;&#160;We entered into a
transitional operating agreement with Cenac in which our fleet of tow boats and
tank barges (which were primarily acquired from Cenac) continued to be operated
by employees of Cenac for a period of up to two years following the
acquisition.&#160;&#160;Under this agreement, we paid Cenac a monthly operating
fee and reimbursed Cenac for personnel salaries and related employee benefit
expenses, certain repairs and maintenance expenses and insurance premiums on the
equipment.&#160;&#160;Effective August 1, 2009, the transitional operating
agreement was terminated.&#160;&#160;Personnel providing services pursuant to
the agreement became employees of EPCO and will continue to provide services
under the ASA.&#160;&#160;Concurrently with the termination of the transitional
operating agreement, we entered into a two-year consulting agreement with Mr.
Cenac and Cenac Marine Services, L.L.C. under which Mr. Cenac has agreed to
supervise the day-to-day operations of our marine services business and, at our
request, provide related management and transitional services.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On May
18, 2006, the State of Texas enacted House Bill 3 which revised the pre-existing
state franchise tax.&#160;&#160;In general, legal entities that conduct business
in Texas are subject to the Revised Texas Franchise Tax (i.e., the Texas Margin
Tax), including previously non-taxable entities such as limited liability
companies, limited partnerships and limited liability
partnerships.&#160;&#160;The tax is assessed on Texas sourced taxable margin
which is defined as the lesser of (i) 70% of total revenue or (ii) total revenue
less (a) cost of goods sold or (b) compensation and benefits.</font></div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Although
the bill states that the Texas Margin Tax is not an income tax, it has the
characteristics of an income tax since it is determined by applying a tax rate
to a base that considers both revenues and expenses.&#160;&#160;Due to the
enactment of the Texas Margin Tax, we recorded a net deferred tax asset of $0.3
million and a liability of $1.0 million during the years ended December 31, 2009
and 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;The offsetting net benefit of $0.3 million
and net charge of $1.0 million is shown on our Statements of Consolidated
Operations for the years ended December 31, 2009 and 2008, respectively, as a
component of &#8220;Provision for income taxes.&#8221;</font></div><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="n17">Note 17.&#160;</a>&#160;Earnings Per Unit</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Basic and
diluted earnings per unit is computed by dividing net income or loss allocated
to limited partners by the weighted-average number of Units outstanding during a
period, including Class B Units (see below).&#160;&#160;The amount of net income
allocated to limited partners is derived by subtracting, from net income or
loss, our general partner&#8217;s share of such net income or loss.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As
consideration for the contribution of 4,400,000 common units of TEPPCO and the
100% membership interest in TEPPCO GP (including associated TEPPCO IDRs) in May
2007, the Parent Company issued 14,173,304 Class B Units and 16,000,000 Class C
Units to private company affiliates of EPCO that are under common control with
the Parent Company.&#160;&#160;As a result of this common
control</font></div><br>

securities for purposes of calculating our basic and diluted earnings per
Unit.&#160;&#160;On July 12, 2007, all of the outstanding 14,173,304 Class B
Units were converted to Units on a one-to-one basis.&#160;&#160;On February 1,
2009, all of the outstanding 16,000,000 Class&#160;C Units were converted to
Units on a one-to-one basis.&#160;&#160;The Class C Units were non-participating
in current or undistributed earnings prior to conversion.&#160;&#160;The Units
into which the Class C Units were converted were eligible to receive cash
distributions beginning with the distribution paid in May 2009.&#160;&#160;See
Note 13 for additional information regarding the Class B and C
Units.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Litigation</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
occasion, we or our unconsolidated affiliates are named as defendants in
litigation and legal proceedings relating to our normal business activities,
including regulatory and environmental matters.&#160;&#160;Although we are
insured against various risks to the extent we believe it is prudent, there is
no assurance that the nature and amount of such insurance will be adequate, in
every case, to indemnify us against liabilities arising from future legal
proceedings.&#160;&#160;We are not aware of any litigation, pending or
threatened, that we believe is reasonably likely to have a significant adverse
effect on our financial position, results of operations or cash
flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
evaluate our ongoing litigation based upon a combination of litigation and
settlement alternatives.&#160;&#160;These reviews are updated as the facts and
combinations of the cases develop or change.&#160;&#160;Assessing and predicting
the outcome of these matters involves substantial uncertainties.&#160;&#160;In
the event that the assumptions we used to evaluate these matters change in
future periods or new information becomes</font></div><br>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Parent
Company Matters</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>In February
2008, Joel A. Gerber, a purported unitholder of the Parent Company, filed
a&#160;derivative complaint&#160;on behalf of the Parent Company in the Court of
Chancery of the State of Delaware.&#160;&#160;The complaint names as defendants
EPE Holdings, the Board of Directors of EPE Holdings, EPCO,&#160;and Dan L.
Duncan and certain of his affiliates.&#160;&#160;The Parent Company is named as
a nominal defendant.&#160;The complaint alleges that the defendants, in breach
of their fiduciary duties to the Parent Company and its unitholders, caused the
Parent Company to purchase in May 2007 the TEPPCO GP membership interests and
TEPPCO units from Mr. Duncan&#8217;s affiliates at an unfair price.&#160;&#160;The
complaint also alleges that Charles E. McMahen, Edwin E. Smith and Thurmon
Andress, constituting the three members of EPE Holdings&#8217; ACG Committee, cannot
be considered independent because of their relationships with
Mr.&#160;Duncan.&#160; The complaint seeks relief (i)&#160;awarding damages for
profits allegedly obtained by the defendants as a result of the alleged
wrongdoings in the complaint and (ii)&#160;awarding plaintiff costs of the
action, including fees and expenses of his attorneys and
experts.&#160;&#160;Management believes this lawsuit is without merit and
intends to vigorously defend against it.&#160;&#160;See Note 15 for information
regarding our relationship with Mr. Duncan and his affiliates.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Enterprise
Products Partners&#8217; Matters</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>On September 18,
2006, Peter Brinckerhoff, a purported unitholder of TEPPCO, filed a complaint in
the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (the &#8220;Delaware Court&#8221;), in his
individual capacity, as a putative class action on behalf of other unitholders
of TEPPCO and derivatively on behalf of TEPPCO, concerning, among other things,
certain transactions involving TEPPCO and Enterprise Product Partners or their
affiliates.&#160;&#160;Mr. Brinckerhoff filed an amended complaint on July 12,
2007.&#160;&#160;The amended complaint names as defendants (i) TEPPCO, certain
of its current and former directors, and certain of its affiliates, (ii)
Enterprise Products Partners and certain of its affiliates, (iii) EPCO and (iv)
Dan L. Duncan.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The amended complaint alleges, among
other things, that the defendants caused TEPPCO to enter into specified
transactions that were unfair to TEPPCO or otherwise unfairly favored Enterprise
Products Partners or its affiliates over TEPPCO.&#160;&#160;These transactions
are alleged to include: (i) the joint venture to further expand the Jonah system
entered into by TEPPCO and Enterprise Products Partners in August 2006 (the
plaintiff alleges that TEPPCO did not receive fair value for allowing Enterprise
Products Partners to participate in the joint venture); (ii) the sale by TEPPCO
of its Pioneer natural gas processing plant and certain gas processing rights to
Enterprise Products Partners in March 2006 (the plaintiff alleges that the
purchase price paid by Enterprise Products Partners did not provide fair value
to TEPPCO) and (iii) certain amendments to TEPPCO&#8217;s partnership agreement,
including a reduction in the maximum tier of TEPPCO&#8217;s incentive distribution
rights in exchange for TEPPCO units.&#160;&#160;The amended complaint seeks (i)
rescission of the amendments to TEPPCO&#8217;s partnership agreement, (ii) damages for
profits and special benefits allegedly obtained by defendants as a result of the
alleged wrongdoings in the amended complaint and (iii) an award to plaintiff of
the costs of the action, including fees and expenses of his attorneys and
experts.&#160;&#160;By its Opinion and Order dated November 25, 2008, the
Delaware Court dismissed Mr. Brinckerhoff&#8217;s individual and putative class action
claims with respect to the amendments to TEPPCO&#8217;s partnership
agreement.&#160;&#160;We refer to this action and the remaining claims in this
action as the &#8220;Derivative Action.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>On April 29, 2009, Peter Brinckerhoff
and Renee Horowitz, as Attorney in Fact for Rae Kenrow, purported unitholders of
TEPPCO, filed separate complaints in the Delaware Court as putative class
actions on behalf of other unitholders of TEPPCO, concerning the TEPPCO
Merger.&#160;&#160;On May 11, 2009, these actions were consolidated under the

4548-VCL (&#8220;Merger Action&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The complaints name as defendants
Enterprise Products Partners, EPGP, TEPPCO GP, the directors of TEPPCO GP, EPCO
and Dan L. Duncan.</font></div>

and that the TEPPCO Merger is an attempt to extinguish the Derivative Action
without consideration.&#160;&#160;The complaints further allege that the process
through which the Special Committee of the</font></div><br>

Delaware Court approved the Settlement Agreement on January 15, 2010, dismissing
with prejudice the Merger Action and the Derivative Action.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Additionally,
on June 29 and 30, 2009, respectively, M. Lee Arnold and Sharon Olesky,
purported unitholders of TEPPCO, filed separate complaints in the District
Courts of Harris County, Texas, as putative class actions on behalf of other
unitholders of TEPPCO, concerning the TEPPCO Merger (the &#8220;Texas
Actions&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The complaints name as defendants Enterprise Products
Partners, TEPPCO, TEPPCO GP, EPGP, EPCO, Dan L. Duncan, Jerry Thompson, and the
board of directors of TEPPCO GP.&#160;&#160;The allegations in the complaints
are similar to the complaints filed in Delaware on April 29, 2009 and seek
similar relief.&#160;&#160;The named plaintiffs in the two Texas Actions (the
&#8220;Texas Plaintiffs/Objectors&#8221;) also appeared in the Delaware proceedings as
objectors to the settlement of those cases which were then awaiting court
approval.&#160;&#160;On October 7, 2009, the Texas Plaintiffs/Objectors and the
parties to the Settlement Agreement entered into a Stipulation to Withdraw
Objection (the &#8220;Stipulation&#8221;).&#160;&#160;In accordance with the Stipulation,
and upon the receipt of Final Court Approval (as defined in the Settlement
Agreement), the Texas Plaintiffs/Objectors agreed to dismiss the Texas Actions
with prejudice. As of March 1, 2010, the Texas Actions have been dismissed with
prejudice pursuant to the Settlement Agreement.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
February 2007, EPO received a letter from the Environment and Natural Resources
Division of the U.S. Department of Justice related to an ammonia release in
Kingman County, Kansas on October 27, 2004 from a pressurized anhydrous ammonia
pipeline owned by a third-party, Magellan Ammonia Pipeline, L.P. (&#8220;Magellan&#8221;),
and a previous release of ammonia on September 27, 2004 from the same
pipeline.&#160;&#160;EPO was the operator of this pipeline until July 1,
2008.&#160;&#160;This matter was settled in September 2009, and Magellan has
agreed to pay all assessed penalties.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Attorney General of Colorado on
behalf of the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (&#8220;CDPHE&#8221;)
filed suit against Enterprise Products Partners and others on April 15, 2008 in
connection with the construction of a pipeline near Parachute, Colorado.&#160;
The State sought a temporary restraining order and an injunction to halt
construction activities since it alleged that the defendants failed to install
measures to minimize damage to the environment and to follow requirements for
the pipeline&#8217;s storm water permit and appropriate storm water plan.&#160;
Enterprise Products Partners has entered into a settlement agreement with the
State that dismisses the suit and assesses a fine of approximately $0.2
million.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
CDPHE, through its Air Pollution Control Division, has proposed a Compliance
Order on Consent with Enterprise Gas Processing, L.L.C for alleged violations of
the Colorado Air Pollution and Prevention and Control Act (&#8220;Colorado Act&#8221;) with
respect to operations of the Meeker Gas Processing Plant.&#160;&#160;The
Compliance Order proposes an administrative fine of approximately $0.3 million
and would require the Meeker Gas Processing Plant to be operated in compliance
with the Colorado Act.&#160;&#160;We have entered into discussions regarding the
terms of the Compliance Order.</font></div><br>

            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ENTERPRISE
GP HOLDINGS L.P.</font></div>
            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTES
TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>
            <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
January 2009, the State of New Mexico filed suit in District Court in Santa Fe
County, New Mexico, under the New Mexico Air Quality Control Act.&#160; The
lawsuit arose out of a February 27, 2008 Notice Of Violation issued to Marathon
Oil Corp. (&#8220;Marathon&#8221;) as operator of the Indian Basin natural gas processing
facility located in Eddy County, New Mexico.&#160;&#160;We own a 42.4% undivided
interest in the assets comprising the Indian Basin facility.&#160;&#160;The
State alleges violations of its air laws.&#160;&#160;Marathon agreed to a
Consent Decree with the State which was approved by the District Court on
December 21, 2009.&#160; Under the Decree, Marathon paid the State approximately
$0.6 million, agreed to $4.5 million of additional environmental projects in New
Mexico and agreed to two projects for &#8220;corrective measures&#8221; at the
facility.&#160;&#160;&#160;We are in discussions with Marathon regarding the
responsibility for these payments.&#160;&#160;We believe that any potential
payment we make will not have a material impact on our consolidated financial
position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
connection with our dissociation from TOPS (see Note 8), Oiltanking filed an
original petition against Enterprise Offshore Port System, LLC, EPO, TEPPCO O/S
Port System, LLC, TEPPCO and TEPPCO GP in the District Court of Harris County,
Texas, 61st Judicial District (Cause No. 2009-31367), asserting, among other
things, that the dissociation was wrongful and in breach of the TOPS partnership
agreement, citing provisions of the agreement that, if applicable, would
continue to obligate us and TEPPCO to make capital contributions to fund the
project and impose liabilities on us and TEPPCO.&#160;&#160;On September 17,
2009, Enterprise Products Partners and TEPPCO entered into a settlement
agreement with certain affiliates of Oiltanking and TOPS that resolved all
disputes between the parties related to the business and affairs of the TOPS
project (including the litigation described above).&#160;&#160;We recognized
approximately $66.9 million of expense during 2009 in connection with this
settlement.&#160;&#160;This charge is classified within our Offshore Pipelines
&amp; Services business segment.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Energy
Transfer Equity Matters</font>.&#160;&#160;In July 2007, ETP announced that it
was under investigation by the FERC with respect to (i) whether ETP engaged in
manipulation or improper trading activities in the Houston Ship Channel market
around the time of the hurricanes in the fall of 2005 and other prior periods in
order to benefit financially from commodity derivative instrument positions and
from certain index-priced physical gas purchases in the Houston Ship Channel
market and (ii) whether ETP manipulated daily prices at the Waha and Permian
hubs in west Texas on two dates.&#160;&#160;Certain third-party lawsuits were
also filed in connection with these matters.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In September 2009, ETP announced that
the FERC approved a settlement agreement related to these
allegations.&#160;&#160;The settlement agreement provides that ETP make a $5.0
million payment to the federal government and the FERC will dismiss all claims
against ETP.&#160;&#160;Separate from the payment to the federal government, ETP
also is required to establish a $25.0 million fund for the purpose of settling
related third-party claims against ETP.&#160;&#160;This fund amount will be paid
into a specific account held by a financial institution selected by mutual
agreement of ETP and the FERC.&#160;&#160;An administrative law judge appointed
by the FERC will determine the validity of any third-party claim against this
fund.&#160;&#160;Any party who receives money from this fund will be required to
waive all claims against ETP related to this matter.&#160;&#160;Management of
ETP believes that the application of this fund will resolve the existing
litigation related to this matter, although, in the event that all plaintiffs in
the existing litigation do not participate in this fund, these non-participating
plaintiffs will be entitled to continue their litigation claims through the
judiciary system.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Pursuant
to the settlement agreement, the FERC made no findings of fact or conclusions of
law.&#160;&#160;In addition, the settlement agreement specifies that ETP does
not admit or concede to the FERC or any third-party any actual or potential
fault, wrongdoing or liability in connection with its alleged conduct related to
the FERC claims.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
FERC&#8217;s actions against ETP also included allegations related to its Oasis
pipeline, which is an intrastate pipeline that transports natural gas between
the Waha and Katy hubs in Texas.&#160;&#160;The allegations related to the Oasis
pipeline included claims that the pipeline violated Natural Gas Policy Act
regulations from January 2004 through June 2006 by granting undue preference to
ETP&#8217;s affiliates.&#160;&#160;In March 2009, ETP entered into a separate
settlement agreement with the FERC related to these allegations.&#160;&#160;The
Oasis settlement agreement did not require ETP to make any payments to the
federal government or any other parties.</font></div><br>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Regulatory
Matters</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Certain<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>recent
scientific studies have suggested that emissions of certain gases, commonly
referred to as &#8220;greenhouse gases&#8221; and including carbon dioxide and methane, may
be contributing to climate change.&#160;&#160;On June 26, 2009, the U.S. House
of Representatives passed the &#8220;American Clean Energy and Security Act of 2009,&#8221;
or &#8220;ACESA,&#8221; which would establish an economy-wide cap-and-trade program intended
to reduce the emissions of greenhouse gases in the United States and would
require most sources of greenhouse gas emissions to obtain greenhouse gas
emission &#8220;allowances&#8221; corresponding to their annual emissions of greenhouse
gases.&#160;&#160;The U.S. Senate has also begun work on its own legislation for
controlling and reducing emissions of greenhouse gases in the United
States.&#160;&#160;In addition, on December 7, 2009, the U.S. Environmental
Protection Agency (&#8220;EPA&#8221;) announced its finding that emissions of greenhouse
gases presented an endangerment to human health and the
environment.&#160;&#160;These findings by the EPA allow the agency to proceed
with the adoption and implementation of regulations that would restrict
emissions of greenhouse gases under existing provisions of the federal Clean Air
Act.&#160;&#160;Although it may take the EPA several years to adopt and impose
regulations limiting emissions of greenhouse gases, any such regulation could
require us to incur costs to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases associated
with our operations.&#160;&#160;Any laws or regulations that may be adopted to
restrict or reduce emissions of greenhouse gases would likely require us to
incur increased operating costs, and may have an adverse effect on our business,
financial position, demand for our operations, results of operations and cash
flows.</font></div>

            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ENTERPRISE

            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTES
TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

      </div><br>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
significant lease agreements involve (i) the lease of underground caverns for
the storage of natural gas and NGLs, (ii) leased office space with affiliates of
EPCO and (iii) land held pursuant to right-of-way agreements.&#160;&#160;In
general, our material lease agreements have current terms that range from 14 to
20 years.&#160;&#160;The agreements for leased office space with affiliates of
EPCO and underground NGL storage caverns we lease from a third party include
renewal options that could extend these contracts for up to an additional 20
years.&#160;&#160;The remainder of our material lease agreements do not provide
for additional renewal terms.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Lease expense is charged to operating
costs and expenses on a straight line basis over the period of expected economic
benefit.&#160;&#160;Contingent rental payments are expensed as
incurred.&#160;&#160;We are generally required to perform routine maintenance on
the underlying leased assets.&#160;&#160;In addition, certain leases give us the
option to make leasehold improvements.&#160;&#160;Maintenance and repairs of
leased assets resulting from our operations are charged to expense as
incurred.&#160;&#160;We did not make any significant leasehold improvements
during the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 or 2007.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
operating lease commitments shown in the preceding table exclude the non-cash,
related party expense associated with retained leases contributed to us by EPCO
in 1998.&#160;&#160;EPCO remains liable for the actual cash lease payments
associated with these agreements, which it accounts for as operating
leases.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009, the retained leases were for
approximately 100 railcars.&#160;&#160;EPCO&#8217;s minimum future rental payments
under these leases are $0.7 million for each of the years 2010 through 2015 and
$0.3 million for 2016.&#160;&#160;We record the full value of these payments
made by EPCO on our behalf as a non-cash related party operating lease expense,
with the offset to equity accounted for as a general contribution to our
partnership.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
retained lease agreements contain lessee purchase options, which are at prices
that approximate fair value of the underlying leased assets.&#160;&#160;EPCO has
assigned these purchase options to us.&#160;&#160;&#160;We exercised our
election under the retained leases to purchase a cogeneration unit in December
2008 for $2.3 million.&#160;&#160;Should we decide to exercise the purchase
option associated with the remaining agreement, we would pay the original lessor
$3.1 million in June 2016.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Lease and
rental expense included in costs and expenses was $60.7 million, $56.8 million
and $61.4 million during the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007,
respectively.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Purchase
Obligations</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.
</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>We
define a purchase obligation as an agreement to purchase goods or services that
is enforceable and legally binding (unconditional) on us that specifies all
significant terms, including: fixed or minimum quantities to be purchased;
fixed, minimum or variable price provisions; and the approximate timing of the
transactions.&#160;&#160;We have classified our unconditional purchase
obligations into the following categories:</font></div>

also market natural gas, NGLs, crude oil and other hydrocarbon
products.&#160;&#160;As such, our financial position, results of operations and
cash flows may be affected by changes in the commodity prices of these
hydrocarbon products, including changes in the relative price levels among these
products (e.g., natural gas processing margins are influenced by the ratio of
natural gas prices to crude oil prices).&#160;&#160;The prices of hydrocarbon
products are subject to fluctuation in response to changes in supply, market
uncertainty and a variety of additional factors that are beyond our
control.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
profitability could be impacted by a decline in the volume of hydrocarbon
products gathered, transported, processed, fractionated or stored at our
facilities.&#160;&#160;A material decrease in natural gas or crude oil
production or crude oil refining, for reasons such as depressed commodity prices
or a decrease in exploration and development activities, could result in a
decline in the volume of natural gas, NGLs, refined products and crude oil
handled by our facilities.</font></div>

crude oil, NGL and other hydrocarbon products by the petrochemical, refining or
heating industries, whether because of: (i) general economic conditions, (ii)
reduced demand by consumers for the end products made using such products, (iii)
increased competition from other products due to pricing differences, (iv)
adverse weather conditions, (v) government regulations affecting energy
commodity prices, production levels of hydrocarbons or the content of motor
gasoline or (vi) other reasons, could adversely affect our financial position,
results of operations and cash flows.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Credit
Risk Due to Industry Concentrations</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A
substantial portion of our revenues are derived from companies in the domestic
natural gas, NGL and petrochemical industries.&#160;&#160;This concentration
could affect our overall exposure to credit risk since these customers may be
affected by similar economic or other conditions.&#160;&#160;We generally do not
require collateral for our accounts receivable; however, we do attempt to
negotiate offset, prepayment, or automatic debit agreements with customers that
are deemed to be credit risks in order to minimize our potential exposure to any
defaults.&#160;&#160;See Note 14 for information regarding our largest
customers.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Counterparty
Risk with Respect to Derivative Instruments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In those
situations where we are exposed to credit risk in our derivative instrument
transactions, we analyze the counterparty&#8217;s financial condition prior to
entering into an agreement, establish credit and/or margin limits and monitor
the appropriateness of these limits on an ongoing basis.&#160;&#160;Generally,
we do not require collateral nor do we anticipate nonperformance by our
counterparties.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Insurance-Related
Risks</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
participate as a named insured in EPCO&#8217;s insurance program, which provides us
with property damage, business interruption and other coverages, the scope and
amounts of which are customary and sufficient for the nature and extent of our
operations.&#160;&#160;While we believe EPCO maintains adequate insurance
coverage on our behalf, insurance will not cover every type of damage or
interruption that might occur.&#160;&#160;If we were to incur a significant
liability for which we were not fully insured, it could have a material impact
on our consolidated financial position, results of operations and cash
flows.&#160;&#160;In addition, the proceeds of any such insurance may not be
paid in a timely manner and may be insufficient to reimburse us for our repair
costs or lost income.&#160;&#160;Any event that interrupts the revenues
generated by our consolidated operations, or which causes us to make significant
expenditures not covered by insurance, could reduce our ability to pay
distributions to our partners and, accordingly, adversely affect the market
price of our common units.</font></div>

            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTES
